summary: Boxer and Pilloni build Hida theory for the coherent cohomology of Siegel Shimura varieties for GSp_{2g} in every cohomological degree, higher Hida theory. The theories are indexed by the Kostant set ^M W of minimal-length representatives of W_M\W: for each w, RΓ_w(K^p, cusp/∅) is the ordinary part of the cohomology, with support conditions attached to w, of toroidal compactifications of the ordinary Igusa formal schemes. Theorem 1.4.3: these complexes are admissible; for g ≤ 2 they have integral amplitude [0, ℓ(w)] (cuspidal) and [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2] (non-cuspidal), and rationally for all g; in regular weight they compute the ordinary part of classical coherent cohomology, and in any weight a Cousin spectral sequence computes it from the RΓ_w with w ∈ C(κ). Over Λ = Z_p⟦T(Z_p)⟧ the perfect complexes M^•_w interpolate these ordinary parts over the whole weight space (Proposition 1.4.7) and satisfy Serre duality (Theorem 1.4.8). The slope-0 part of the higher Coleman theory of [BP21] is the rational part of higher Hida theory (Theorems 6.2.9, 6.2.15); this proves the slope bounds conjectured in [BP21] in the Siegel case (Theorem 1.4.10), and gives the vanishing of the ordinary part of H^i(Γ, Q_p) for i < g(g+1)/2 for principal congruence subgroups of Sp_{2g}(Z) of level divisible by p (Theorem 1.5.1). The method rests on an abstract formalism of cohomology with partial support for dynamic correspondences on compactifications, in the solid quasi-coherent formalism of Clausen–Scholze (§2), on a tower of smooth ordinary Igusa formal schemes over finite-level groups K_{p,P} ⊆ P′(Q_p) (§3), and on integral models at deep Iwahori level with Hecke correspondences at p controlled by Fargues's degree function and integral cohomological correspondences from the fundamental class of Fakhruddin–Pilloni (§4). The atlas plans solid modules and localization (SolidAnalyticRings, AnalyticStacks), the Siegel datum and moduli at good level (ShimuraData, PELModuli, ShimuraCompactifications), Iwasawa algebras and weight spaces, perfect complexes and the Hodge–Tate period map, but no cohomology with support for correspondences, no Siegel Igusa formal schemes, no deep-level Siegel models with Hecke correspondences at p, and no higher Hida theory. Routes: additions to four proposals made by other extractions, and one new Part II: HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the Part II of PadicFamilies proposed by PAPER-PILLONI-20; 247 items, the paper's core including its §2 formalism), IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (20), ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII (4), ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary (2), and a new Part II of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration on ordinary Igusa formal schemes of Siegel varieties (31); and source routes to seventeen roadmaps, chiefly the draft AnalyticStacks (six-functor inputs of §2) and ShimuraData (the root data of GSp_{2g} and the Kostant set). 133 mistakes are recorded, none previously known. Among them: the Serre duality pairing of Theorem 1.4.8 is Λ-bilinear only after twisting one factor by the involution t ↦ w_0t^{−1}; Theorem 1.3.8 claims a uniqueness that the cohomological degree does not give; the concrete description of ^M W uses the wrong order on {1, …, 2g}; several §2 statements need extra hypotheses (p₁ proper in Proposition 2.9.9, bounded below in Lemma 2.10.1(4)); and the proof of the Cousin spectral sequence (Theorem 4.5.2) leaves the vanishing of the E₁ terms with w ∉ C(κ) and two comparisons unproved.

items.name: Coherent cohomology complexes and their cuspidal counterparts
items.statement: For κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}, consider colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) and its cuspidal counterpart colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ(−D_{K,Σ})). The paper asserts that they are independent of the choice of Σ and are complexes of smooth admissible G(A_f)-representations.
items.note: Two claims are not planned. (1) Independence of the whole complex RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) (and its cuspidal version) from Σ: AutomorphicBundles B3 plans only 'independence of spaces of sections from the chosen sufficiently fine admissible fan', and ShimuraCompactifications C3 says 'Where higher direct images are required, make their vanishing a separate theorem'. (2) The action of G(A_f) on colim_K RΓ in all degrees, with smoothness and admissibility: B5 plans Hecke pullback and trace on sections only; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0 supplies the general notions ('Define admissibility by finite generation of every compact-open invariant module'). The genus-2 counterparts in Pilloni (Duke 2020), independence from the cone decomposition and the Hecke action on H^i, were classified missing and routed respectively to ShimuraCompactifications (source, C3/C5) and to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes; this item generalises both to genus g. External input: [Har90]; for independence of the cone decomposition cf. [Lan17] Prop. 7.5 (cited in §3.4.15)

items.name: Coherent cohomology is computed by automorphic forms (Su)
items.statement: After tensoring with C, the complexes colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) and colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ(−D_{K,Σ})) can be computed in terms of automorphic forms on G.
items.note: Planned nowhere. AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.5 is the Betti analogue ('compare relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of all smooth functions of the required growth'); no layer computes coherent cohomology of toroidal compactifications by automorphic forms. Harris's description of interior coherent cohomology, the nearest earlier item, was routed to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes in the extractions of Calegari–Geraghty (2020) and Pilloni (2020). External input: J. Su, Ann. Sci. ÉNS (4) 57 (2024), 1039–1099. External input: [Su24] J. Su, Coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties and automorphic forms, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4) 57 (2024), 1039–1099

items.name: Classical Hida theory for Siegel modular forms (background)
items.statement: p-adic modular forms are the functions on the ordinary Igusa variety that are invariant under the unipotent subgroup of the Borel of M_µ(Z_p). (1) They form a flat, p-adically complete Z_p-algebra with an action of Hecke operators and of the weight torus T(Z_p). (2) Restriction from the Shimura variety to its ordinary locus gives an injective map from classical modular forms H^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) to p-adic modular forms. (3) Control theorem: in regular and cohomological weight, the ordinary part of p-adic modular forms identifies with the ordinary classical modular forms. (4) Interpolation theorem: the ordinary part of cuspidal p-adic modular forms can be organized into a finite projective module over the Iwasawa algebra Z_p[[T(Z_p)]].
items.note: No layer plans Hida theory for GSp_{2g}. PadicFamilies L0 plans ordinary p-adic modular forms for modular curves and L5 for totally real fields; OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O7 is Hilbert and states 'Hida's ordinary-projector/control theorems require additional hypotheses and are not claimed merely from this coefficient comparison'. The generic ordinary projector (PadicFamilies L0a) and the Iwasawa algebra Z_p[[T(Z_p)]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1) are planned. This generalises the genus-2 degree-0 Hida theory of Pilloni (Duke 2020, the first layer of the proposed Part II) to genus g. External input: H. Hida, p-adic automorphic forms on Shimura varieties (2004). External input: [Hid04] and the references given there

items.name: Higher Hida theory for g = 1 ([BP22]) and for Hilbert modular varieties ([Gro22])
items.statement: For g = 1 there is a Hida theory for the H^1 coherent cohomology of modular curves. It is obtained by considering the cohomology with compact support of the ordinary locus and of the Igusa variety ([BP22]). Grossi extended this theory to Hilbert modular varieties over a totally real field F in which p is totally split ([Gro22]). The introduction writes 'when p splits in F'; the title of [Gro22] specifies the totally split case.
items.note: Planned nowhere. PadicFamilies plans Hida families for modular curves (L0) and totally real fields (L5) in cohomological degree 0 only; Hida theory for H^1 coherent cohomology via compactly supported cohomology of the ordinary locus is not planned. Background results (g = 1 is also the case g = 1 of Theorem 1.4.3). External inputs: Boxer–Pilloni, Épijournal Géom. Algébrique 6 (2022), Art. 16; Grossi (2022). External input: [BP22] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Hida and Coleman theories on the modular curve, Épijournal Géom. Algébrique 6 (2022), Art. 16; [Gro22] G. Grossi, Higher Hida theory for Hilbert modular varieties in the totally split case (2022)

items.name: Pilloni's higher Hida complex for GSp_4 in singular weight (background)
items.statement: For g = 2, along a one-dimensional line of the weight space corresponding to Galois representations with singular Hodge–Tate weights (0, 0, k−1, k−1), there is a complex M^0 → M^1 of amplitude [0, 1]. It interpolates the ordinary parts of H^0 and H^1 with coefficients in the singular-weight automorphic vector bundles ω^{(k,2)} ([Pil20]). Refinements and extensions were obtained in [BCGP21] (applied to potential modularity of abelian surfaces) and [LPSZ21] (applied to p-adic L-functions).
items.note: This is the main theorem of Pilloni (Duke 2020), Theorem 1.1: a perfect Λ-complex of amplitude [0,1] over Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] interpolating the ordinary H^0 and H^1 of Ω^{(k,2)}(−D). Its extraction classified it missing and routed it to the proposed HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, which can never be a planned target. The refinements of [BCGP21] and [LPSZ21] are not planned either. External input: [Pil20] V. Pilloni, Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights, Duke Math. J. 169 (2020); [BCGP21] Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021); [LPSZ21] Duke Math. J. 170 (2021)

items.name: Claim: Pilloni's M^0, M^1 extend over the whole weight space
items.statement: The paper claims to show that the modules M^0 and M^1 of [Pil20] extend over the entire weight space, as the higher Hida theories for H^0 and H^1, which interpolate regular-weight cohomology.
items.note: Planned nowhere. It generalises Pilloni's Theorem 1.1 from the one-dimensional singular-weight line to the whole weight space of GSp_4 (the modules become the higher Hida theories for w = Id and ℓ(w) = 1); the brief of the proposed Part II already names this paper as the future source for exactly this extension.

items.name: Higher Coleman theory (Boxer–Pilloni 2021)
items.statement: [BP21] develops higher Coleman theory for Shimura varieties of abelian type. This is the rational analogue of higher Hida theory, namely the theory of overconvergent modular forms in higher cohomological degree. It provides overconvergent and locally analytic overconvergent cohomologies with support conditions indexed by w ∈ ^MW, their finite slope parts, spectral sequences to classical cohomology, and eigenvarieties. It also proves classicality and vanishing theorems under 'strongly small slope' hypotheses; the weaker 'small slope' hypotheses need its slope-bound conjectures. This paper cites the following from [BP21]. Conjecture 5.10.7 (the Katz–Mazur inequality for classical coherent cohomology), together with 5.10.12 (the case κ + ρ regular) and Theorem 6.10.1 (interior cohomology). Conjectures 5.9.2 and 6.8.1 (lower bounds on slopes of overconvergent and locally analytic overconvergent cohomology). The classicality results 5.12.3 and 6.8.4. The vanishing theorems 5.12.5, 5.12.11 and 5.12.20, and Theorem 6.9.3(2). Theorem 6.7.3: finite slope cuspidal locally analytic cohomology is concentrated in degrees [0, ℓ(w)] and the non-cuspidal one in [ℓ(w), d]. Lemma 5.9.10 (construction of lattices). In the October 2021 arXiv version of [BP21], 5.10.12 and 6.8.4 are corollaries.
items.note: Higher Coleman theory is planned nowhere. Ingredients are planned: overconvergent coefficient sheaves on Siegel varieties of every genus (OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O8: 'Instantiate the general coefficient construction on Siegel varieties of arbitrary genus on the proven anticanonical domains'), compact operators and Fredholm theory (LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4), eigenvariety gluing (PadicFamilies L2a). Overconvergent and locally analytic cohomology with support conditions indexed by ^MW, its finite-slope parts, the spectral sequences to classical cohomology, and the classicality and vanishing theorems are not. The Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni guide asks for higher Coleman theory as its own roadmap; the proposed Part II carries the genus-2 Klingen-level theory of Pilloni (2020), and [BP21] is its general (abelian-type) form. External input: G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, arXiv:2110.10251. External input: [BP21] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, arXiv:2110.10251 (2021); numbering checked against arXiv v1

items.name: Higher Hida theory as ordinary cohomology with supports; independence of the support condition (Remark 1.3.2)
items.statement: Each w ∈ ^MW determines support conditions on the ordinary Igusa variety. Higher Hida theory for w is constructed as the ordinary part of cohomology with these support conditions. The authors found the definition of the support conditions subtle: except for the degree 0 and top degree theories, there does not seem to be a canonical choice of support condition. There are many suitable support conditions, and they all give the same ordinary cohomology. Section 2 shows that there is at most one reasonable way to attach an ordinary cohomology theory (the ordinary part of a cohomology with partial support) to a scheme and a correspondence over it. For this reason the paper defines only the ordinary part of a space of higher p-adic modular forms, not the space itself.
items.note: Planned nowhere: ordinary cohomology with support conditions on the ordinary Igusa variety, and its independence of the support condition (proved in §2.11, 'change of support'), belong to the new theory of this paper.

items.name: M_µ-dominant weights as Weyl translates of dominant weights
items.note: Kostant's description of the M_µ-dominant weights is planned nowhere; the Calegari–Geraghty (2020) companion statement W^M = {w : w X*(T)^+ ⊆ X*(T)^+_M} was classified missing and routed to ShimuraData. Checked: for w ∈ ^MW, w^{-1} sends positive roots of M_µ to positive roots, so w X*(T)^+ is M_µ-dominant; conversely an M_µ-dominant μ = vλ with λ dominant and v = uw (u ∈ W_M, w ∈ ^MW) satisfies u^{-1}μ = wλ, and both are M_µ-dominant in one W_M-orbit, so μ = wλ. Tau Ceti has the existence half of the fundamental-domain statement (TauCeti.exists_mem_dominantChamber); uniqueness of the dominant representative is planned in Tau Ceti RootSystems Layer 4.

items.name: ν + ρ is the infinitesimal character in weight κ
items.statement: For κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}, ν + ρ = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) (for w ∈ C(κ)) is the dominant representative of the infinitesimal character of the automorphic forms that contribute to the coherent cohomology in weight κ.
items.note: Planned nowhere. The general notions are planned: infinitesimal characters (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4: 'Define algebraic highest weights, infinitesimal characters and cohomological representations') and central characters up to the dot action (Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 7: 'χ_λ = χ_μ ⟺ μ ∈ W·λ'). The computation of the infinitesimal character of automorphic forms contributing to coherent cohomology in weight κ, via (p_µ, K_∞)-cohomology, is not. The paper gives no reference; it is [Har90] Prop. 3.1.4 as used in [BP21] Prop. 5.10.3. The corresponding genus-2 items of Pilloni (2020) and Calegari–Geraghty (2020) were routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups. External input: [Har90] Prop. 3.1.4, as cited in [BP21] Prop. 5.10.3 (the paper itself gives no reference)

items.name: Jacquet module J_B
items.statement: If π is a smooth admissible representation of G(Q_p) defined over Q_p, J_B(π) denotes its Jacquet module with respect to B. It is a smooth admissible T(Q_p)-representation.
items.note: Planned: J_B(π) is the N-coinvariants of SR.2 for P = B. SR.2 does not list as a target the admissibility of J_B(π) for admissible π (Jacquet's theorem, proved in [Cas]); its blueprint should state it. Earlier extractions classified the same definition planned at SR.2. External input: [Cas] W. Casselman, Introduction to admissible representations of p-adic groups

items.name: Slope v(χ) of a character of T(Q_p)
items.statement: For a character χ : T(Q_p) → Q̄_p^×, composing with the valuation v : Q̄_p^× → R gives v(χ) : T(Q_p)/T(Z_p) → R. Through T(Q_p)/T(Z_p) ≅ X_⋆(T), v(χ) is regarded as an element of X⋆(T)_R.
items.note: Planned nowhere. It uses the identification T(Q_p)/T(Z_p) ≅ X_*(T), λ(p) ↔ λ, for the split torus, so that a homomorphism T(Q_p)/T(Z_p) → R is an element of Hom(X_*(T), R) = X*(T)_R; this normalisation is not stated in any layer.

items.name: Character ordinary in weight κ (Definition 1.3.5)
items.statement: A character χ : T(Q_p) → Q̄_p^× is ordinary in weight κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} if v(χ) = w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) + ρ = −ν (for w ∈ C(κ); the value does not depend on w).
items.note: Planned nowhere. Checked: ν + ρ = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) gives w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) + ρ = −ν, so the two printed forms of the condition agree and do not depend on w ∈ C(κ).

items.name: Ordinary part J_B^{ord} of the Jacquet module
items.statement: J_B^{ord}(colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ)) is the sum of the generalized eigenspaces, for the characters that are ordinary in weight κ, in the Jacquet module J_B(colim_K RΓ(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ)).
items.note: Planned nowhere. Mathlib has generalized eigenspaces of a single endomorphism (Module.End.maxGenEigenspace), and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans the Jacquet functor; the sum of generalized eigenspaces of T(Q_p) for the characters ordinary in weight κ, on the Jacquet module of the colimit of coherent cohomology, is not planned.

items.name: Katz–Mazur inequality v(χ) ≥ −ν (Remark 1.3.6)
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} and let ν = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) − ρ for w ∈ C(κ). Katz–Mazur inequality: every character χ of T(Q_p) occurring in the Jacquet module of the coherent cohomology in weight κ satisfies v(χ) ≥ −ν, for the partial order on X⋆(T)_R in which λ ≥ λ′ means that λ − λ′ is a non-negative combination of positive roots. The ordinary characters (Definition 1.3.5) are those with equality, so ordinarity means that the Newton and Hodge polygons match. The introduction presents the inequality as a postulate, citing [BP21] Conjecture 5.10.7, which is proved there when κ + ρ is regular and for interior cohomology. For Siegel Shimura varieties the paper proves it in Remark 4.3.19: the normalized Hecke operators for t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) preserve a lattice in rational coherent cohomology.
items.locator: §1.3.4, Remark 1.3.6, p. 3; Siegel case: Remark 4.3.19, p. 49
items.note: Planned nowhere. In general it is [BP21] Conjecture 5.10.7 and must be recorded as a Prop-valued statement, never assumed; the proved cases (κ + ρ regular, and interior cohomology) are [BP21] results. It generalises the slope bounds of Pilloni (2020) for GSp_4 (Proposition 13.3.1.1 and the valuations of ordinary Hecke parameters in Corollary 14.9.1), which were routed to the proposed Part II. External input: [BP21] Conjecture 5.10.7 (stated there as a conjecture); proved there when κ + ρ is regular ([BP21] Corollary 5.10.12, cited as 'thm. 5.10.12') and for interior cohomology ([BP21] Thm. 6.10.1)

items.name: Hecke operators at p from an Iwahori decomposition
items.statement: Let K_p ⊆ G(Q_p) be a compact open subgroup admitting an Iwahori decomposition K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p}, with respect to the unipotent radicals of B and of the opposite Borel. Let T^+(Q_p) ⊆ T(Q_p) be the monoid of t whose image v(t) ∈ X_⋆(T) is dominant. Here v : T(Q_p) → X_⋆(T) is induced by the valuation (normalized by v(p) = 1), with section λ ↦ λ(p). Then t ↦ [K_p t K_p] defines an algebra morphism Z[T^+(Q_p)/T_{K_p}] → C_c^0(K_p\G(Q_p)/K_p, Z).
items.locator: §1.3.4, p. 3; T^+(Q_p) defined in §3.1, p. 34; used for K_{p,n} on p. 43
items.note: Planned nowhere. SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1 plans Hecke algebras over rings and 'integral double-coset operators by finite correspondences'; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4 plans the Iwahori–Bruhat decomposition of G(E) into double cosets, which is not the factorisation K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p}; PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.2 constructs 'commuting positive-monoid operators' only for its unitary application. The multiplicativity [K_p t K_p][K_p t′ K_p] = [K_p tt′ K_p] for t, t′ ∈ T^+(Q_p) is not stated anywhere. Casselman's results on Iwahori-level invariants were routed to SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups in earlier extractions. The paper uses the case K_p = K_{p,n}, the subgroup of matrices in G(Z_p) that reduce modulo p^n into B(Z/p^nZ) (§4.1, p. 40), for which T_{K_{p,n}} = T(Z_p). In §4.2 (p. 43) it cites Casselman's notes [Cas], Lemma 4.1.5, for the algebra map Z[T^+(Q_p)/T(Z_p)] → C_c(K_{p,n}\G(Q_p)/K_{p,n}, Z) sending t to the characteristic function of K_{p,n}tK_{p,n}. It then attaches a Hecke correspondence and an integral model to each such double coset. External input: Standard fact, stated without reference (cf. [Cas] §4.1)

items.name: Ordinary part RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord}
items.statement: For K_p with an Iwahori decomposition as above, RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} is the direct factor of RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ) on which T^+(Q_p) (acting by the operators [K_p t K_p]) acts through invertible operators and the associated characters of T(Q_p) are ordinary in weight κ.
items.note: The part on which the operators [K_p t K_p], t ∈ T^+(Q_p), act invertibly is an instance of PadicFamilies L0a ('Apply the result degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U and differential'); the further restriction to characters ordinary in weight κ, and the Hecke action at p on coherent cohomology of S^tor_{K^pK_p}, are planned nowhere.

items.name: Ordinary cohomology via the Jacquet module
items.statement: For K_p with an Iwahori decomposition K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p} and fixed K^p, there is a natural quasi-isomorphism of complexes of smooth T(Q_p)-representations RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ≅ J_B^{ord}(colim_{K′_p} RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK′_p,Σ}, ω^κ))^{T_{K_p}}, where the colimit runs over compact open K′_p ⊆ G(Q_p) [printed with colim_K over all levels; sourceIssues E4].
items.note: Planned nowhere. The local input is Casselman's canonical lifting V^{K_p} → J_B(V)^{T_{K_p}}, an isomorphism on the part where T^+ acts invertibly; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans Jacquet functors but not this comparison. The paper gives neither proof nor reference. The statement takes the colimit over p-levels at fixed K^p; p. 3 prints colim_K over all levels. External input: Casselman's canonical lifting, [Cas] Lemma 4.1.1 and Prop. 4.1.4 (the form used in [BP21] Prop. 4.3.1); no proof or reference is given in the text

items.name: Non-degenerate limits of discrete series indexed by C(κ) (Theorem 1.3.8)
items.statement: Let K_∞ ⊆ G(R) be the stabilizer of h (a real form of M_µ), V_κ the representation of K_∞ of highest weight κ, and p_µ the Lie algebra of P_µ. Let κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} and w ∈ C(κ). There exists a non-degenerate limit of discrete series representation π_∞(κ, w) of G(R), uniquely attached to (κ, w), such that π_∞(κ, w) ⊗ V_κ has (p_µ, K_∞)-cohomology in degree ℓ(w).
items.note: Planned nowhere. AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 plans only (g, K)-cochains ('Define relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k),V)'); non-degenerate limits of discrete series and (p_µ, K_∞)-cohomology are not planned. It generalises to GSp_{2g} the GSp_4 items of Pilloni (2020) on limits of discrete series π(λ, C) and their (p, K_∞)-cohomology, which were routed to AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups. External input: [Har90] Thm. 3.4 (as cited).

items.name: Cuspidal representations with π_∞ = π_∞(κ,w) contribute to H^{ℓ(w)}
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}, w ∈ C(κ), and let π = π_∞(κ, w) ⊗ π_f be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G. Then π_f ↪ colim_K H^{ℓ(w)}(S^tor_{K,Σ}, ω^κ) ⊗ C. When w = Id, π_∞(κ, Id) is a holomorphic limit of discrete series and π is generated by holomorphic modular forms.
items.note: Planned nowhere. AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms as sections with the transformation law; the passage from a cuspidal π with π_∞ = π_∞(κ, w) to H^{ℓ(w)} is not planned. It generalises the genus-2 degree-0 statement of Pilloni (2020) (holomorphic cusp forms embed in H^0), routed to the proposed IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, to all degrees ℓ(w) and genus g. External input: No reference given (cf. [Har90], [Su24])

items.name: Hodge–Tate period map and T(Q_p)-fixed points
items.statement: Let S_{K^p} be the good reduction perfectoid Siegel Shimura variety of tame level K^p. The Hodge–Tate period map is π_HT : S_{K^p} → FL = P_µ\G. The set ^MW (identified with W_M\W) is the set of fixed points of T(Q_p) acting on FL.
items.note: Planned: the perfectoid Siegel variety at infinite level at p (S1) and π_HT to the flag variety (S3, T2), as in the Caraiani–Scholze (2017) extraction. The sentence identifying ^MW with the T(Q_p)-fixed points of FL is stated in no layer; it follows from the Bruhat decomposition planned in Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7 ('Bruhat decomposition and BN-pairs / Tits systems'), and its blueprint should add it. External input: [Sch15]. External input: [Sch15] P. Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties, Ann. of Math. 182 (2015)

items.name: Tame level K^p and the spherical Hecke algebra T^sph
items.statement: K^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} K_ℓ is a product compact open subgroup of G(A_f^p) (neat, as fixed in §3.3). T^sph is the abstract Hecke algebra given by the restricted tensor product of the spherical Hecke algebras at all primes ℓ ≠ p for which K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ) is hyperspecial.
items.note: Planned. Neat tame level (D5), the local spherical Hecke algebras at hyperspecial K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ) (SR.1, SR.4) and restricted tensor products of local compactly supported functions (AF.0). The genus-2 spherical Hecke algebra of Pilloni (2020) was classified planned at SR.1, SR.4 and ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.4.

items.name: T′(Z_p), C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p) and Λ′
items.statement: T′(Z_p) is the pro-p subgroup of T(Z_p). C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p) is the T′(Z_p)-module of continuous Z_p-valued functions on T′(Z_p). Its Z_p-dual is the algebra of measures on T′(Z_p), equal to the completed group algebra Λ′ = Z_p[[T′(Z_p)]].
items.note: Planned: continuous functions on the profinite group T′(Z_p), measures as their dual, and the identification of integral measures with Λ′ = Z_p[[T′(Z_p)]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0–L1; Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups plans the completed group algebra). T′(Z_p) is the pro-p part of T(Z_p) ≅ (Z_p^×)^{g+1}.

items.name: Admissible complex and its amplitude (Definition 1.4.1)
items.statement: A complex in D(Z_p[T′(Z_p)]) is admissible if it can be represented by a bounded complex M^• of T′(Z_p)-modules with each M^i isomorphic to C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p)^{n_i}. An admissible complex has amplitude [a, b] if it can be represented by such a complex M^• concentrated in degrees [a, b].
items.note: Planned nowhere; the notion is specific to this paper. Its ingredients are planned: C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0) and bounded complexes in derived categories (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7).

items.name: The dual of an admissible complex is perfect over Λ′ (Remark 1.4.2)
items.statement: If a complex is admissible, then its Z_p-dual is a perfect complex over the Iwasawa algebra Λ′. If it has amplitude [a, b], then its dual has amplitude [−b, −a] over Λ′.
items.note: Missing because 'admissible' is. The proof is immediate from planned material: the Z_p-dual of C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p) is Λ′ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0–L1), so the dual of an admissible complex in degrees [a, b] is a bounded complex of finite free Λ′-modules in degrees [−b, −a]; perfect complexes and their duals are DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7 ('construct minimal representatives over local rings, uniqueness up to homotopy, Tor-amplitude, duals').

items.name: Classicality in regular weight (Theorem 1.4.3(4))
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW, ν ∈ X⋆(T)^+, and κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν + ρ) − ρ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}. Let K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p} be a compact open subgroup of G(Q_p) admitting an Iwahori decomposition, and let n ∈ Z_{≥0} satisfy {t ∈ T(Z_p) : t ≡ 1 mod p^n} ⊆ T_{K_p}. Then there is a T(Q_p)-equivariant quasi-isomorphism RHom_{T_{K_p}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p)) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n})(−ν) ≅ RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}), and similarly for cuspidal cohomology (RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) and ω^κ(−D)).
items.locator: §1.4, Theorem 1.4.3(4), p. 5; body: Corollary 4.5.5 (p. 52) with the control Theorem 5.3.5 (p. 56)
items.note: Main theorem, planned nowhere. It generalises the control theorem of Pilloni (2020), Theorem 1.1(1) and Theorem 11.3.1(3), to GSp_{2g}, all w and all regular weights. Checked: κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν + ρ) − ρ is equivalent to ν + ρ = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ), so w ∈ C(κ) and the weights match §1.3.3.

items.name: Cousin spectral sequence (Theorem 1.4.3(5))
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} and ν = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) − ρ for any w ∈ C(κ). Let K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p} be a compact open subgroup of G(Q_p) admitting an Iwahori decomposition, and let n ∈ Z_{≥0} satisfy {t ∈ T(Z_p) : t ≡ 1 mod p^n} ⊆ T_{K_p}. There is a T(Q_p)-equivariant spectral sequence ⊕_{w ∈ C(κ), ℓ(w) = a} H^{a+b}(RHom_{T_{K_p}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p))) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n})(−ν) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}).
items.note: Main theorem, planned nowhere. The Cousin complex of §4.5 and its spectral sequence from the w-graded higher Hida cohomologies to ordinary classical cohomology are new; point (4) of Theorem 1.4.3 is its degenerate case when #C(κ) = 1 (Remark 1.4.5).

items.name: Interpolation of ordinary classical cohomology (Proposition 1.4.7)
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW. Let ν = ν_alg χ : T(Z_p) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× with ν_alg ∈ X⋆(T)^+ and χ a finite order character, and let κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν_alg + ρ) − ρ. Let K_p = U_{K_p} × T_{K_p} × Ū_{K_p} be a compact open subgroup of G(Q_p) admitting an Iwahori decomposition, with T_{K_p} ⊆ ker χ. Then M^•_w ⊗_{Λ,−ν} Q_p(ζ_{p^n}) ≅ RΓ(S^tor_{K^pK_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} ⊗_{Q_p} Q_p(ζ_{p^n})[χ], where [χ] denotes the χ-isotypic part for the diamond operators in T(Z_p)/T_{K_p}. A similar statement holds for cuspidal cohomology.
items.note: Planned nowhere. It generalises Pilloni (2020), Theorem 1.1(1), to the whole weight space and all w. On p. 5 the right-hand side prints Q_p(ζ^n_p) for Q_p(ζ_{p^n}), a misprint; the statement uses Q_p(ζ_{p^n}).

items.name: The involution w ↦ w_{0,M} w w_0 of ^MW
items.statement: The map w ↦ w_{0,M} w w_0 is an involution of ^MW.
items.note: Planned nowhere. Checked by direct computation: w ↦ w_{0,M}ww_0 squares to the identity, and it preserves ^MW, because for a positive root α of M_µ, (w_{0,M}ww_0)^{-1}α = w_0w^{-1}(w_{0,M}α) with w_{0,M}α a negative root of M_µ, w^{-1} sending it to a negative root (w ∈ ^MW) and w_0 to a positive one.

items.name: Slope 0 higher Coleman theory = rational higher Hida theory (Theorem 1.4.9)
items.statement: The slope 0 part of higher Coleman theory canonically identifies with the rational part of higher Hida theory (informal statement).
items.locator: §1.4, Theorem 1.4.9, p. 6; precise forms Theorems 6.2.9 (p. 62) and 6.2.15 (p. 64)
items.note: Planned nowhere. It generalises the comparison of Pilloni (2020) between the overconvergent complex M† and M ⊗ Q_p (quasi-isomorphism in all weights), routed to the proposed Part II, to GSp_{2g} and all w. Precise content (Theorems 6.2.9, p. 62, and 6.2.15, p. 64). Fix w ∈ ^MW, t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and ε ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q. In fixed weight, t acts on the integral overconvergent cohomology RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ))^{int}. This is the limit over s of the cohomologies over Z/p^s with support in the closed subset Ẑ_{<w+ε} ∩ 𝒰_{≥w−ε} of the locale, taken with coefficients in an integral model ω̃^κ(χ). Its ordinary part is the higher Hida complex RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ) (Theorem 6.2.9(1), (2)). After inverting p it becomes the overconvergent cohomology whose support condition is defined by the degrees of the subgroups H_{g+i}. Its image in each slope ≤ h part, a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space, is a Z_p-lattice (Theorem 6.2.9(3)). The finite slope part of this cohomology agrees canonically with that of the overconvergent cohomology of [BP21], whose support condition is defined by the Hodge–Tate period map. The reason is that both support conditions cut out S^tor_w (Propositions 6.1.7, 6.1.10 and 6.1.11, pp. 59–60). In families over a quasi-compact open Spa(A[1/p], A) of the weight space W, the ordinary part of the corresponding integral cohomology of the locally analytic induction sheaf is M_w^• ⊗_Λ A (Theorem 6.2.15(1)).

items.name: Γ(N) ⊆ Sp_{2g}(Z), its Hecke algebra and ordinary cohomology
items.statement: Let N be an integer divisible by p and Γ = {γ ∈ Sp_{2g}(Z) : γ ≡ 1 mod N}. H^⋆(Γ, Z) is the cohomology of Γ with coefficients in the trivial module Z; it is finitely generated in each degree (printed 'finite'). The Hecke algebra T_N is generated by the double classes [ΓtΓ], t ∈ Sp_{2g}(Q), acting by [ΓtΓ] : H^⋆(Γ, Z) → H^⋆(t^{-1}Γt ∩ Γ, Z) → H^⋆(tΓt^{-1} ∩ Γ, Z) → H^⋆(Γ, Z) (restriction, conjugation by t, corestriction). For 0 ≤ i ≤ g, t_i = diag(p, …, p, 1, …, 1, p^{-1}, …, p^{-1}) is the diagonal matrix with 2i entries equal to 1; the double classes {Γt_iΓ}_{0≤i≤g} generate a commutative subalgebra of T_N. H^⋆(Γ, Z_p) = H^⋆(Γ, Z) ⊗_Z Z_p and H^⋆(Γ, Q_p) = H^⋆(Γ, Z) ⊗_Z Q_p. H^⋆(Γ, Z_p)^{ord} ⊆ H^⋆(Γ, Z_p) is the direct factor on which the operators [Γt_iΓ] act invertibly, and H^⋆(Γ, Q_p)^{ord} = H^⋆(Γ, Z_p)^{ord} ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p.
items.note: Parts are available or planned, the whole is not. Mathlib has group cohomology (groupCohomology), restriction (groupCohomology.resNatTrans), the map induced by a group homomorphism, such as conjugation by t (groupCohomology.map), and symplectic matrices (Matrix.symplecticGroup); it has no corestriction in group cohomology and no principal congruence subgroups of Sp_{2g}(Z). ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.3 plans the same double-coset operators on locally symmetric spaces ('construct the two finite-level maps through K∩gKg⁻¹, pullback and trace ... composition via the double-coset algebra'), ALS.1 plans finite projective models (hence finite generation), and PadicFamilies L0a plans the ordinary projector. The commutativity of the subalgebra generated by the [Γt_iΓ] is stated nowhere. p. 6 prints 'a finite Z-module'; H^*(Γ, Z) is finitely generated in each degree.

items.name: Vanishing of ordinary cohomology of Γ(N) below the middle degree (Theorem 1.5.1)
items.statement: Let N be divisible by p and Γ = {γ ∈ Sp_{2g}(Z) : γ ≡ 1 mod N}. Then H^i(Γ, Q_p)^{ord} = 0 for 0 ≤ i < g(g+1)/2.
items.note: Application, planned nowhere; it is deduced on p. 62 from the rational vanishing and the comparison with higher Coleman theory.

items.name: Expected degrees of tempered cohomology (Remark 1.5.2)
items.statement: It is generally believed that the tempered part of H^⋆(Γ, Q) is concentrated in degrees ≥ g(g+1)/2. Theorem 1.5.1 is the analogue with temperedness (a condition on the archimedean size of Hecke eigenvalues) replaced by ordinarity (a condition on their p-adic size).
items.note: An expectation, not a theorem of the paper; record it as a Prop-valued statement, never assumed. Relative Lie algebra cohomology, which controls the tempered degrees, is planned in AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1; the statement for the cohomology of Γ is planned nowhere. External input: [Ven17] §4.2. External input: [Ven17] A. Venkatesh, Cohomology of arithmetic groups and periods of automorphic forms, Jpn. J. Math. 12 (2017), sect. 4.2

items.name: Compactification of a scheme (Definition 2.1.2)
items.statement: Let S be a noetherian affine scheme; all schemes are S-schemes. Let X be a separated S-scheme of finite type. A compactification of X (over S) is a proper S-scheme X̄ together with an open immersion j_X : X ↪ X̄. A map of compactifications ξ : (j_X : X ↪ X̄) → (j′_X : X ↪ X̄′) is a map of S-schemes ξ : X̄ → X̄′ extending the identity of X.
items.note: Planned. The notions in the definition (proper S-scheme, open immersion, morphisms over S) are in Mathlib; compactifications of separated finite-type morphisms and their category are owned by AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2.

items.name: Nagata compactification (Remark 2.1.3)
items.statement: Every separated S-scheme X of finite type (S noetherian affine) admits a compactification.
items.note: Planned: L2 plans Nagata's theorem for separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes, which contains the case of a noetherian affine base. L2 attributes the noetherian base case to the upstream compact-support proposal and owns the extension. External input: Nagata's theorem, [Sta22] Tag 0F41

items.name: Strict map of compactifications
items.statement: A map of compactifications ξ : (j_X : X ↪ X̄) → (j′_X : X ↪ X̄′) is strict if ξ^⋆X = X, i.e. the inverse image under ξ of X ⊆ X̄′ is X ⊆ X̄.
items.note: Planned nowhere. The Zavyalov (2025) extraction classified the same strict-morphism adapter for compactifications missing and routed it to AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2.

items.name: Compactifications with Cartier boundary are cofinal (Lemma 2.1.5)
items.statement: Compactifications j_X : X ↪ X̄ such that X̄ \ X admits the structure of an effective Cartier divisor in X̄ are cofinal among compactifications, and the maps to a given compactification can be taken to be strict.
items.note: Planned nowhere. Blow-ups are planned only in restricted scope: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7a ('Construct blowups by the Rees algebra with their projective universal property') within 'varieties of finite type over a characteristic-zero field', and AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5 ('flattening by blowup, strict transforms'). The proof on p. 7 prints 'the blow-up of X at the ideal I' for the blow-up of X̄ along I. External input: [Sta22] Tag 02OS

items.name: Compactifications to which a vector bundle extends are cofinal (Lemma 2.1.6)
items.statement: Let F be a locally free sheaf of finite rank on X. The compactifications j_X : X ↪ X̄ such that F extends to a locally free sheaf on X̄ are cofinal among compactifications, with strict maps.
items.note: Planned nowhere. It needs extension of coherent sheaves over a compactification and a blow-up making the strict transform locally free; the latter is AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5's 'flattening by blowup'. External input: [Sta22] Tag 0G41 (coherent extension), Tag 0ESN (blow-up making the strict transform locally free)

items.name: Compactification of a correspondence (Definition 2.1.9, Remark 2.1.10)
items.statement: A compactification (C̄, X̄, p̄_1, p̄_2) of a correspondence (C, X, p_1, p_2) is a commutative diagram with open immersions j_C : C ↪ C̄ and j_X : X ↪ X̄, maps p̄_1, p̄_2 : C̄ → X̄ extending j_X ∘ p_1 and j_X ∘ p_2, X̄ and C̄ proper over S, and C = C̄ ×_{X̄×X̄} (X × X). In particular (C̄, X̄, p̄_1, p̄_2) is itself a correspondence.
items.note: Planned nowhere. It uses compactifications (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2) and serves the formalism of cohomology with support for correspondences in the rest of §2, which is new with this paper. Remark 2.1.10 holds because C̄ is proper over S and X̄ ×_S X̄ is separated.

items.name: Standing assumptions of §2: noetherian affine base S, schemes of finite type over Z
items.statement: In §2.1, S is a noetherian affine scheme and one works in the category of S-schemes; products such as X × X and X̄ × X̄ are fibre products over S. From §2.2 on, all schemes are also assumed to be of finite type over Z, so that the solid quasi-coherent formalism of Clausen–Scholze applies to them. The subsections §2.2.1–§2.2.3 still speak of S-schemes.
items.note: The conventions of §2.1 (p. 7) and §2.2 (p. 12) are Mathlib notions: S is IsNoetherian and IsAffine; S-schemes are schemes with Scheme.Over S, and X × X means the fibre product over S; 'of finite type over Z' is LocallyOfFiniteType together with QuasiCompact for the structure morphism to Spec Z (Mathlib has no single finite-type class for morphisms of schemes). The reason given on p. 12, that such schemes carry the Clausen–Scholze solid quasi-coherent formalism, is not supplied by either library; that formalism is recorded separately and is missing.

items.name: Compactifications of a scheme form a cofiltered category
items.statement: The category of compactifications of X is cofiltered. Any two compactifications X̄, X̄' of X are dominated by a third: the closure of the diagonal image of X in X̄ ×_S X̄' is a compactification of X that maps to both X̄ and X̄'.
items.note: The domination statement of p. 7 is exactly the filteredness L2 plans. The construction on p. 7 takes the scheme-theoretic closure of the diagonal image of X in X̄ ×_S X̄'; Mathlib has the scheme-theoretic image of a morphism (Scheme.Hom.image, cut out by the kernel ideal sheaf, with the factorisation Scheme.Hom.toImage), and the library audit of L2 lists 'Scheme-theoretic image and closure' as present in Mathlib. The refinement 'with strict maps', used later in the paper, is recorded separately.

items.name: A map out of a compactification in which X is dense is strict
items.statement: Let ξ : (j_X : X ↪ X̄) → (j'_X : X ↪ X̄') be a map of compactifications of X, and assume that X is dense in X̄. Then ξ is strict.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.4 (p. 7) is planned nowhere. Its proof uses only library facts: the section s of the separated morphism ξ^{-1}(X) → X is a closed immersion (Mathlib's IsClosedImmersion.of_comp: if f ≫ g is a closed immersion and g is separated, f is a closed immersion); s is also an open immersion because j_X is; and an open and closed immersion with dense image is an isomorphism. It is a general lemma about compactifications and goes with the strictness condition.

items.name: Blow-ups: exceptional divisor is Cartier; blowing up a product of ideals
items.statement: Let Y be a scheme, I ⊆ O_Y a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type (e.g. a coherent ideal on a noetherian Y), Z = V(I), and b : Y′ → Y the blow-up of Y along I. Then b is an isomorphism over Y \ Z, and the exceptional divisor b^{-1}(Z) = V(I·O_{Y′}) is an effective Cartier divisor on Y′ ([Sta22], Tag 02OS); b is projective. The complement of an effective Cartier divisor is scheme-theoretically dense ([Sta22], Tag 07ZU; used without reference in the proof of Lemma 2.1.5). For two such ideals I, J, the blow-up along IJ is the blow-up along I followed by the blow-up along J·O ([Sta22], Tag 080A). Since IJ = JI, both I·O and J·O are invertible on the blow-up along IJ.
items.locator: §2.1.1, proof of Lemma 2.1.5, p. 7; §2.1.25, proof of Lemma 2.1.30, p. 10
items.note: Projectivity, the isomorphism away from the centre and the Cartier exceptional divisor are named in StableReduction Layer 4 (the library audit of R09.7a records the two layers as the same blow-up package). The two further facts cited in the proofs of Lemmas 2.1.5 and 2.1.30 (pp. 7 and 10), that the complement of an effective Cartier divisor is scheme-theoretically dense and that the blow-up along IJ is the blow-up along I followed by the blow-up along J·O, are not named there; they follow from the local nonzerodivisor equation and from the universal property, and the blueprint of Layer 4 must state them. Mathlib has only the ring-level Rees algebra; the audits record blow-ups and effective Cartier divisors (even absolute ones) as absent. External input: The Stacks Project [Sta22], Tags 02OS and 080A (cited in the proofs of Lemmas 2.1.5 and 2.1.30).

items.name: Coherent sheaves extend from open subschemes and are pseudo-coherent
items.statement: Let X̄ be a noetherian scheme and X ⊆ X̄ an open subscheme. Every coherent O_X-module F is the restriction of some coherent O_X̄-module F̄. Coherent modules on a noetherian scheme are pseudo-coherent.
items.note: Mathlib has quasi-coherent and finitely presented sheaves of modules (SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent, SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation) but neither library has the theorem that a coherent sheaf on an open subscheme of a noetherian scheme extends to a coherent sheaf, nor pseudo-coherent complexes on schemes. No atlas layer states either. SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 ('Construct schemes, quasi-coherent modules and relative Spec/Proj, affine gluing and fiber products') owns quasi-coherent modules and is the natural home of the extension theorem. On p. 16 pseudo-coherence is used for objects of the solid category D(O_{X̄,■}), which comes with the solid formalism. External input: The Stacks Project [Sta22], Tag 0G41 (cited in Lemma 2.1.6 and Remark 2.3.3).

items.name: Flattening by blow-up (Raynaud–Gruson)
items.statement: Flattening by blow-up, in the form cited in the proof of Lemma 2.1.6 ([Sta22], Tag 0ESN). Let X̄ be a scheme and F̄ a finitely presented O_X̄-module (e.g. a coherent module on a noetherian scheme). Let X ⊆ X̄ be a scheme-theoretically dense open subscheme such that F̄|_X is finite locally free of constant rank r. Let b : X̄′ → X̄ be the blow-up of X̄ in the r-th Fitting ideal of F̄. Then the centre of b is disjoint from X, and the strict transform of F̄ on X̄′ (the quotient of b^*F̄ by its sections supported on b^{-1}(X̄ \ X)) is locally free of rank r. The density and constant-rank hypotheses can be dropped using the flattening theorem of Raynaud–Gruson ([Sta22], Tag 0815). Let X̄ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, X ⊆ X̄ a quasi-compact open subscheme, and F̄ of finite type with F̄|_X locally free of finite rank. Then there is a blow-up X̄′ → X̄ with centre disjoint from X such that the strict transform of F̄ is flat and of finite presentation, hence locally free of finite rank.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.6 (p. 7) needs the Raynaud–Gruson form: a coherent sheaf that is locally free on the open X becomes flat, hence locally free, after a blow-up with centre disjoint from X. L5 plans flattening by blow-up and strict transforms for schemes of finite type, the setting used here. The library audit of L5 records 'Blowups, strict transforms and flattening by blowup' as absent from both libraries. External input: Raynaud–Gruson flattening by blow-up; The Stacks Project [Sta22], Tag 0ESN (cited in Lemma 2.1.6).

items.name: Correspondence
items.statement: A correspondence is a quadruple (C, X, p1, p2), where X and C are separated S-schemes of finite type and p1, p2 : C ⇉ X are S-morphisms such that p1 × p2 : C → X ×_S X is proper.
items.note: Definition 2.1.8 (p. 7) is a combination of Mathlib notions: C and X separated of finite type over S, two S-morphisms p1, p2 : C → X, and IsProper for pullback.lift p1 p2 : C → X ×_S X. Neither library has a named correspondence structure. PAPER-PILLONI-20 records Pilloni's Definition 4.3.1(1), a bare span of S-schemes, as library in the same way; Boxer–Pilloni add the properness of p1 × p2, which the proof of Lemma 2.1.11 uses.

items.name: Compactifications of correspondences exist
items.statement: Every correspondence (C, X, p1, p2) admits a compactification.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.11 (p. 8) is planned nowhere. The proof uses Nagata compactifications of X and C (planned in AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2), the scheme-theoretic closure of C in C̄' × X̄ × X̄ (Mathlib's Scheme.Hom.image), and the fact that an open immersion with dense image between schemes proper over X × X is proper, hence an isomorphism.

items.name: Maps and strict maps of compactifications of a correspondence
items.statement: A map (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) → (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2) between compactifications of (C, X, p1, p2) consists of morphisms C̄ → C̄' and X̄ → X̄' that induce the identity on C and on X and commute with the p̄_i and p̄'_i. Such a map is strict if X̄ → X̄' is a strict map of compactifications of X.
items.note: The definition on p. 8 is new with the paper and planned nowhere; it depends on compactifications of correspondences (missing) and on strict maps of compactifications of X (missing).

items.name: Compactifications of a correspondence can be pulled back along maps of compactifications of X
items.statement: Let (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) be a compactification of (C, X, p1, p2), and let (X ↪ X̄') → (X ↪ X̄) be a map of compactifications of X. Then C̄' := C̄ ×_{X̄×X̄} (X̄' × X̄'), with its two projections p̄'1, p̄'2 to X̄', is a compactification of (C, X, p1, p2). The projections give a map (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2) → (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) compatible with X̄' → X̄.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.12 (p. 8) is planned nowhere. Its proof is the fibre product C̄ ×_{X̄×X̄} (X̄' × X̄'), which Mathlib's pullbacks provide; the verification C = C̄' ×_{X̄'×X̄'} (X × X) uses that X ↪ X̄' → X̄ is j_X.

items.name: Compactifications of a correspondence form a cofiltered category with strict maps
items.statement: The category of compactifications of (C, X, p1, p2) is cofiltered with strict maps. For two compactifications (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) and (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2), there is a compactification (C̄'', X̄'', p̄''1, p̄''2) with strict maps to both. One may take X̄'' to be the closure of X in X̄ × X̄' and C̄'' the closure of C in C̄ × C̄'.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.13 (p. 8) is planned nowhere. The proof takes closures of X in X̄ × X̄' and of C in C̄ × C̄'; strictness of the resulting maps follows from Lemma 2.1.4 because X is dense in the closure. It refines the cofilteredness of compactifications of a scheme (planned in AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons:L2) to correspondences and strict maps.

items.name: Locally principal and Cartier closed subschemes; the twists O(−D) and F(nD)
items.statement: Let X̄ be a scheme and D = V(I) a closed subscheme. D is locally principal if there are an invertible sheaf L on X̄ and a map L → O_X̄ with image I. One writes O_X̄(−D) for L; the choice of L and of the map is part of the data and need not be unique. D is Cartier (an effective Cartier divisor) if I itself is an invertible sheaf, and then O_X̄(−D) = I. For an object F on X̄ and n ∈ Z, F(nD) := F ⊗ O_X̄(−D)^{⊗(−n)}. For two locally principal D+, D−, F(n+D+ − n−D−) is defined in the same way.
items.note: Effective Cartier divisors (closed subschemes with invertible ideal) and the tensor powers and inverses of invertible sheaves needed for O(−nD) and F(nD) are planned in these Tau Ceti layers; the library audit records effective Cartier divisors as absent from both libraries (Tau Ceti's Cartier divisors are on integral schemes only). Tau Ceti has invertible sheaves (InvertibleSheaf) and the tensor product of O_X-modules, Mathlib has ideal sheaves (IdealSheafData). A locally principal subscheme in the sense of p. 8 is an invertible sheaf with a morphism to O_X̄ whose image is the ideal; this is data, not a new notion, and the paper warns that the choice is not unique. On p. 15 the twist F(nD) is applied to objects of the solid category D(O_{X̄,■}); that use needs the solid tensor product, which is missing with the solid formalism.

items.name: Set-theoretic inclusion D ⊆ D' of closed subschemes
items.statement: Let D = V(I) and D' = V(I') be closed subschemes of X̄. One writes D ⊆ D' if D is contained in D' as a subset of X̄; equivalently, I' ⊆ √I.
items.note: For D = V(I) and D' = V(I') with I, I' Mathlib ideal sheaves, D ⊆ D' in the sense of Definition 2.1.15(1) (p. 8) is I.support ≤ I'.support. Taking Z = I.support in le_support_iff_le_vanishingIdeal and rewriting with vanishingIdeal_support gives the equivalence with I' ≤ I.radical, the printed I' ⊆ √I. The scheme-theoretic inverse images p̄_i^*D used in §2.1.18 are IdealSheafData.comap, whose support is the preimage (IdealSheafData.support_comap).

items.name: The relation D ≤ sD' for s ∈ Q>0
items.statement: Let D = V(I) and D′ = V(I′) be closed subschemes of X̄, and let s ∈ Q_{>0}. One writes D ≤ sD′ if there exist integers p, q ≥ 1 with s = p/q and (I′)^p ⊆ I^q. (The text writes p, q ∈ Z_{≥0}; since s > 0, both are positive.) The condition depends on the chosen representation of s. Locally, for D = V(f) and D′ = V(f′) principal, it says that (f′)^p ∈ f^q·A, i.e. that the closed subscheme V(f^q) = qD is contained in V((f′)^p) = pD′. D ≤ D′ implies D ⊆ D′ as subsets of X̄, but it does not give a morphism D → D′ of subschemes (Remark 2.1.16).
items.note: The relation D ≤ sD' of Definition 2.1.15(2) (p. 8) is new with the paper and planned nowhere. It is a one-line condition on Mathlib ideal sheaves (powers of IdealSheafData, IdealSheafData.ideal_pow, and their order), but neither library names it or proves Remark 2.1.16. For s = p/q to lie in Q_{>0}, p and q must be positive; the page prints p, q ∈ Z_{≥0}.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.17(1): D ≤ D' for Cartier divisors gives O(−n0D') ↪ O(−n0D)
items.statement: Let D = V(I) and D′ = V(I′) be Cartier divisors on X̄ with D ≤ D′. Then there is an integer n0 ≥ 1 with (I′)^{n0} ⊆ I^{n0}, i.e. a canonical injective map O_X̄(−n0D′) → O_X̄(−n0D). Indeed D ≤ 1·D′ means (I′)^p ⊆ I^q for some p = q ≥ 1.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.17(1) (p. 8) is planned nowhere. With D ≤ D' written as (I')^{n0} ⊆ I^{n0}, the map is this inclusion of invertible ideals, O(−n0D') ⊆ O(−n0D); the inputs are effective Cartier divisors (planned in JacobianChallenge Layer C) and powers of ideal sheaves (Mathlib).

items.name: Lemma 2.1.17(2): on a normal scheme, D ≤ D' gives O(−D') ↪ O(−D)
items.statement: If X̄ is normal, D and D' are Cartier divisors, and D ≤ D', then there is a canonical injective map O_X̄(−D') → O_X̄(−D), i.e. I' ⊆ I.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.17(2) (p. 8) is planned nowhere. The local step (p. 8) is that for local equations f, f' of D, D', (f'/f)^{n0} ∈ A implies f'/f ∈ A because A is normal; Mathlib has integrally closed domains (IsIntegrallyClosed) but no normal schemes or effective Cartier divisors.

items.name: Lemma 2.1.17(3): canonical maps O(−p'D') → O(−q'D) from D ≤ sD' with s < 1
items.statement: Let X̄ be quasi-compact, and let D = V(I), D' = V(I') be locally principal closed subschemes with chosen maps O_X̄(−D) → I and O_X̄(−D') → I' onto the ideals. Suppose D ≤ sD' for some 0 < s < 1. Then for every s' with s < s' < 1 there are positive integers p', q' with s' = p'/q' and a canonical map O_X̄(−p'D') → O_X̄(−q'D). This map makes the square formed with the induced maps O_X̄(−p'D') → (I')^{p'}, O_X̄(−q'D) → I^{q'} and the inclusion (I')^{p'} ⊆ I^{q'} commute.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.17(3) (pp. 8–9) is planned nowhere. The construction is local: from (f')^p = a f^q it produces, for k large and divisible by p', maps A(f')^{k'p'} → A f^{k'q'} depending only on the chosen generators, and glues them over a finite affine cover of the quasi-compact X̄.

items.name: The Frobenius correspondence strictly contracts every closed subscheme
items.statement: Let S = Spec F_p and consider the Frobenius correspondence on X̄: C̄ = X̄, p̄1 = id, and p̄2 = F the absolute Frobenius. Every closed subscheme D = V(I) ⊆ X̄ is strictly contracted, with s = 1/p. Indeed p̄2^*D = V(I^{[p]}), where I^{[p]} ⊆ I^p is generated by the p-th powers of local sections of I, so p̄1^*D ≤ (1/p)·p̄2^*D. When D is locally principal, p̄2^*D = p·p̄1^*D.
items.note: Neither library has the absolute Frobenius of an F_p-scheme (Mathlib has only the ring endomorphism frobenius), and no atlas layer plans this example. Example 2.1.21 (p. 9) prints p̄2^*D = p·p̄1^*D 'for any closed subscheme D'. That identity holds for locally principal D. For general D = V(I) one has p̄2^*D = V(I^{[p]}) with I^{[p]} ⊆ I^p, possibly strictly (checked by direct computation: for I = (x, y) in F_p[x, y], I^{[p]} = (x^p, y^p) ≠ (x, y)^p). The conclusion, D strictly contracted with s = 1/p, holds for every D, as the statement records.

items.name: Expanded and contracted closed subschemes
items.statement: Let (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) be a correspondence and D ⊆ X̄ a closed subscheme, with scheme-theoretic inverse images p̄_i^*D ⊆ C̄. D is expanded by the correspondence if p̄2^*D ⊆ p̄1^*D, and contracted by it if p̄1^*D ⊆ p̄2^*D. Here ⊆ is the inclusion of underlying sets of Definition 2.1.15(1). These notions are set-theoretic (Remark 2.1.20).
items.note: Definition 2.1.19(1),(4) (p. 9) is new with the paper and planned nowhere. It is expressible with Mathlib's scheme-theoretic inverse images of ideal sheaves (IdealSheafData.comap) and their supports (IdealSheafData.support, with support_comap giving the preimage).

items.name: Strictly expanded and strictly contracted closed subschemes
items.statement: In the setting of Definition 2.1.19, D is strictly expanded if p̄2^*D ≤ s·p̄1^*D for some 0 < s < 1. It is strictly contracted if p̄1^*D ≤ s·p̄2^*D for some 0 < s < 1. Both use the relation of Definition 2.1.15(2), and these notions are scheme-theoretic (Remark 2.1.20).
items.note: Definition 2.1.19(2),(5) (p. 9) is new with the paper and planned nowhere; it uses the relation D ≤ sD' of Definition 2.1.15(2) (missing) on the ideal sheaves p̄_i^*D (Mathlib's IdealSheafData.comap).

items.name: Compactly expanded and compactly contracted closed subschemes
items.statement: For a subset T of a topological space V, T° denotes the interior of T in V. In the setting of Definition 2.1.19, D is compactly expanded if p̄2^*D ⊆ (p̄1^*D)°, and compactly contracted if p̄1^*D ⊆ (p̄2^*D)°, with interiors taken in C̄. These notions are topological (Remark 2.1.20).
items.note: Definition 2.1.19(3),(6) and footnote 1 (p. 9) are new with the paper and planned nowhere. The interior is Mathlib's interior, and the sets p̄_i^*D are supports of IdealSheafData.comap.

items.name: Compact expansion in terms of closures
items.statement: If D is compactly expanded by (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2), then the closure of C̄ \ p̄1^*D in C̄ is contained in C̄ \ p̄2^*D.
items.note: Remark 2.1.22 (p. 9) is the topological fact that A ⊆ interior(B) implies closure(Bᶜ) = (interior B)ᶜ ⊆ Aᶜ, applied in C̄ to A = p̄2^*D and B = p̄1^*D; Mathlib's closure_compl gives the equality and the inclusion is complementation. The notion of a compactly expanded subscheme itself is recorded separately and is missing.

items.name: Dynamic correspondence
items.statement: A dynamic correspondence is a tuple (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) with the following properties: (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) is a correspondence with p̄1 and p̄2 proper; D+ and D− are closed subschemes of X̄; D+ is expanded by C̄ (p̄2^*D+ ⊆ p̄1^*D+); and D− is contracted by C̄ (p̄1^*D− ⊆ p̄2^*D−).
items.note: Definition 2.1.24(1) (p. 9) is new with the paper and planned nowhere. Pilloni (2020) has no analogue: there the Hecke operators act on cohomology of open loci (the p-rank ≥ 1 locus) rather than on cohomology with partial support. The ingredients (proper morphisms, closed subschemes and their inverse images) are in Mathlib.

items.name: Strict dynamic correspondence
items.statement: A strict dynamic correspondence is a dynamic correspondence (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) in which D+ is strictly expanded and D− is strictly contracted.
items.note: Definition 2.1.24(2) (p. 9) is new with the paper and planned nowhere; it rests on strict expansion and contraction (missing).

items.name: Compact dynamic correspondence
items.statement: A compact dynamic correspondence is a dynamic correspondence (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) in which D+ is compactly expanded and D− is compactly contracted.
items.note: Definition 2.1.24(3) (p. 9) is new with the paper and planned nowhere; it rests on compact expansion and contraction (missing). It is the input for the finite rank operators of §2.10.

items.name: Dynamic (strict dynamic, compact dynamic) compactification of a correspondence
items.statement: Let (C, X, p1, p2) be a correspondence. A dynamic compactification of (C, X, p1, p2) is a dynamic correspondence (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) such that (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) is a compactification of (C, X, p1, p2) and X̄ \ X = D− ∪ D+. It is a strict (resp. compact) dynamic compactification if it is a strict (resp. compact) dynamic correspondence. D+ and D− are not required to be disjoint (Remark 2.1.27).
items.note: Definition 2.1.26 and Remark 2.1.27 (p. 10) are new with the paper and planned nowhere. For Shimura varieties the relevant compactifications are the toroidal ones (ShimuraCompactifications C2–C3), but no layer plans the boundary decomposition X̄ \ X = D− ∪ D+ with the dynamic conditions.

items.name: Non-strict and strict maps of dynamic compactifications
items.statement: A (non-strict) map ξ : (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2, D'+, D'−) → (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) of dynamic compactifications of (C, X, p1, p2) is a map ξ : (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2) → (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) of compactifications such that D'+ ⊇ ξ^*D+ and D'− ⊇ ξ^*D− for the map ξ : X̄' → X̄. It is strict if D'+ = ξ^*D+ and D'− = ξ^*D−.
items.note: Definition 2.1.28 (p. 10) is new with the paper and planned nowhere; ξ^*D± are Mathlib's IdealSheafData.comap.

items.name: Dynamic structures pull back along strict maps of compactifications
items.statement: Let (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) be a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification of (C, X, p1, p2). Let (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2) be a compactification of (C, X, p1, p2), and ξ : (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2) → (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) a strict map of compactifications. Then (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2, ξ^*D+, ξ^*D−) is a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification, and ξ is a strict map of dynamic compactifications.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.29 (p. 10) is planned nowhere. Its proof uses ξ^*(D+ ∪ D−) = X̄' \ X, which is strictness, together with the stability of the three dynamic conditions under pullback.

items.name: Refinement to Cartier D+, D− with Cartier pullbacks
items.statement: Let 𝒞 = (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) be a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification. There are a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification 𝒞' = (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2, D'+, D'−) and a strict map 𝒞' → 𝒞 with the following properties: D'+ and D'− are Cartier divisors on X̄', and (p̄'_i)^*D'+, (p̄'_i)^*D'− (i = 1, 2) are Cartier divisors on C̄'.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.30 (p. 10) is planned nowhere. The proof blows up X̄ along V(IJ) and then the fibre product C̄'' along the four pulled-back subschemes; the blow-up inputs are planned in StableReduction Layer 4 (see the blow-up item).

items.name: Unions of two dynamic structures on the same compactification
items.statement: Let (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2) be a compactification of (C, X, p1, p2). Suppose that (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+ = V(I), D− = V(J)) and (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D'+ = V(I'), D'− = V(J')) are both dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactifications. Then (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D'+ ∪ D+ = V(II'), D'− ∪ D− = V(JJ')) is a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.31 (p. 10, proof 'Obvious') is planned nowhere. The identity V(II') = V(I) ∪ V(I') is Mathlib's IdealSheafData.support_mul; the strict case needs the product rule for the relation ≤ s under products of ideals.

items.name: Dynamic compactifications form a cofiltered category
items.statement: The category of dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactifications of (C, X, p1, p2), with non-strict maps, is cofiltered. For any two such compactifications (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) and (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2, D'+, D'−), there is a third (C̄'', X̄'', p̄''1, p̄''2, D''+, D''−) of the same kind with maps to both.
items.note: Lemma 2.1.32 (p. 10) is planned nowhere; it combines Lemmas 2.1.13, 2.1.29 and 2.1.31.

items.name: Permanence of dynamic compactifiability under proper maps of correspondences
items.statement: Let (C, X, p1, p2) and (C', X', p'1, p'2) be correspondences with morphisms C' → C and X' → X such that p_i ∘ (C' → C) = (X' → X) ∘ p'_i for i = 1, 2. Assume C' → C and X' → X are proper. If (C, X, p1, p2) admits a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−), then so does (C', X', p'1, p'2).
items.note: Lemma 2.1.34 (p. 11) is planned nowhere. The proof takes closures of X' and C' in products with X̄ and C̄ and pulls back D± along r : X̄' → X̄; the key step is that X' → X̄' ×_X̄ X is both an open immersion and proper, hence an isomorphism.

items.name: Dynamic structures can be checked on the reduced compactification
items.statement: Let (C, X, p1, p2) be a correspondence with a compactification (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2); then (C̄^red, X̄^red, p̄1^red, p̄2^red) is a compactification of (C^red, X^red, p1^red, p2^red). Suppose closed subschemes D+^red, D−^red of X̄^red make (C̄^red, X̄^red, p̄1^red, p̄2^red, D+^red, D−^red) a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification. Then (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+^red, D−^red), with D±^red viewed as closed subschemes of X̄, is a dynamic (resp. strict dynamic, resp. compact dynamic) compactification of (C, X, p1, p2).
items.note: Lemma 2.1.35 (pp. 11–12) is planned nowhere. The strict case is the substantive one: generators of the ideals over the reduced scheme are lifted, the nilradical of each affine V ⊆ C̄ has some power r with (√0_V)^r = 0, and pl < q(l − r) for l large gives the inequality over C̄; quasi-compactness of C̄ finishes. Mathlib has reduced schemes (IsReduced) and nilradicals.

items.name: Solid quasi-coherent sheaves and their six-functor formalism
items.statement: For every scheme X of finite type over Z there is a triangulated (stable) category D(O_{X,■}) of solid O_X-modules. It carries a six-functor formalism (f^*, f_*, f_!, f^!, ⊗, internal Hom) for morphisms of such schemes, with j^! = j^* for open immersions j and f_! = f_* for proper f. Locally, for X = Spec A, it is the derived category of solid modules over the analytic ring (A, A)■. The usual derived category D(O_X) of quasi-coherent O_X-modules embeds fully faithfully in D(O_{X,■}), and its image is by definition the full subcategory of discrete objects.
items.locator: §2.2, p. 12; proof of Lemma 2.2.8, p. 14; proof of Proposition 2.3.2, p. 15; proof of Proposition 2.3.13, p. 17
items.note: Mathlib has only the solid predicate on condensed modules (CondensedMod.IsSolid, a naive definition over an arbitrary ring), with no derived category of solid modules, no analytic rings and no six functors for schemes. No atlas layer plans solid quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes: VStackSheavesAndLisseCategories:VS2 ('Condensed and solid foundations') plans solid coefficient categories on small v-stacks, a different theory. The draft roadmap AnalyticStacks, not yet in the atlas, plans exactly this formalism in AnalyticStacks:AS.3: 'Solid quasi-coherent sheaves (Scholze Lecture IX). Theorem 9.7: the formalism X ↦ D_■(X) on derived schemes almost of finite type over Z, with P proper maps, I open immersions and E separated maps', built on the draft roadmap SolidAnalyticRings. Classical schemes of finite type over Z are among the derived schemes it covers. The paper cites the earlier account of Clausen–Scholze ([CSb], Theorem 9.8 and Lecture XI, p. 12). External input: D. Clausen and P. Scholze, Lectures on condensed mathematics, course notes [CSb], Theorem 9.8 and Lecture XI.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.2(1),(2): base change maps for pullback
items.statement: Consider a cartesian square with open immersions j_C : C → C̄, j_X : X → X̄, a morphism p̄ : C̄ → X̄ and its restriction p : C → X, and let F ∈ D(O_{X,■}). (1) There is a natural map p̄^*(j_X)_*F → (j_C)_*p^*F. Under adjunction it corresponds to the identity of p^*F, using j_C^*p̄^* = p^*j_X^* and j_X^*(j_X)_* = id. (2) There is a natural isomorphism p̄^*(j_X)_!F ≅ (j_C)_!p^*F; this is base change, as C̄ and X are tor-independent over X̄.
items.note: Lemma 2.2.2(1),(2) (p. 12) is formal once the solid formalism exists: (1) is the mate of j_C^*p̄^* = p^*j_X^* under the adjunctions j^* ⊣ j_*, and (2) is the base change isomorphism. The abstract mates are planned in EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E3 ('Supply mates, Beck–Chevalley transformations, and identity/composition/pasting coherence for adjunctions'), but the functors are those of the solid formalism, which is missing (planned only in the draft roadmap AnalyticStacks, AS.3).

items.name: Lemma 2.2.2(3),(4): base change maps for upper shriek
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 2.2.2: (3) there is a natural map (j_C)_!p^!F → p̄^!(j_X)_!F; (4) there is a natural isomorphism (j_C)_*p^!F ≅ p̄^!(j_X)_*F.
items.note: Lemma 2.2.2(3),(4) (p. 12; 'the other points are similar') is formal in the solid formalism. Passing to left adjoints, the isomorphism (4) (j_C)_*p^! ≅ p̄^!(j_X)_* is equivalent to j_X^*p̄_! ≅ p_!j_C^*, the base change of p̄_! along the open immersion j_X (checked by direct computation of the adjoints). The solid formalism is missing (planned only in the draft roadmap AnalyticStacks, AS.3).

items.name: Cohomology with partial support RΓ_{D+,D−} and RΓ_{D−,D+}
items.statement: Let X̄ be an S-scheme, D+ and D− closed subschemes, D = D+ ∪ D−, and X = X̄ \ D. Consider the open immersions X →(j−) X̄ \ D+ →(j+) X̄ and X →(i+) X̄ \ D− →(i−) X̄. For F ∈ D(O_{X,■}) define RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) := RΓ(X̄, (j+)_*(j−)_!F) and RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F) := RΓ(X̄, (i−)_!(i+)_*F). Convention (Remark 2.2.5): let X ⊆ X' ⊆ X̄ be an intermediate open, j : X → X', and F ∈ D(O_{X',■}). Then RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) means RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, j^*F), and likewise for RΓ_{D−,D+}.
items.note: Definition 2.2.4 and Remark 2.2.5 (p. 12) are new with the paper and planned nowhere. Cohomology with support in the étale theory (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.0, 'Construct cohomology with support as the localization fiber') concerns a single closed subset of an étale site, not this mixed coherent notion with compact support towards D− and none towards D+. Pilloni (2020) used instead cohomology of the p-rank ≥ 1 locus and its formal completion; this definition is what replaces that device for GSp_{2g}.

items.name: Change-of-support maps
items.statement: Let X̄ be an S-scheme and D+, D−, D'+, D'− closed subschemes of X̄ with D'− ⊆ D− and D+ ⊆ D'+. For F ∈ D(O_{X̄ \ (D'− ∪ D+),■}) there are natural maps RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D'+,D'−}(X̄, F) and RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D'−,D'+}(X̄, F). Both sides are understood via the convention of Remark 2.2.5.
items.note: Lemma-construction 2.2.6 (pp. 12–13) is planned nowhere. The proof reduces to the cases D'− = D− or D'+ = D+ and uses flat base change for open immersions and the unit and counit of j^* ⊣ j_* and j_! ⊣ j^* in the solid formalism (missing).

items.name: Pullback maps on cohomology with partial support
items.statement: Let p̄ : C̄ → X̄ be a morphism and D+, D− ⊆ X̄ closed subschemes. Put X = X̄ \ (D+ ∪ D−) and C = C̄ \ p̄^*(D+ ∪ D−), and let p : C → X be the induced morphism. For F ∈ D(O_{X,■}) there are canonical pullback maps RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{p̄^*D+,p̄^*D−}(C̄, p^*F) and RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{p̄^*D−,p̄^*D+}(C̄, p^*F).
items.note: Lemma 2.2.7, pullback part (p. 13), is planned nowhere; it is deduced from Lemma 2.2.2(1),(2) (missing with the solid formalism).

items.name: Trace maps on cohomology with partial support for proper maps
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 2.2.7, if p̄ is proper, there are canonical trace maps RΓ_{p̄^*D+,p̄^*D−}(C̄, p^!F) → RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) and RΓ_{p̄^*D−,p̄^*D+}(C̄, p^!F) → RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F).
items.note: Lemma 2.2.7, trace part (p. 13), is planned nowhere. It uses Lemma 2.2.2(4) and, for proper p̄, p̄_! = p̄_* and the counit p̄_!p̄^! → id of the solid formalism (missing). The coherent trace of Grothendieck duality that PAPER-PILLONI-20 routes to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension is the discrete analogue.

items.name: Pullback and trace are quasi-isomorphisms when p is an isomorphism and p̄ is proper
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 2.2.7, assume that p : C → X is an isomorphism and that p̄ is proper. Then the two pullback maps and the two trace maps of Lemma 2.2.7 are quasi-isomorphisms.
items.note: Lemma 2.2.8 (p. 14) is planned nowhere. The proof given (for the first map) uses that the restriction p' of p̄ over X̄ \ D+ is proper, so p'_* = p'_!, and base change; the other three cases are left to the reader in the paper.

items.name: Cohomological correspondence
items.statement: Let (C, X, p1, p2) be a correspondence and F ∈ D(O_{X,■}). A cohomological correspondence on F is a map T : p2^*F → p1^!F in D(O_{C,■}). From §2.3.12 on, F is a coherent sheaf on X.
items.note: Neither library has upper-shriek functors, so maps p2^*F → p1^!F cannot be stated. This generalises Pilloni (2020), Remark 4.3.2 (the adjoint form p2^*F → p1^!G of a coherent cohomological correspondence, which PAPER-PILLONI-20 records as missing and routes to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, layer 3) from coherent sheaves with Hartshorne's p1^! to objects of D(O_{X,■}) with the solid p1^!. From §2.3.12 (p. 17) on, F is coherent, and the two notions must be identified there. The solid version is needed for the Λ-adic sheaves of the families, so it belongs with the higher Hida formalism, which states the comparison with the coherent version.

items.name: The endomorphism T_𝒞 induced by a cohomological correspondence on a dynamic correspondence
items.statement: Let 𝒞 = (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) be a dynamic correspondence, X = X̄ \ (D+ ∪ D−), C = C̄ ×_{X̄×X̄} (X × X) with p_i = p̄_i|_C, F ∈ D(O_{X,■}), and T : p2^*F → p1^!F a map in D(O_{C,■}). Then T induces an endomorphism T_𝒞 of RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F), defined as the composite RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{p̄2^*D+,p̄2^*D−}(C̄, p2^*F) → RΓ_{p̄1^*D+,p̄2^*D−}(C̄, p2^*F) → RΓ_{p̄1^*D+,p̄2^*D−}(C̄, p1^!F) → RΓ_{p̄1^*D+,p̄1^*D−}(C̄, p1^!F) → RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F). The first map is pullback along p̄2 and the last is the trace along the proper map p̄1 (Lemma 2.2.7). The second and fourth are change-of-support maps (Lemma 2.2.6), available because p̄2^*D+ ⊆ p̄1^*D+ and p̄1^*D− ⊆ p̄2^*D−. The middle map is RΓ(C̄, (j_{C,+})_*(j_{C,−})_!T) for C →(j_{C,−}) C̄ \ p̄1^*D+ →(j_{C,+}) C̄. Likewise T induces an endomorphism T_𝒞 of RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F), the composite RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{p̄2^*D−,p̄2^*D+}(C̄, p2^*F) → RΓ_{p̄2^*D−,p̄1^*D+}(C̄, p2^*F) → RΓ_{p̄2^*D−,p̄1^*D+}(C̄, p1^!F) → RΓ_{p̄1^*D−,p̄1^*D+}(C̄, p1^!F) → RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F). In the second and fifth terms of each chain, p2^*F and p1^!F denote the pullback along p̄2^{-1}(X) → X and the upper shriek along p̄1^{-1}(X) → X, as in Lemma 2.2.7; on C they restrict to p2^*F and p1^!F.
items.note: Proposition 2.2.10 (p. 14) is planned nowhere. It generalises the action of a cohomological correspondence on RΓ(X, F) in Pilloni (2020), Definition 4.3.1(2) (missing, routed by PAPER-PILLONI-20 to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes), to cohomology with partial support; the expanding and contracting conditions on D+ and D− are exactly what the two change-of-support steps need. In the second chain the printed diagram writes C and X where C̄ and X̄ are meant.

items.name: T_𝒞 is invariant under strict maps of dynamic compactifications
items.statement: Let (C, X, p1, p2) be a correspondence with a cohomological correspondence T : p2^*F → p1^!F. Let 𝒞 = (C̄, X̄, p̄1, p̄2, D+, D−) → 𝒞' = (C̄', X̄', p̄'1, p̄'2, D'+, D'−) be a strict map of dynamic compactifications of (C, X, p1, p2). Then the canonical quasi-isomorphisms of Lemma 2.2.8, RΓ_{D+,D−}(X̄, F) ≅ RΓ_{D'+,D'−}(X̄', F) and RΓ_{D−,D+}(X̄, F) ≅ RΓ_{D'−,D'+}(X̄', F), are equivariant for T_𝒞 and T_𝒞'. Thus T_𝒞 depends on 𝒞 only up to strict maps.
items.note: Proposition 2.2.11 (p. 15) is planned nowhere. It is the general form of Pilloni (2020), Proposition 7.2.1 (independence of T1, T2 from the toroidal compactification; missing, routed by PAPER-PILLONI-20 to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory), for arbitrary strict maps of dynamic compactifications. The proof is a commutative diagram built from Lemmas 2.2.6–2.2.8.

items.name: The inverse system of twists F̄(−nD) and its derived limit
items.statement: Let j : X → X̄ be an open immersion with locally principal complement D: there are an invertible sheaf O_X̄(−D) and a map O_X̄(−D) → O_X̄ whose image I defines D. For F ∈ D(O_{X,■}), choose F̄ ∈ D(O_{X̄,■}) with j^*F̄ = F, and set F̄(−nD) := F̄ ⊗_{O_X̄} O_X̄(−D)^{⊗n} for n ≥ 0 (and similarly F̄(nD)). The maps F̄(−(n+1)D) → F̄(−nD) induced by O_X̄(−D) → O_X̄ form an inverse system. Its derived limit lim_n F̄(−nD) is the fibre of the map ∏_n F̄(−nD) → ∏_n F̄(−nD), (m_n)_n ↦ (m_n − m_{n+1})_n, where m_{n+1} is sent to the n-th factor by the transition map.
items.note: The construction of §2.3.1 (p. 15) is planned nowhere as stated. Twisting by the invertible sheaf O(−D) is planned with JacobianChallenge Layer A for O_X-modules, but here F̄ lies in the solid category D(O_{X̄,■}), which is missing. The derived limit of a sequential inverse system, as the fibre of 1 − shift on products, is standard in a stable category with products; neither library has sequential homotopy limits in derived categories, and EnhancedDerivedSheaves:E2 plans them only for Postnikov towers ('Construct truncation and Postnikov towers, their enhanced inverse limits').

items.name: !-pushforward along the affine line in solid modules
items.statement: For a ring A (of finite type over Z), the !-pushforward of solid modules along Spec A[X] → Spec A sends M to M ⊗_{(A[X],A)■} (A((X^{-1}))/A[X]), placed in cohomological degree 1 (shift [−1]). Composing with the closed immersion Spec A[1/f] = Spec A[X]/(Xf − 1) ↪ Spec A[X] computes j_! for the open immersion j : Spec A[1/f] → Spec A.
items.note: Neither library has it. The draft roadmap AnalyticStacks (not yet in the atlas) plans it in AnalyticStacks:AS.3: 'The key computation: for A^1_Z → Spec Z, f_!1 = fib(Z[T] → Z((T^{-1}))) = T^{-1}Z[[T^{-1}]][−1], with trace given by the coefficient of T^{-1}.' That fibre is (Z((T^{-1}))/Z[T])[−1], the formula used on p. 15 after base change to A. The proof of Proposition 2.3.2 cites [CSb], Lecture VIII. External input: D. Clausen and P. Scholze, Lectures on condensed mathematics [CSb], Lecture VIII (cited as the definition of j_! in the proof of Proposition 2.3.2).

items.name: j_! as the derived limit of the twists F̄(−nD)
items.statement: In the setting of §2.3.1 (D = X̄ \ X locally principal, F̄ ∈ D(O_{X̄,■}) with j^*F̄ = F), assume F̄ is pseudo-coherent. Then there is a canonical isomorphism j_!F ≅ lim_n F̄(−nD) in D(O_{X̄,■}). The map j_!F → lim_n F̄(−nD) is adjoint to the identity F → j^* lim_n F̄(−nD) = lim_n j^*F̄(−nD) = F.
items.note: Proposition 2.3.2 (pp. 15–16) is planned nowhere. The local computation reduces to Spec A[1/f] → Spec A[X] → Spec A, the solid j_! of the affine line (missing), and the identity M ⊗ A[[X^{-1}]]X^{-1} = ∏_{n≥1} M X^{-n} for pseudo-coherent M. It is the solid replacement for Hartshorne's definition of compactly supported coherent cohomology (Proposition 2.3.5).

items.name: Cohomology of j_!F as a limit of cohomology of twists
items.statement: Under the assumptions of Proposition 2.3.2, RΓ(X̄, j_!F) ≅ lim_n RΓ(X̄, F̄ ⊗_{O_X̄} O_X̄(−nD)). By Remark 2.3.3 this applies whenever F is a coherent sheaf on X: F extends to a coherent sheaf F̄ on X̄, which is pseudo-coherent.
items.note: Corollary 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.3 (p. 16) are planned nowhere; the proof uses only that RΓ, a right adjoint, commutes with limits, applied to Proposition 2.3.2.

items.name: Comparison with Hartshorne's cohomology with compact support over an artinian base
