For Y = Spec R and Z = Spec R/J the map is RHom_R(R/J, M) → RHom_{R_□}(R̂^I, M), induced by the surjection R̂^I → R/J. No layer states it.

items.name: Lemma 2.10.1(2): excision for cohomology with support
items.statement: If Z ⊆ Y′ ↪(j) Y with Y′ open in Y, then RΓ_Z(Y, F) = RΓ_Z(Y′, j^⋆F) and RΓ_Ẑ(Y, F) = RΓ_Ẑ(Y′, j^⋆F).
items.note: Missing. It follows formally from j^⋆ = j^! for open immersions and from base change of i^! (resp. î^!) along an open neighbourhood of Z. Both are part of the planned formalism: AnalyticStacks AS.0 for base change, AS.3 for schemes and SolidAnalyticRings SA.2 for the locale. No layer states excision for coherent or solid cohomology with supports; the étale analogue belongs to EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.0.

items.name: Lemma 2.10.1(3): change-of-support maps through RΓ_Z and RΓ_Ẑ
items.statement:
Let j_U : U ↪ Y and j_{U′} : U′ ↪ Y be open subschemes with U ⊆ Z ⊆ U′ ⊆ Y. U must be an open subscheme of the closed subscheme Z, not only a subset [sourceIssues E43]. Then there are natural maps
RΓ(Y, (j_U)_!j_U^⋆F) → RΓ_Z(Y, F) → RΓ_Ẑ(Y, F) → RΓ(Y, (j_{U′})_!j_{U′}^⋆F).
They come from the standard adjunctions and Lemma 2.10.1(1).
items.note:
Missing. The maps are formal from planned adjunctions.
- The first map: write j_U = i ∘ k with k : U ↪ Z open. Then (j_U)_!j_U^⋆ = i_⋆k_!k^⋆i^!, and the counit k_!k^⋆ → Id gives the map. This is why U must be an open subscheme of Z.
- The middle map is the map from RΓ_Z to RΓ_Ẑ.
- The last map: î_⋆î^!F is supported in U′, because the idempotent algebras of Ẑ and of Y ∖ U′ have zero tensor product. So it equals (j_{U′})_!j_{U′}^⋆î_⋆î^!F, which maps to (j_{U′})_!j_{U′}^⋆F by the counit.
The identities used are Rodríguez Camargo's Proposition 5.1.2 and Remark 5.1.5, in SolidAnalyticRings SA.2. No layer states the chain.

items.name: Lemma 2.10.1(4): finiteness of RΓ_Z for proper Z
items.statement: Let A be noetherian and Y → Spec A as in §2.10. If Z is proper over Spec A and F is bounded below with coherent cohomology sheaves, then RΓ_Z(Y, F) has finitely generated cohomology groups (as A-modules).
items.note:
Missing. It has two inputs.
- Coherence of i^!F = RHom(𝒪_Z, F) for a closed immersion of noetherian schemes and F bounded below with coherent cohomology. This is classical, but no layer states it for solid sheaves.
- Finiteness of coherent cohomology for proper Z over Spec A. This is planned (AnalyticStacks AS.1 and AS.3, Scholze's Theorem 8.10 = 9.18).
The boundedness hypothesis is necessary. Take A = k, Y = Spec k[ε]/(ε²), Z = Spec k and F = ⊕_{m≥0} k[m]. Then H^0(RΓ_Z(Y, F)) contains ⊕_{m≥0} Ext^m(k, k), which is infinite-dimensional (checked by direct computation). The lemma itself is not stated in any layer.

items.name: Finiteness of coherent cohomology on proper schemes
items.statement: Let A be a noetherian ring, Z a proper A-scheme and G a coherent 𝒪_Z-module. Then H^n(Z, G) is a finitely generated A-module for every n. Consequently H^n(Z, G^•) is finitely generated for every G^• ∈ D^+(𝒪_Z) with coherent cohomology sheaves: Z has finite cohomological dimension, so only finitely many cohomology sheaves contribute to each degree.
items.note: Planned. AnalyticStacks AS.1 states Theorem 8.10 of Scholze's Six-Functor Formalisms (arXiv:2510.26269v2), and AS.3 proves it as Theorem 9.18: 'Let f : X → Y be a proper map of derived schemes. Then f_* takes pseudo-coherent objects of D_qc(X) to pseudocoherent objects of D_qc(Y), and coherent objects to coherent objects.' Scholze adds that it 'can also be deduced from the usual finiteness results in coherent cohomology'. For Y = Spec A with A noetherian, and Z proper (hence of finite presentation) over A, coherent objects have finitely generated cohomology. The case of G ∈ D^+ with coherent cohomology sheaves reduces to bounded complexes, since H^n(Z, G) = H^n(Z, τ^{≤n+1}G). Tau Ceti's JacobianChallenge layer C plans 'Proper-flat-finitely-presented pushforward of coherent sheaves', which covers only flat morphisms. External input: Grothendieck, EGA III₁, Théorème 3.2.1 (coherence of higher direct images under proper morphisms). The paper invokes 'the finiteness of the cohomology of proper schemes' without a reference.

items.name: Lemma 2.10.2: change of support factors through cohomology with proper support
items.statement:
Let X̄ be a scheme (of finite type over Z) and let D₊, D₋, D′₊, D′₋ be closed subschemes with
(1) D₊ ⊆ (D′₊)° ⊆ D′₊,
(2) D′₋ ⊆ (D₋)° ⊆ D₋,
where (−)° is the interior in X̄. Recall (Definition 2.2.4) RΓ_{A₊,A₋}(X̄, F) = RΓ(X̄, (j₊)_⋆(j₋)_!F) for X̄ ∖ (A₊ ∪ A₋) ↪ X̄ ∖ A₊ ↪ X̄, and RΓ_{A₋,A₊}(X̄, F) = RΓ(X̄, (i₋)_!(i₊)_⋆F) for X̄ ∖ (A₊ ∪ A₋) ↪ X̄ ∖ A₋ ↪ X̄.
Let F ∈ D(𝒪_{X̄,■}). Let Y = X̄ ∖ (D′₊)°. This is a closed subset of X̄, the closure of X̄ ∖ D′₊, and is treated as a closed subscheme. Let Z = X̄ ∖ ((D′₊)° ∪ (D₋)°) ⊆ Y, a closed subset. There are natural maps
RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_Z(Y, F) → RΓ_{D′₊,D′₋}(X̄, F),
RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F) → RΓ_Z(Y, F) → RΓ_{D′₋,D′₊}(X̄, F).
The middle term is printed as RΓ_{X̄∖(D′₊°∪D₋°)}(X̄ ∖ D′₊°, F). The maps are composites of three steps.
(a) Restriction to Y (Lemma 2.2.7 for Y → X̄; D₊ ∩ Y = ∅) gives RΓ_{∅,D₋}(Y, F) = RΓ_{D₋,∅}(Y, F).
(b) The maps of Lemma 2.10.1(3) for U = Y ∖ D₋ ⊆ Z ⊆ U′ = Y ∖ D′₋ give RΓ_{∅,D′₋}(Y, F), resp. RΓ_{D′₋,∅}(Y, F).
(c) The change of support of Lemma 2.2.6 on Y, from (∅, D′₋) to (D′₊ ∩ Y, D′₋ ∩ Y). Its target is RΓ_{D′₊,D′₋}(X̄, F), resp. RΓ_{D′₋,D′₊}(X̄, F), once Y carries the scheme structure of the scheme-theoretic closure of X̄ ∖ D′₊.
items.note: Missing. It combines Lemma 2.10.1(3) with the pullback and change-of-support maps of Lemmas 2.2.6–2.2.7. Those lemmas concern the mixed-support cohomologies RΓ_{A₊,A₋} of Definition 2.2.4. No layer plans cohomology with partial supports along the boundary divisors D₊ and D₋ of a dynamic compactification, or these comparison maps.

items.name: Proposition 2.10.3: compact dynamic correspondences act by finite rank operators
items.statement:
Let S = Spec A with A noetherian. Let (C, X, p₁, p₂) be a correspondence and 𝒞 = (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D₊, D₋) a compact dynamic compactification (Definitions 2.1.19, 2.1.24, 2.1.26), so that p̄₂^⋆D₊ ⊆ (p̄₁^⋆D₊)° and p̄₁^⋆D₋ ⊆ (p̄₂^⋆D₋)°. Let F ∈ D(𝒪_{X,■}) and T : p₂^⋆F → p₁^!F a map in D(𝒪_{C,■}). Put Z_𝒞 = C̄ ∖ ((p̄₁^⋆D₊)° ∪ (p̄₂^⋆D₋)°), a closed subset of C̄. Assume:
- F has coherent cohomology sheaves;
- T extends to a map over an open neighbourhood V of Z_𝒞 in C̄, for an extension of F near p̄₁(V) ∪ p̄₂(V);
- (needed for the finiteness step as the paper argues it, since Lemma 2.10.1(4) requires a bounded below complex; the paper omits it [sourceIssues E45]) the pullback of this extension by p̄₂ is bounded below on V, e.g. F is bounded and p̄₂ is flat there.
Then the endomorphisms T_𝒞 of RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F) and of RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F) (Proposition 2.2.10) have finite rank (Definition 2.4.5), i.e. each factors through a complex whose cohomology groups are finite A-modules. Precisely, the map RΓ_{p̄₂^⋆D₋,p̄₂^⋆D₊}(C̄, p₂^⋆F) → RΓ_{p̄₁^⋆D₋,p̄₁^⋆D₊}(C̄, p₁^!F), and its analogue with the supports in the order (+, −), factors as
RΓ_{Z_𝒞}(C̄ ∖ (p̄₁^⋆D₊)°, p₂^⋆F) → RΓ_{Z_𝒞}(C̄ ∖ (p̄₁^⋆D₊)°, p₁^!F),
where the first term has finitely generated cohomology.

items.name: Proposition 2.10.4(1): nested supports give compact dynamic correspondences
items.statement: Let (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D₊, D₋) and (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D′₊, D′₋) be two dynamic correspondences (Definition 2.1.24) on the same (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂). Assume D₊ ⊆ (D′₊)° ⊆ D′₊, D₋ ⊆ (D′₋)° ⊆ D′₋, p̄₂^⋆D′₊ ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D₊ and p̄₁^⋆D′₋ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆D₋ (set-theoretically). Then the correspondences (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D₊, D₋), (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D₊, D′₋), (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D′₊, D₋) and (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D′₊, D′₋) are compact dynamic.
items.note: Missing. It is a statement about dynamic and compact dynamic correspondences (Definitions 2.1.24 and 2.1.26), which no layer plans. For example, p̄₂^⋆D₊ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆(D′₊)° ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D₊ gives the compactness condition for (D₊, D₋), as the paper notes on p. 31.

items.name: Proposition 2.10.4(2): the maps T between cohomologies with mixed supports
items.statement:
In the situation of Proposition 2.10.4(1), let C = C̄ ∖ (p̄₁^⋆D₊ ∪ p̄₂^⋆D₋) and p_i = p̄_i|_C. These map C into X = X̄ ∖ (D₊ ∪ D₋). Let F ∈ D(𝒪_{X,■}) and T : p₂^⋆F → p₁^!F a map. There are canonical maps
T : RΓ_{D′₊,D₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D₊,D′₋}(X̄, F),
T : RΓ_{D₋,D′₊}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D′₋,D₊}(X̄, F).
The first is the composite RΓ_{D′₊,D₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{p̄₂^⋆D′₊,p̄₂^⋆D₋}(C̄, p₂^⋆F) → RΓ_{p̄₁^⋆D₊,p̄₁^⋆D′₋}(C̄, p₁^!F) → RΓ_{D₊,D′₋}(X̄, F). Its pieces are:
- pullback along p̄₂ (Lemma 2.2.7);
- the change of support of Lemma 2.2.6 on C̄, allowed by p̄₂^⋆D′₊ ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D₊ and p̄₁^⋆D′₋ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆D₋, combined with T on C;
- the trace along p̄₁ (Lemma 2.2.7).
The second map is built the same way.
items.note: Missing. The construction composes three maps. The first is the pullback along p̄₂ (Lemma 2.2.7). The second is the change of support of Lemma 2.2.6 on C̄, combined with T. The third is the trace along p̄₁ (Lemma 2.2.7). No layer plans mixed-support cohomology or these maps. The underlying six-functor operations and base change are planned in AnalyticStacks AS.0 and AS.3.

items.name: Proposition 2.10.4(3): T_𝒞 on the four supports factors through the maps T
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 2.10.4(1)–(2), there are commutative diagrams (squares with a diagonal). The horizontal maps RΓ_{D₊,D′₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F) and RΓ_{D′₊,D′₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D′₊,D₋}(X̄, F), and the vertical maps RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D′₊,D₋}(X̄, F) and RΓ_{D₊,D′₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D′₊,D′₋}(X̄, F), are the change-of-support maps of Lemma 2.2.6. The diagonal is T : RΓ_{D′₊,D₋}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D₊,D′₋}(X̄, F). Going around the diagram once yields, on each of the four complexes, the endomorphism T_𝒞 of Proposition 2.2.10 for the corresponding compact dynamic correspondence. The same holds for RΓ_{D₋,D₊}, RΓ_{D′₋,D₊}, RΓ_{D₋,D′₊}, RΓ_{D′₋,D′₊}, with diagonal T : RΓ_{D₋,D′₊}(X̄, F) → RΓ_{D′₋,D₊}(X̄, F).
items.note: Missing. The paper calls it 'an exercise in bookkeeping' with the change-of-support, pullback and trace maps of Lemmas 2.2.6–2.2.7 and the operators T_𝒞 of Proposition 2.2.10, all from §2.2. None of these is planned.

items.name: Proposition 2.10.4(4): on ordinary parts all change-of-support maps are quasi-isomorphisms
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 2.10.4(3), all maps in these diagrams become quasi-isomorphisms after taking ordinary parts for T (Definition 2.4.2).
items.note: Missing. It follows formally from part (3) of the proposition: whenever f ∘ g and g ∘ f are the operators T, both f and g become quasi-isomorphisms on ordinary parts. That argument needs the ordinary part of Definition 2.4.2 (§2.4) for complexes in D(A_■), which no layer plans in this form.

items.name: Proposition 2.10.4(5): the eight ordinary cohomologies with mixed supports agree
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 2.10.4(1)–(2), RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F)^{C−ord} and RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F)^{C−ord} are canonically quasi-isomorphic. More generally, the eight complexes RΓ_{D₊^{(′)},D₋^{(′)}}(X̄, F)^{C−ord} and RΓ_{D₋^{(′)},D₊^{(′)}}(X̄, F)^{C−ord} are canonically quasi-isomorphic. Here each prime may or may not be present, and ord is the ordinary part for T.
items.note: Missing. The proof uses Lemma 2.10.2 to factor the relevant change-of-support maps through the cohomology supported on the proper set X̄ ∖ ((D′₊)° ∪ (D′₋)°). The maps T of part (2) then act on the five complexes involved, which agree on ordinary parts. No layer plans any of this. The paper uses the statement in §6.2 (p. 62) to compare higher Hida and higher Coleman theory.

items.name: §2.11: the setting of the control theorems (three nested dynamic correspondences)
items.statement:
Consider three dynamic correspondences (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D₊, D₋), (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D′₊, D′₋) and (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D″₊, D″₋) on the same (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂), with
D″₊ ⊆ (D′₊)° ⊆ D′₊ ⊆ (D₊)° ⊆ D₊ and D″₋ ⊆ (D′₋)° ⊆ D′₋ ⊆ (D₋)° ⊆ D₋.
Let X = X̄ ∖ (D₊ ∪ D₋), X′ = X̄ ∖ (D′₊ ∪ D′₋) and X″ = X̄ ∖ (D″₊ ∪ D″₋). Let C = C̄ ∖ (p̄₁^⋆D₊ ∪ p̄₂^⋆D₋), C′ = C̄ ∖ (p̄₁^⋆D′₊ ∪ p̄₂^⋆D′₋) and C″ = C̄ ∖ (p̄₁^⋆D″₊ ∪ p̄₂^⋆D″₋). Let p′_i and p″_i be the restrictions of p̄_i to C′ and C″. Assume:
- there is 0 < s < 1 such that, over C″, (p″₂)^⋆D₊ ≤ s(p″₁)^⋆D₊ and (p″₁)^⋆D₋ ≤ s(p″₂)^⋆D₋ (Definition 2.1.15(2)), i.e. D₊ is strictly expanded and D₋ strictly contracted over C″;
- p̄₂^⋆D′₊ ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D″₊ and p̄₁^⋆D′₋ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆D″₋ [printed 'p̄₁^⋆D′₊ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆D″₊ and p̄₂^⋆D′₋ ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D″₋', with p̄₁ and p̄₂ interchanged; sourceIssues E48];
- D₊, D₋, D″₊ and D″₋ are locally principal subschemes.
Finally, let F″ be a coherent sheaf on X″, let T : (p″₂)^⋆F″ → (p″₁)^!F″ be a cohomological correspondence, and let F = F″|_X.
items.note: Missing. The setting combines three dynamic correspondences on the same compactified correspondence and the strict inequality of divisors of Definition 2.1.15(2). It also needs locally principal boundary subschemes, a coherent sheaf F″ on X″ and a cohomological correspondence T. No layer plans dynamic correspondences or this configuration. The paper prints the inclusions between pullbacks of D′± and D″± with p̄₁ and p̄₂ swapped (sourceIssues E48). The setting is stated here with the inclusions the proofs use, p̄₂^⋆D′₊ ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D″₊ and p̄₁^⋆D′₋ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆D″₋.

items.name: Remark 2.11.2: the intermediate correspondences are compact dynamic
items.statement: In the setting of §2.11 (with the corrected inclusions p̄₂^⋆D′₊ ⊆ p̄₁^⋆D″₊ and p̄₁^⋆D′₋ ⊆ p̄₂^⋆D″₋), the correspondences (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D′₊, D′₋) and (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D″₊, D″₋) are compact dynamic. So are (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D″₊, D′₋) and (C̄, X̄, p̄₁, p̄₂, D′₊, D″₋).
items.note: Missing. With the corrected inclusions it follows from Proposition 2.10.4(1), which is itself unplanned.

items.name: Remark 2.11.3: closures of X and C are proper inside X′ and C′
items.statement: In the setting of §2.11, the closure of X in X̄ lies in X̄ ∖ ((D₊)° ∪ (D₋)°) ⊆ X′ ⊆ X″, so the closure of X in X′ is proper. The closure of C in C̄ lies in C̄ ∖ ((p̄₁^⋆D₊)° ∪ (p̄₂^⋆D₋)°) ⊆ C′ ⊆ C″, so the closure of C in C′ is proper.
items.note: Missing as stated. It is point-set bookkeeping in the setting of §2.11: X ⊆ X̄ ∖ (D₊ ∪ D₋) has closure in X̄ ∖ ((D₊)° ∪ (D₋)°), which lies in X′ because D′± ⊆ (D±)°. The closure is proper because it is closed in the proper X̄. Mathlib has proper morphisms (AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper), but the statement concerns the unplanned configuration of §2.11.

items.name: Theorem 2.11.4(1): T acts on the change-of-support squares
items.statement:
In the setting of §2.11, T acts on every term of the following commutative squares, and all their maps are T-equivariant. In each square the horizontal and vertical maps are the change-of-support maps of Lemma 2.2.6.
First square: top row RΓ_{D″₊,D₋}(X̄, F″) → RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F); bottom row RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″) → RΓ_{D₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″); vertical maps RΓ_{D″₊,D₋} → RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋} and RΓ_{D₊,D₋} → RΓ_{D₊,D″₋}.
Second square: top row RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″) → RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F); bottom row RΓ_{D″₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″) → RΓ_{D″₋,D₊}(X̄, F″); vertical maps RΓ_{D₋,D″₊} → RΓ_{D″₋,D″₊} and RΓ_{D₋,D₊} → RΓ_{D″₋,D₊}.
On each term T acts through Proposition 2.2.10, for the dynamic correspondence with the indicated supports and the restriction of T to the corresponding open subset of C″.
items.note: Missing. It rests on the change-of-support maps of Lemma 2.2.6 and the operators of Proposition 2.2.10 for the dynamic correspondences of §2.11, none of which is planned.

items.name: Theorem 2.11.4(2): (C, X, p₁, p₂) has a strict dynamic compactification, and partial supports compute RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord}
items.statement: In the setting of §2.11, let X^cl be the closure of X in X̄ and C^cl the closure of C in C̄; then X^cl ⊆ X″ and C^cl ⊆ C″. The correspondence (C, X, p₁, p₂) admits the strict dynamic compactification (C^cl, X^cl, p̄₁, p̄₂, D₊ ∩ X^cl, D₋ ∩ X^cl). Moreover RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F)^{ord} = RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F)^{ord} = RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord}, where RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord} is the ordinary cohomology of Theorem 2.5.1 and the ordinary parts on the left are for T_𝒞 (Proposition 2.2.10).
items.note: Missing. The proof uses Lemma 2.2.8, which says restriction to a strict dynamic compactification is a quasi-isomorphism. It also uses the ordinary cohomology RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord} of Theorem 2.5.1 and its independence of the compactification. None of these is planned.

items.name: Theorem 2.11.4(3): control theorem when T improves poles and zeros by one step
items.statement:
In the setting of §2.11, assume the following.
(a) T : (p″₂)^⋆F″ → (p″₁)^!F″ factors as (p″₂)^⋆F″ → (p″₂)^⋆F″(D₊) → (p″₁)^!F″(−D₋) → (p″₁)^!F″. The first and last maps are the natural ones.
(b) There are maps (p″₂)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(D₊) → (p″₁)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(D₊) and (p″₂)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(−D₋) → (p″₁)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(−D₋).
Then on ordinary parts all maps in the diagrams of Theorem 2.11.4(1) become quasi-isomorphisms, and there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism
RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″)^{ord} = RΓ_{D″₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″)^{ord} → RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord}.
items.note: Missing. Despite its name, this control theorem compares cohomologies with different supports at a fixed weight. It shows that the ordinary part of cohomology with bounded poles and zeros computes RΓ(X, F)^{C−ord}. It is not the specialisation in the weight variable of Pilloni's GSp4 control theorem (Duke 2020, Theorem 11.3.1(3)), which is proposed for the same Part II. The paper uses Theorem 2.11.4 in §6.2 (p. 62) to identify ordinary parts with higher Hida cohomology modulo p^s.

items.name: Theorem 2.11.4(4): control theorem in general, after a twist
items.statement:
In the setting of §2.11, after replacing D₊ and D₋ by nD₊ and nD₋ for some n ∈ Z_{>0}, there is m ≥ 0 and a quasi-isomorphism
RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″(mD₊ − mD₋))^{ord} = RΓ_{D″₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″(mD₊ − mD₋))^{ord} → RΓ_{D₊,D₋}(X̄, F)^{ord}.
Here F″(mD₊ − mD₋) = F″ ⊗ 𝒪_{X″}(D₊)^{⊗m} ⊗ 𝒪_{X″}(−D₋)^{⊗m}, whose restriction to X is F. T acts on it through the twisted correspondence.
items.note: Missing. It reduces to part (3) of the theorem through Lemma 2.5.3 and Lemma 2.1.17, which are unplanned. Replacing D± by nD± gives the factorisation of the twisted correspondence and the maps between the pulled-back line bundles.

items.name: Step in the proof of Theorem 2.11.4(3): RΓ_{D″₊,D₋}(X̄, F″)^{ord} = RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″)^{ord}
items.note: Missing. The argument follows the proof of Proposition 2.10.4(5). It factors the relevant change-of-support maps through RΓ_{∅,D₋}(Y, F″) on the closed subscheme Y = X̄ ∖ (D′₊)°. The maps T are built as in Proposition 2.10.4(2). No layer plans any of this.

items.name: Step in the proof of Theorem 2.11.4(3): limit and colimit presentations, constant on ordinary parts
items.statement:
In the setting of §2.11, under the hypotheses (a) and (b) of Theorem 2.11.4(3):
(i) The maps RΓ_{D″₊,D₋}(X̄, F″) → RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″(−mD₋)), m ≥ 0, induce an isomorphism RΓ_{D″₊,D₋}(X̄, F″) ≅ lim_m RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″(−mD₋)). On this limit, T factors through maps RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″(−mD₋)) → RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″(−(m+1)D₋)). Hence RΓ_{D″₊,D₋}(X̄, F″)^{ord} = RΓ_{D″₊,D″₋}(X̄, F″)^{ord}.
(ii) The maps RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″(mD₊)) → RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F) induce an isomorphism colim_{m≥0} RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″(mD₊)) ≅ RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F). On this colimit, T factors through maps RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″(mD₊)) → RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″((m−1)D₊)) for m > 0. Hence the colimit is constant on ordinary parts, and RΓ_{D₋,D″₊}(X̄, F″)^{ord} = RΓ_{D₋,D₊}(X̄, F)^{ord}.
items.note:
Missing. It needs:
- the limit and colimit presentations of cohomology with supports along locally principal divisors (Corollary 2.3.11, resting on Proposition 2.3.2, j_!F = lim_n F(−nD));
- ordinary parts of limits and colimits along which T shifts the index (§2.4).
None of these is planned.

items.name: Step in the proof of Theorem 2.11.4(4): the twisted correspondence satisfies the hypotheses of (3)
items.statement: In the setting of §2.11, after replacing D₊ and D₋ by nD₊ and nD₋ for some n ∈ Z_{>0}, there is m ≥ 0 with two properties. First, the twisted correspondence T : (p″₂)^⋆F″(mD₊ − mD₋) → (p″₁)^!F″(mD₊ − mD₋) factors as in Theorem 2.11.4(3)(a). Second, there are maps (p″₂)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(D₊) → (p″₁)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(D₊) and (p″₂)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(−D₋) → (p″₁)^⋆𝒪_{X″}(−D₋).
items.note: Missing. It applies Lemmas 2.5.3 and 2.1.17: after replacing D± by nD±, the strict inequalities of divisors over C″ give the factorisation and the maps between the pulled-back line bundles. These lemmas concern dynamic correspondences, which no layer plans.

items.name: The group G = GSp_{2g} and its symplectic form
items.statement: G = GSp_{2g} is the group scheme over Z of symplectic similitudes of the free module V = Z^{2g}. V has canonical basis e_1, …, e_{2g} and carries the symplectic form with matrix J = (0 S; −S 0), where S is the g × g antidiagonal matrix with 1 on the antidiagonal. Thus ⟨e_i, e_j⟩ = 0 if i + j ≠ 2g + 1, and ⟨e_i, e_{2g+1−i}⟩ = 1 for 1 ≤ i ≤ g.
items.note: G = GSp_{2g} over Z is the similitude group of the integral Siegel datum (Z^{2g}, J), where J = (0 S; −S 0) and S is antidiagonal. Its matrix form was checked on the p. 33 image. The libraries have only Sp_{2m}, for the forms fromBlocks 0 (−1) 1 0 and its Fin (m + m) transport. The paper's antidiagonal form is conjugate to these by a signed permutation, so a transport lemma is needed. The similitude character is in neither library. This is the same status as the GSp4 group in the extractions of Pilloni (Duke 2020) and Calegari–Geraghty (2020), extended here to every genus g.

items.name: Siegel Shimura datum (G, X) and the Hodge cocharacter μ
items.statement: Let h_0 : Res_{C/R} G_m → G_R be the morphism z = x + iy ↦ (x·Id_g, y·S; −y·S, x·Id_g), a 2 × 2 block matrix. X is the G(R)-conjugacy class of h_0, and (G, X) is the Siegel Shimura datum. X has two connected components, the Siegel upper and lower half-spaces, which are exchanged by elements of negative similitude such as diag(Id_g, −Id_g); each component is a Hermitian symmetric domain. Identify (Res_{C/R} G_m)_C = (G_m)_C × (G_m)_C via z ↦ (z, z̄). Each h ∈ X then defines a cocharacter μ_h : (G_m)_C → G_C by μ_h(z) = h(z, 1). The paper fixes the representative μ(z) = diag(Id_g, z·Id_g) of the conjugacy class of μ_h.
items.note: The formula for h_0 was checked on the p. 33 image. Checked by direct computation: h_0(i) = J, so X is the usual Siegel double half-space. μ_{h_0} has weights 0 and 1, each with multiplicity g, so the chosen representative μ(z) = diag(Id_g, z·Id_g) lies in its conjugacy class. The identification z ↦ (z, z̄), μ_h(z) = h(z, 1) and the representative μ are coordinate choices on these planned objects. The introduction recalls this set-up in §1.1 (p. 2): µ is the Hodge cocharacter of a point h, P_µ is the Siegel parabolic attached to µ, M_µ is its Levi (printed there as 'the unipotent radical of P_µ'; sourceIssues E1), and T ⊆ B ⊆ P_µ are a maximal torus and a Borel. Some conventions are stated only in the introduction. The irreducible objects of Rep(M_µ) are labelled by M_µ-dominant weights κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} (§1.1, p. 2). w_{0,M} is the longest element of W_M (§1.3.3, p. 3), and w_0, the longest element of W, enters through the involution w ↦ w_{0,M}ww_0 of ^MW (§1.4, p. 5). On X⋆(T)_R, λ ≥ λ′ means that λ − λ′ is a linear combination of positive roots with non-negative coefficients (Remark 1.3.6, p. 3).

items.name: The parabolics P^std and P = P_μ, the Levi M and the unipotent radical U_P
items.statement: P^std_μ = P^std is the stabilizer of ⟨e_1, …, e_g⟩, i.e. the block upper triangular matrices in G. P_μ = P is the opposite parabolic, the stabilizer of ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩, i.e. the block lower triangular matrices in G. M_μ = M is the Levi subgroup (block diagonal matrices), and U_P is the unipotent radical of P (the lower left block).
items.note: P^std is the Siegel parabolic stabilizing the Lagrangian ⟨e_1, …, e_g⟩, and P = P_μ is its opposite. M consists of block-diagonal matrices (≅ GL_g × G_m). U_P is the lower-left block, a vector group of rank g(g+1)/2 ≅ Sym². The extraction of Caraiani–Scholze (2017) marks P_μ and P^std_μ planned at ShimuraData:D3. The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty (2020) marks the GSp4 Siegel parabolic planned at Tau Ceti Layer 7 and C1. This item is the genus-g instance.

items.name: The diagonal torus T and the parametrization of X*(T)
items.statement: T = {diag(t_1, …, t_{2g}) : t_i t_{2g+1−i} = c for all i} is the diagonal maximal torus. T^der = {diag(t_1, …, t_g, t_g^{-1}, …, t_1^{-1})} is the maximal torus of the derived group, and the center Z consists of the scalar diagonal matrices. The character group X*(T) is identified with the set of tuples κ = (k_1, …, k_g; k) ∈ Z^g × Z with Σ_{i=1}^g k_i ≡ k mod 2, via κ(diag(zt_1, …, zt_g, zt_g^{-1}, …, zt_1^{-1})) = z^k ∏_{i=1}^g t_i^{k_i}.
items.note: Checked by direct computation. T = (T^der × Z)/μ_2, with μ_2 embedded as (−1, −1). A character z^k ∏ t_i^{k_i} of T^der × Z descends to T exactly when Σ k_i ≡ k mod 2, which is the parity condition stated on p. 33. The parametrization of X*(T) is a coordinate choice on planned objects. The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty (2020) marks its GSp4 torus the same way.

items.name: The Borel B ⊆ P, positive roots Φ^+ = Φ^+_M ⊔ Φ^{+,M}, ρ and ρ_nc
items.statement: B ⊆ P is the Borel subgroup of elements of P that are upper triangular on the two diagonal g × g blocks. Φ is the set of roots and Φ^+ the positive roots for B. Φ^+ = Φ^+_M ⊔ Φ^{+,M}, where Φ^+_M is the set of positive roots in m = Lie(M) and Φ^{+,M} is the set of roots in u_P = Lie(U_P). ρ = ½ Σ_{α∈Φ^+} α and ρ_nc = ½ Σ_{α∈Φ^{+,M}} α.
items.note: No layer states the root datum of GSp_{2g} in the paper's coordinates. In particular no layer states the Borel B ⊆ P used here (U_P lower-left, upper triangular on the diagonal blocks), the splitting Φ^+ = Φ^+_M ⊔ Φ^{+,M}, or ρ_nc. Checked by direct computation in the coordinates (k_1, …, k_g; k): Φ^+_M = {e_i − e_j : i < j}; Φ^{+,M} = {−e_i − e_j : i ≤ j}, of cardinality g(g+1)/2 = dim U_P; the simple roots are e_i − e_{i+1} (1 ≤ i < g) and −2e_1; ρ_nc = (−(g+1)/2, …, −(g+1)/2; 0) and ρ = (−1, −2, …, −g; 0), which lies in the interior of the dominant cone of p. 34. The GSp4 analogue (Pilloni 2020; Calegari–Geraghty 2020) is also missing and routed to ShimuraData:D5.

items.name: Dominant cones X*(T)^+ and X*(T)^{+,M}
items.statement: The dominant cone X*(T)^+ is {κ = (k_1, …, k_g; k) : 0 ≥ k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g}. The dominant cone for the Levi M is X*(T)^{+,M} = {κ : k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g}.
items.note: Checked by direct computation for the paper's B. The simple coroot conditions are k_i ≥ k_{i+1} and −k_1 ≥ 0, which give 0 ≥ k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g. For M only the first family applies, giving k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g. The printed cones on p. 34 are therefore correct. What is missing is the GSp_{2g} root datum in these coordinates (see the Borel and roots item). The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty (2020) marks the GSp4 Weyl chambers missing.

items.name: The map v : T(Q_p) → X_*(T) and the monoids T^+(Q_p) ⊇ T^{++}(Q_p)
items.statement: X_*(T) is the cocharacter group of T. The map v : T(Q_p) → X_*(T) is obtained by writing T(Q_p) = Q_p^× ⊗ X_*(T) and applying the valuation Q_p^× → Z, normalized by v(p) = 1. v has the section λ ↦ λ(p), so T(Q_p) = X_*(T) × T(Z_p). T^+(Q_p) (resp. T^{++}(Q_p)) is the set of t ∈ T(Q_p) with v(t) dominant (resp. dominant regular). Concretely, t = diag(t_1, …, t_{2g}) lies in T^+(Q_p) iff v(t_{g+1}) ≥ v(t_{g+2}) ≥ ⋯ ≥ v(t_{2g}) ≥ v(t_1) ≥ ⋯ ≥ v(t_g), and lies in T^{++}(Q_p) iff all these inequalities are strict.
items.note: For the split torus T, v is the map T(Q_p)/T(Z_p) ≅ X_*(T) with v(λ(p)) = λ, which underlies the Cartan decomposition of RG2.4. Up to a sign convention that must be pinned, it is BG1's Kottwitz map for T. Checked by direct computation: with the paper's B, a_i/a_j is a positive root exactly when i precedes j in the order g+1, …, 2g, 1, …, g. Hence v(t) is dominant if and only if v(t_{g+1}) ≥ ⋯ ≥ v(t_{2g}) ≥ v(t_1) ≥ ⋯ ≥ v(t_g), as printed on p. 34. T^+(Q_p) and T^{++}(Q_p) are subsets defined directly from these planned notions.

items.name: Weyl groups W ⊇ W_M and the Kostant set ^M W
items.statement: W is the Weyl group of G and W_M that of M. ^M W is the set of minimal length representatives of W_M\W. It is characterized by w X*(T)^+ ⊆ X*(T)^{+,M}, or equivalently by w^{-1}Φ^+_M ⊆ Φ^+. Concretely, W is the group of permutations w of {1, …, 2g} with w(i) + w(2g+1−i) = 2g+1, acting by w(diag(t_1, …, t_{2g})) = diag(t_{w^{-1}(1)}, …, t_{w^{-1}(2g)}). W_M is the subgroup of those w with w({1, …, g}) = {1, …, g}. ^M W is the set of w such that w^{-1}(g+1), w^{-1}(g+2), …, w^{-1}(2g) are increasing for the order g+1 ≺ g+2 ≺ ⋯ ≺ 2g ≺ 1 ≺ 2 ≺ ⋯ ≺ g. W has a partial order (the Bruhat order), which induces a partial order on ^M W, and there is a length function ℓ : ^M W → [0, g(g+1)/2].
items.note: No layer plans ^M W or its characterization. The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty (2020) marks the GSp4 Kostant representatives missing and routes them to ShimuraData:D5. The statement above uses corrected forms of two printed conditions on p. 34, both checked on the image and by direct computation for g = 2 and 3. (a) The page prints 'equivalently by the condition w^{-1}Φ^{+,M} ⊆ Φ^+'. That condition holds exactly for w ∈ W_M. The correct condition is w^{-1}Φ^+_M ⊆ Φ^+ (sourceIssues E52). (b) The page prints 'w^{-1}(g+1) < w^{-1}(g+2) ⋯ < w^{-1}(2g)'. This holds for the order g+1 ≺ ⋯ ≺ 2g ≺ 1 ≺ ⋯ ≺ g, not for the usual order (sourceIssues E53). For g = 2, the minimal representative with w^{-1}{3, 4} = {2, 4} has (w^{-1}(3), w^{-1}(4)) = (4, 2). The characterization w X*(T)^+ ⊆ X*(T)^{+,M} is correct as printed. The maximal length g(g+1)/2 equals dim FL.

items.name: Bruhat stratification of FL = P\G by B-orbits
items.statement: Let FL = P\G be the partial flag variety, viewed as a scheme, with G acting by right translation. The B-orbits give a stratification FL = ⊔_{w∈^M W} C_w, where C_w = P\PwB is a Bruhat cell. For w ∈ ^M W, ℓ(w) = dim C_w. For w, w' ∈ ^M W, w' ≤ w if and only if C_{w'} ⊆ \overline{C_w}.
items.note: Four things are not planned: the partial flag variety P\G as a scheme over a general base; its decomposition into B-orbits C_w = P\PwB indexed by ^M W; dim C_w = ℓ(w) for Kostant representatives; and the closure relation C_{w'} ⊆ closure(C_w) ⟺ w' ≤ w (Chevalley). The paper recalls this standard fact without a reference. Consistency checked by direct computation: C_1 = P\PB is a point (B ⊆ P), and the maximal length g(g+1)/2 in ^M W equals dim P\G. External input: Bruhat decomposition of a partial flag variety (standard; recalled in the paper without a reference).

items.name: The subset and the sequence (w_1, …, w_g) attached to w ∈ ^M W
items.statement: To w ∈ ^M W one attaches the set w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g} ∩ {g+1, …, 2g}, which determines w. One also attaches the sequence (w_1, …, w_g) defined by w_0 = 0 and, for 1 ≤ i ≤ g, w_i − w_{i−1} = 1 if g+i ∈ w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g} and w_i − w_{i−1} = 0 if g+i ∉ w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g}.
items.note: This is a combinatorial invariant of Kostant representatives for GSp_{2g}. It is planned nowhere, because ^M W itself is missing. Checked by direct computation. The set S = w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g} contains exactly one of i and 2g+1−i for each i, so S ∩ {g+1, …, 2g} determines S and hence the coset. For g ≤ 3, ℓ(w) = g(g+1)/2 − (w_1 + ⋯ + w_g) on ^M W, a consistency check with the dimension of C_w.

items.name: Geometric meaning of (w_1, …, w_g) on the Bruhat cell C_w
items.statement: For x ∈ P\G, the parabolic x^{-1}Px is the stabilizer of x^{-1}⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩. If w ∈ ^M W and x ∈ C_w, then w_i = dim(x^{-1}⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩ ∩ ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{g+i}⟩) for 1 ≤ i ≤ g.
items.note: Planned nowhere, since it depends on the missing Bruhat cells and ^M W. Checked by direct computation, with the permutation matrix w e_i = e_{w(i)} (the convention matching w(diag(t)) = diag(t_{w^{-1}(1)}, …)). For x = Pwb one has x^{-1}⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩ = b^{-1}⟨e_j : j ∈ w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g}⟩. Since ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{g+i}⟩ is B-stable, its intersection with this space has dimension #(w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g} ∩ {g+1, …, g+i}) = w_i. The statement is correct and independent of the coset representative.

items.name: Siegel Shimura variety S_{K,Q} and its moduli description
items.statement: For a neat compact open subgroup K ⊆ G(A_f), S_{K,Q} → Spec Q is the Siegel Shimura variety, with S_{K,Q}(C) = G(Q)\(X × G(A_f)/K). For a connected affine Q-scheme Spec R, S_{K,Q}(Spec R) is the set of isomorphism classes of triples (A, λ, η), where (1) A → Spec R is an abelian scheme of dimension g; (2) λ : A → A^D is a quasi-polarization; (3) η : V ⊗_Z A_f → H_1(A) ⊗_Z Q is a K-orbit of symplectic isomorphisms, up to a similitude factor, of pro-étale sheaves. An isomorphism (A, λ, η) → (A', λ', η') is a quasi-isogeny ξ : A → A' with η' = H_1(ξ) ∘ η and ξ^D λ' ξ = rλ for some r ∈ Q_{>0} [printed ξ^D λξ = rλ; sourceIssues E54].
items.note: This is the rational quasi-isogeny moduli problem with adelic level for the Siegel datum. Its comparison with G(Q)\(X × G(A_f)/K) is M3. For GSp_{2g} the relevant ker¹ is trivial, so M3's single-variety identification applies after the Hasse-principle calculation that M3 requires. The Pilloni (2020) Siegel-threefold items are planned at the same layers. The introduction (§1.1, p. 2) presents the S_K as a tower {S_K}_{K ⊆ G(A_f)} of Shimura varieties over the reflex field Q, parametrizing polarized abelian schemes of dimension g with level structure and carrying an action of G(A_f). There S^tor_{K,Σ} denotes a toroidal compactification of S_K and D_{K,Σ} its boundary divisor.

items.name: Toroidal compactifications S^tor_{K,Q,Σ}
items.statement: For a suitable choice Σ of K-admissible rational polyhedral cone decompositions, S_{K,Q} has a toroidal compactification S^tor_{K,Q,Σ}.
items.note: Existence over Q for a K-admissible cone decomposition, following Faltings–Chai and Lan (2013), Theorem 6.4.1.1. The Pilloni (2020) toroidal item is planned at the same layers. External input: [FC90] G. Faltings, C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of Abelian Varieties, Springer (1990); [Lan13] K.-W. Lan, Arithmetic Compactifications of PEL-Type Shimura Varieties, LMS Monographs 36 (2013), Theorem 6.4.1.1.

items.name: Level data at p and the perfectoid Siegel space S^tor_{K^p,Σ} ⊇ S_{K^p}
items.statement: Fix a prime p, a neat compact open subgroup K^p ⊆ G(A_f^p), a compact open subgroup K_p ⊆ G(Q_p) and a K^pK_p-admissible cone decomposition Σ. S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} denotes the adic space over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) attached to the scheme S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ}. S^tor_{K^p,Σ} = lim_{K'_p ⊆ K_p} S^tor_{K^pK'_p,Σ} is the perfectoid Siegel moduli space, formed with the same cone decomposition at every level of the tower. S_{K^p} is the open complement of the boundary in S^tor_{K^p,Σ}.
items.note: The adic spaces attached to S^tor_{K^pK_p,Σ} (analytification of the planned toroidal models) and the inverse limit as a diamond are planned. The perfectoidness of lim_{K'_p} S^tor_{K^pK'_p,Σ}, with the same cone decomposition at every level, is planned nowhere. That is Pilloni–Stroh (2016), Théorème 0.4, and it is what the paper uses to define π_HT on the toroidal tower. External input: [Sch15] P. Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties, Ann. of Math. 182 (2015); [PS16] V. Pilloni, B. Stroh, Cohomologie cohérente et représentations galoisiennes, Ann. Math. Québec 40 (2016), Théorème 0.4.

items.name: Equivariance of π_HT
items.statement: For f ∈ G(Q_p), (A, Ψ)f = (A, Ψ ∘ f) and g(Ψ ∘ f) = f^{-1} g(Ψ). Hence π_HT((A, Ψ ∘ f)) = π_HT((A, Ψ)) f, i.e. π_HT is G(Q_p)-equivariant for the right action of G(Q_p) on P\G.
items.note: Checked by direct computation: Ψ∘f carries ⟨f^{-1}g(Ψ)e_{g+1}, …, f^{-1}g(Ψ)e_{2g}⟩ onto Lie_A(1), so g(Ψ∘f) = f^{-1}g(Ψ). Hence π_HT(A, Ψ∘f) = P g(Ψ)^{-1} f, as stated in Remark 3.3.1.

items.name: The ordinary p-divisible group X_ord, its polarization λ_can and b_ord
items.statement: X_ord = (μ_{p^∞})^g ⊕ (Q_p/Z_p)^g over Z_p. Its canonical polarization λ_can : X_ord → X_ord^D = (Q_p/Z_p)^g ⊕ (μ_{p^∞})^g is given by the block matrix (0, S·Id_{(Q_p/Z_p)^g}; −S·Id_{(μ_{p^∞})^g}, 0), with S the antidiagonal matrix. The Frobenius of the Dieudonné module of X_ord|_{F_p} corresponds to b_ord = diag(p^{-1}Id_g, Id_g) ∈ G(Q̆_p).
items.note: Two things are planned only for the unitary datum of Caraiani–Scholze: polarizations of p-divisible groups, and the dictionary between polarized Dieudonné modules with GSp_{2g}-structure and elements b ∈ G(Q̆_p). IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0 treats 'a p-divisible group X ... with its O_F and polarization structures', but that roadmap says 'These geometric constructions do not assert results for every Hodge-type or arbitrary Shimura datum'. The Pilloni (2020) extraction marks quasi-polarizations of BT_1's missing. The block matrix of λ_can and b_ord = diag(p^{-1}Id_g, Id_g) were checked on the p. 35 image.

items.name: The (perfectoid-level) Igusa formal scheme IG_{K^p}
items.statement: Nilp/Z_p is the category of Z_p-algebras in which p is nilpotent. IG_{K^p} is the p-adic formal scheme over Z_p that represents the functor sending R ∈ Nilp/Z_p to the set of isomorphism classes of quadruples (A, λ, η^p, j), where (1) A → Spec R is an abelian scheme of dimension g with a prime-to-p polarization λ and a K^p-level structure η^p; (2) j : X_ord → A[p^∞] is an isomorphism such that j^D ∘ λ ∘ j = c·λ_can : X_ord → X_ord^D for some c ∈ Z_p^×. An isomorphism (A, λ, η^p, j) → (A', λ', η^{p'}, j') is a prime-to-p quasi-isogeny ξ : A → A' that matches λ and λ' up to an element of Z_{(p),>0}^× and matches η^p with η^{p'} and j with j'. This is the Igusa variety attached to b_ord.
items.note: This is the GSp_{2g} generalization of Pilloni's formal Igusa tower (Duke 2020). Pilloni's tower is only a Z_p^×-torsor Isom(μ_{p^∞}, H_∞) over the p-rank ≥ 1 Klingen locus of the Siegel threefold. It is missing in the extraction of that paper and routed to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, whose brief names this paper as a future source. The paper takes the definition from Caraiani–Scholze (2017), §4, Definition 4.3.1. The extraction of that paper proposes the characteristic-p perfect Igusa variety for general PEL data as a source for IG.0–IG.1. The p-adic formal scheme over Z_p with its finite levels (Proposition 3.4.9) is Hida-theoretic and is planned nowhere. The introduction (§1.3.9, p. 4) calls IG_{K^p} a perfectoid p-adic formal scheme and uses it to describe the fibres of the Hodge–Tate period map π_HT : S_{K^p} → FL = P_µ\G of the good-reduction perfectoid Shimura variety. There ^MW is the fixed-point set of T(Q_p) on FL, and each fibre π_HT^{-1}({w}), w ∈ ^MW, is a perfectoid Igusa variety in the sense of Caraiani–Scholze (2017), identified with (the canonical compactification of) IG_{K^p} ×_{Spa(Z_p,Z_p)} Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl). In the body this identification corresponds to the P(Q_p)-equivariant map from the adic generic fibre of IG_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} to S_{K^p} × Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl) of §3.4.17 (p. 39). External input: [CS17] A. Caraiani, P. Scholze, On the generic part of the cohomology of compact unitary Shimura varieties, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017), §4, Definition 4.3.1 (perfectoid Igusa tower).

items.name: Quasi-isogeny formulation of the Igusa moduli problem
items.statement: Equivalently, up to quasi-isogeny, IG_{K^p} parametrizes isomorphism classes of quadruples (A, λ, η^p, j), where (1)' A → Spec R is an abelian scheme of dimension g with a quasi-polarization λ and a K^p-level structure η^p; (2)' j : X_ord → A[p^∞] is a quasi-isogeny with j^D ∘ λ ∘ j = c·λ_can for some c ∈ Q_p^×. Isomorphisms are quasi-isogenies ξ : A → A' that match λ and λ' up to an element of Q_{>0} and match η^p with η^{p'} and j with j'.
items.note: This is the equivalence between the isomorphism and quasi-isogeny moduli problems for the ordinary Igusa tower of GSp_{2g}. It is the formulation through which J_ord acts. It is missing together with IG_{K^p}.

items.name: The group J_ord = J_{b_ord} of symplectic self-quasi-isogenies
items.statement: J_ord = J_{b_ord} is the group functor on Nilp/Z_p given by J_ord(R) = Qisog_symp(X_ord ×_{Spec Z_p} Spec R), the group of self-quasi-isogenies of X_ord that respect the polarization up to a similitude factor in Q_p^×. Let X̃_ord = lim_{×p} X_ord be the universal cover of X_ord. Then Qisog_symp(X_ord ×_{Spec Z_p} Spec R) = Aut_symp(X̃_ord ×_{Spec Z_p} Spec R).
items.note: Universal covers of p-divisible groups (Scholze–Weinstein 2013, §3.1) are planned nowhere. The extraction of Caraiani–Scholze (2017) marks them missing and proposes HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0/T2 for them. The group functor of symplectic self-quasi-isogenies of X_ord, and its identification with Aut_symp of the universal cover, are missing. The introduction (§1.3.9, p. 4) describes J_ord as the group of polarized self quasi-isogenies of µ_{p^∞}^g ⊕ (Q_p/Z_p)^g over Z_p-algebras in which p is nilpotent, acting naturally on IG_{K^p}. Its subgroup P′(Q_p) of self quasi-isogenies that lift to characteristic 0 is a locally profinite group scheme over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) and a form of the constant group scheme P_µ(Q_p). External input: [SW13] P. Scholze, J. Weinstein, Moduli of p-divisible groups, Camb. J. Math. 1 (2013), §3.1 (universal cover; quasi-isogenies are automorphisms of the universal cover).

items.name: Structure of J_ord (Lemma 3.4.3)
items.statement: J_ord is a representable formal group scheme over Spf Z_p, and J_ord = M_μ(Q_p) ⋉ U_{J_ord}. Here M(Q_p), a locally profinite group, is viewed as a locally constant formal group scheme over Spf Z_p, and U_{J_ord} = μ̃_{p^∞} ⊗_{Q_p} Sym² Q_p^g, where μ̃_{p^∞} is the universal cover of μ_{p^∞}. M(Q_p) acts on U_{J_ord} through its usual action on Sym² Q_p^g ≃ U_P(Q_p).
items.note: Lemma 3.4.3 was checked on the p. 36 image. The proof writes Aut(X̃_ord) as block upper triangular, with diagonal blocks Aut(X̃_{ord,m}) ≃ Aut(X̃_{ord,et}) ≃ GL_g(Q_p) and corner Hom(X̃_{ord,et}, X̃_{ord,m}) = μ̃_{p^∞} ⊗ M_{g×g}(Q_p). The polarization cuts the corner down to Sym²Q_p^g. The page writes U_{J_b} and U_{J_ord} for the same group. This item depends on the missing J_ord and universal covers.

items.name: Right action of J_ord on IG_{K^p}
items.statement: J_ord acts on the right on IG_{K^p} through the quasi-isogeny formulation of the moduli problem: (A, λ, η^p, j)g = (A, λ, η^p, j ∘ g) for g ∈ J_ord.
items.note: The action (A, λ, η^p, j)g = (A, λ, η^p, j∘g) uses the quasi-isogeny formulation. Both are missing for GSp_{2g}.

items.name: J^an_ord, its unipotent part, and the locally profinite group P'(Q_p)
items.statement: J^an_ord := J_ord ×_{Spf Z_p} Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is the adic generic fibre of J_ord. There is an exact sequence of fpqc sheaves 0 → T_p(μ_{p^∞}) → μ̃_{p^∞} → μ_{p^∞} → 0. Put Z_p(1) = T_p(μ_{p^∞}) × Spa(Q_p, Z_p), a profinite étale group, and Ĝ^an_m = μ_{p^∞} × Spa(Q_p, Z_p), the open unit ball with its multiplicative structure. Then 0 → Z_p(1) → μ̃_{p^∞} × Spa(Q_p, Z_p) → Ĝ^an_m → 0 is exact. Hence J^an_ord is the semi-direct product of M(Q_p) by the unipotent group U_{J_ord} × Spa(Q_p, Z_p), which fits in an exact sequence 0 → Sym² Z_p^g(1) → U_{J_ord} × Spa(Q_p, Z_p) → Ĝ^an_m ⊗_{Z_p} Sym² Z_p^g → 0. Since multiplication by p is an isomorphism on μ̃_{p^∞} × Spa(Q_p, Z_p), there is an embedding Q_p(1) → μ̃_{p^∞} × Spa(Q_p, Z_p). P′(Q_p) ↪ J^an_ord is the locally profinite subgroup scheme generated by M(Q_p) and U_P(Q_p)(1) ≃ Q_p(1) ⊗_{Z_p} Sym² Z_p^g. Over Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl), a choice of isomorphism Z_p(1) = Z_p identifies P′(Q_p) with P(Q_p). (Remark 3.4.4) J^an_ord is g(g+1)/2-dimensional, whereas P′(Q_p) is zero-dimensional.
items.note: This item needs three missing inputs: the exact sequence 0 → T_p(μ_{p^∞}) → μ̃_{p^∞} → μ_{p^∞} → 0 of fpqc sheaves (the Anschütz–Le Bras extraction also marks exactness of the universal cover sequence missing); the adic generic fibre of the formal group J_ord; and the locally profinite subgroup P'(Q_p) generated by M(Q_p) and U_P(Q_p)(1). The exact sequences were checked on the p. 36 image. Over Q_p^cycl, a choice Z_p(1) = Z_p identifies P'(Q_p) with P(Q_p).

items.name: Level groups K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Q_p), P'(Z_p) = J^int_ord, U_{K_{p,P}} and M_{K_{p,P}}
items.statement: Finite level Igusa varieties are indexed by compact open subgroups K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p). Equivalently, these are the compact open subgroups of P(Q_p) that are stable under the action of Gal(Q_p^cycl/Q_p), which acts on the unipotent radical through the cyclotomic character. J^int_ord := Aut_symp(X_ord). Its generic fibre J^int_ord × Spa(Q_p, Z_p) =: P'(Z_p) is the semi-direct product of M(Z_p) by U_P(Z_p)(1), and P'(Q_p) is generated by P'(Z_p) and M(Q_p). For such K_{p,P} one sets U_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ U_P(Q_p)(1) and M_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ M(Q_p) = K_{p,P}^{Gal(Q_p^cycl/Q_p)}.
items.note: These are definitions on the missing group P'(Q_p). Checked: Gal(Q_p^cycl/Q_p) acts on U_P(Q_p)(1) through χ_cycl, and fixes u ≠ 0 only when χ_cycl(σ) = 1. Hence K_{p,P}^{Gal} = K_{p,P} ∩ M(Q_p), as stated on p. 37.

items.name: For p > 2, K_{p,P} = M_{K_{p,P}} ⋉ U_{K_{p,P}} (and Remark 3.4.7)
items.statement: If p > 2, every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p) satisfies K_{p,P} = M_{K_{p,P}} ⋉ U_{K_{p,P}}. Consequently (Remark 3.4.7), when p > 2 the compact open subgroups of P'(Q_p) are in bijection with the compact open subgroups of P(Q_p) that are semi-direct products M_{K_{p,P}} ⋉ U_{K_{p,P}}.
items.note: The proof on p. 37 was checked by direct computation. For g = m·u and σ with χ_cycl(σ) − 1 ∈ Z_p^×, σ(g)^{-1}g = (1 − χ_cycl(σ))u. Since K_{p,P} ∩ U_P(Q_p)(1) is a Z_p-submodule, u ∈ K_{p,P}. Such σ exist exactly when p > 2. The hypothesis is necessary. For p = 2 and g = 1, the set {diag(a, b)·u : a, b ∈ Z_2^×, u ∈ Z_2, u ≡ (a − 1)/2 mod 2} is a Galois-stable compact open subgroup. Its intersection with M(Q_2) is {a ≡ 1 mod 4}, so it is not (K ∩ M) ⋉ (K ∩ U).

items.name: Schematic closure \overline{K_{p,P}} ⊆ J_ord
items.statement: For a compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p), \overline{K_{p,P}} is the schematic closure of K_{p,P} in J_ord. That is, \overline{K_{p,P}} is defined by the sheaf of ideals of O_{J_ord} consisting of the sections that vanish on K_{p,P}.
items.note: Footnote 3, p. 37: the closure is defined by the ideal of sections of O_{J_ord} vanishing on K_{p,P}. The item is missing because J_ord is.

items.name: \overline{K_{p,P}} is profinite flat with generic fibre K_{p,P} (Lemma 3.4.8)
items.statement: For every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p), the group scheme \overline{K_{p,P}} is a profinite flat group scheme over Z_p whose generic fibre is K_{p,P}.
items.note: Lemma 3.4.8. The proof conjugates K_{p,P} by M(Q_p) into a finite-index subgroup of P'(Z_p). It then writes the closure as lim_n of the closures in M(Z/p^n) ⋉ μ_{p^n} ⊗ Sym²Z_p^g and applies Raynaud (1974), §2. Missing, since J_ord and P'(Q_p) are.

items.name: Exact sequence of closures and the formal torus T̂_{K_{p,P}}
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} be a compact open subgroup of P′(Q_p). The quotient \overline{K_{p,P}}/\overline{U_{K_{p,P}}} is the profinite étale (constant) group scheme attached to the image of K_{p,P} in M(Q_p), which is isomorphic to K_{p,P}/U_{K_{p,P}}. So there is an exact sequence 1 → \overline{U_{K_{p,P}}} → \overline{K_{p,P}} → (image of K_{p,P} in M(Q_p)) → 1. When K_{p,P} = M_{K_{p,P}} ⋉ U_{K_{p,P}}, which is automatic for p > 2, this image is M_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ M(Q_p). The sequence is then the one obtained by taking schematic closures in 1 → U_{K_{p,P}} → K_{p,P} → M_{K_{p,P}} → 1, namely 1 → \overline{U_{K_{p,P}}} → \overline{K_{p,P}} → \overline{M_{K_{p,P}}} → 1, with \overline{M_{K_{p,P}}} profinite étale. The formal torus is T̂_{K_{p,P}} := (μ̃_{p^∞} ⊗ Sym² Z_p^g)/\overline{U_{K_{p,P}}}. It is a formal torus isogenous to Ĝ_m ⊗ Sym² Z_p^g.
items.note: The definition of T̂_{K_{p,P}} = μ̃_{p^∞} ⊗ Sym²Z_p^g / closure(U_{K_{p,P}}) was checked on the p. 37 image. It depends on the missing J_ord and closures.

items.name: Existence of IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} and the torsor IG_{K^p} → IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} (Prop. 3.4.9(1),(2))
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} be a compact open subgroup of P′(Q_p). (1) The fpqc quotient of IG_{K^p} by \overline{K_{p,P}} exists as a p-adic formal scheme, denoted IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}. (2) The map IG_{K^p} → IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} is a \overline{K_{p,P}}-torsor for the fpqc topology.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.9(1)–(2). The proof builds IG_{K^p} as a Frobenius limit over the ordinary locus. It reduces to P'(Z_p)_n ⊆ K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Z_p) and quotients by a finite flat group scheme (Raynaud 1967). On p. 38 the group is printed as closure(K_{p,P})/closure(P(Z_p)_n) and the space as IG_{K^pP(Z_p)_n}; P'(Z_p)_n is meant (sourceIssues E61). The introduction (§1.3.9, p. 4) describes the same tower {IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}}_{K_{p,P} ⊆ P′(Q_p)}, with IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} the quotient of IG_{K^p} by K_{p,P}. It adds that the action of T(Q_p) on the fibre π_HT^{-1}({w}) of the Hodge–Tate period map gives a map T(Q_p) → P′(Q_p), so that each w ∈ ^MW determines the tower together with this map. In the body this map corresponds to conjugation by w: the Hecke correspondences of §5.1 (p. 53) are attached to elements of T_w(Q_p)^{++} = wT(Q_p)^{++}w^{-1}, and at the end of §5.2.6 (p. 55) the T(Q_p)-action on the higher Hida complexes is twisted by w.

items.name: IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} is smooth of finite type over Z_p (Prop. 3.4.9(3))
items.statement: For every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p), the formal scheme IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} is smooth of finite type over Z_p.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.9(3). In the proof on p. 38, formal smoothness comes from the formal-torus description of completed local rings in (6), together with the profinite étale map in (5) (Remark 3.4.10). The printed pointer 'by (4)' does not supply it. Finite type comes from the Raynaud quotient step.

items.name: Existence of IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} (Prop. 3.4.9(4))
items.statement: For every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p), the fpqc quotient of IG_{K^p} by \overline{U_{K_{p,P}}} exists as a p-adic formal scheme, denoted IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}}.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.9(4). The proof is the same as for (1), via Raynaud (1967).

items.name: IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} → IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} is profinite étale with group M_{K_{p,P}} (Prop. 3.4.9(5))
items.statement: For every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P′(Q_p), the map IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} → IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} is a profinite étale map. Its group is \overline{K_{p,P}}/\overline{U_{K_{p,P}}}, i.e. the profinite group K_{p,P}/U_{K_{p,P}}, which is identified with the image of K_{p,P} in M(Q_p). If K_{p,P} = M_{K_{p,P}} ⋉ U_{K_{p,P}}, which is automatic for p > 2, this group is M_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ M(Q_p), as printed in Proposition 3.4.9(5).
items.note: Proposition 3.4.9(5): the quotient by the profinite étale group closure(M_{K_{p,P}}).

items.name: Action of T̂_{K_{p,P}} on IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}}; completions are homogeneous (Prop. 3.4.9(6))
items.statement: For every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P'(Q_p), the action of J_ord on IG_{K^p} induces an action of the formal torus T̂_{K_{p,P}} on IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}}. The formal completions of IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} at closed points are homogeneous spaces under T̂_{K_{p,P}}.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.9(6). The proof uses Serre–Tate local moduli (Katz 1981), which is also missing: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4 plans only the Serre–Tate equivalence. It then passes to the quotient by closure(U_{K_{p,P}})/closure(U_P(Z_p)(1)_n).

items.name: Change of level maps are finite flat and torus-equivariant (Prop. 3.4.9(7))
items.statement: Let K'_{p,P} ⊆ K_{p,P} be compact open subgroups of P'(Q_p). The map IG_{K^pU_{K'_{p,P}}} → IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} is finite flat. It is equivariant for the action of T̂_{K'_{p,P}} on the source, the action of T̂_{K_{p,P}} on the target, and the natural isogeny T̂_{K'_{p,P}} → T̂_{K_{p,P}}. The map IG_{K^pK'_{p,P}} → IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} is also finite flat.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.9(7). The printed text says 'another compact' for another compact open subgroup.

items.name: Completed local rings of Igusa varieties (Remark 3.4.10)
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}}. By Proposition 3.4.9(6), Ô_{IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}}, x} ≅ O_{T̂_{K_{p,P}}} ⊗̂_{Z_p} W(k(x)). By (5), for any closed point x ∈ IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} and any x' ∈ IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} above x, Ô_{IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}, x} ⊗̂_{W(k(x))} W(k(x')) ≃ Ô_{IG_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}}, x'}.
items.note: Remark 3.4.10, checked on the p. 37 image. It is a direct consequence of (5) and (6), both missing.

items.name: Change of level on completions is x_α ↦ x_α^{p^{n_α}} (Remark 3.4.11)
items.statement: Let K'_{p,P} ⊆ K_{p,P} be as in Proposition 3.4.9(7). Assume U_{K_{p,P}} = ∏_{α∈Φ^{+,M}} K_{p,α} is a product over the roots in Φ^{+,M} and U_{K'_{p,P}} = ∏_{α∈Φ^{+,M}} p^{n_α} K_{p,α}. Let x' be a closed point of IG_{K^pK'_{p,P}} mapping to a closed point x ∈ IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}. Then the induced map of formal completions at x' and x is isomorphic to ∏_{α∈Φ^{+,M}} Ĝ_{m,W(k(x'))} → ∏_{α∈Φ^{+,M}} Ĝ_{m,W(k(x))}, (x_α) ↦ (x_α^{p^{n_α}}).
items.note: Remark 3.4.11, checked on the p. 37–38 images; the second product is U_{K'_{p,P}} = ∏ p^{n_α}K_{p,α}. It is consistent with (7): if U_{K_{p,P}} = ∏_α K_{p,α}, then T̂_{K_{p,P}} ≅ ∏_α μ̃_{p^∞}/closure(K_{p,α}) ≅ ∏ Ĝ_m, and the natural isogeny is x_α ↦ x_α^{p^{n_α}}.

items.name: IG_{K^p} as a Frobenius limit over the ordinary locus
items.statement: Take IG_{K^pP'(Z_p)} to be the ordinary locus of the p-adic formal Siegel moduli space of level K^pG(Z_p); it is a smooth formal scheme. Over it, A[p^∞] is an extension 0 → A[p^∞]^m → A[p^∞] → A[p^∞]^e → 0. The pro-étale covering IG_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1)} → IG_{K^pP'(Z_p)} parametrizes isomorphisms x : μ_{p^∞}^g → A[p^∞]^m and y : (Q_p/Z_p)^g → A[p^∞]^e together with c ∈ Z_p^×, such that (x^D, y^D) ∘ λ ∘ (x, y) = c·λ_can. Here λ stands for the map on multiplicative and étale parts deduced from λ : A → A^t. Both spaces carry lifts F of Frobenius, and IG_{K^p} = lim_{×F} IG_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1)}. This limit parametrizes splittings of the connected–étale sequence over IG_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1)}, and so recovers the Igusa formal scheme. Since IG_{K^pP'(Z_p)} is smooth, F is finite flat, and IG_{K^p} → IG_{K^pP'(Z_p)} is profinite flat.
items.locator: proof of Proposition 3.4.9, p. 38; footnote 4, p. 38
items.note: This item needs four missing inputs: the ordinary locus of the p-adic Siegel moduli space; its multiplicative–étale extension (the Pilloni 2020 item on the multiplicative part of a BT group is missing); the pro-étale torsor of trivializations of both parts; and the canonical Frobenius lift F with lim_{×F}, which parametrizes splittings. Footnote 4 (λ on multiplicative and étale parts) was checked on the p. 38 image.

items.name: Serre–Tate local moduli of ordinary abelian varieties
items.statement: The deformation space of a polarized ordinary abelian variety over a perfect field k, with trivialized multiplicative and étale parts of its p-divisible group, is a formal torus. In the setting of IG_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1)}, the action of T̂_{P'(Z_p)} ≅ Ĝ_m ⊗ Sym² Z_p^g on the formal completion at any closed point x is simply transitive. This gives T̂_{P'(Z_p)} ×_{Spf Z_p} Spf W(k(x)) ≃ (IG_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1)})^∧_x, intertwining the Frobenius maps on both sides.
items.note: The formal-torus structure Hom(Sym²T, Ĝ_m) of the deformation space of an ordinary polarized abelian variety is planned nowhere. This includes its simply transitive action at points of the Igusa tower and its compatibility with Frobenius. This is the genus-g form of the Pilloni (2020) item on Serre–Tate local moduli for abelian surfaces, which is missing and routed to A4. External input: [Kat81] N. Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli, in Algebraic Surfaces (Orsay 1976–78), Lecture Notes in Math. 868, Springer (1981), 138–202.

items.name: Quotients by finite flat group schemes
items.statement: Let a finite locally free group scheme H act freely on a (formal) scheme X such that every orbit lies in an affine open. Then the fppf quotient X/H exists, and X → X/H is an H-torsor. The paper uses this for the quotient of IG_{K^pP'(Z_p)_n} by \overline{K_{p,P}}/\overline{P'(Z_p)_n}, and similarly for the unipotent quotients.
items.note: The affine case and the gluing for a finite constant group are planned. Gluing is not planned for a non-constant finite locally free group scheme whose orbits lie in affine opens (Raynaud 1967), nor for the p-adic formal schemes to which the paper applies it. External input: [Ray67] M. Raynaud, Passage au quotient par une relation d'équivalence plate, Proc. Conf. Local Fields (Driebergen 1966), Springer (1967), 78–85.

items.name: Schematic closure of a generic subgroup is finite flat
items.statement: Let H be a finite flat group scheme over Z_p. The schematic closure in H of a closed subgroup scheme of its generic fibre is a finite flat closed subgroup scheme of H.
items.note: The paper applies this to the noncommutative group M(Z/p^nZ) ⋉ μ_{p^n} ⊗ Sym²Z_p^g, so R07.1's statement must not assume commutativity. Over the DVR Z_p, the closure is flat because it is Z_p-torsion free. External input: [Ray74] M. Raynaud, Schémas en groupes de type (p, …, p), Bull. Soc. Math. France 102 (1974), 241–280, §2.

items.name: Smoothness of the hyperspecial-level Siegel moduli space over Z_p
items.statement: Let K^p ⊆ G(A_f^p) be neat. The Siegel moduli space of level K^pG(Z_p), which parametrizes abelian schemes of dimension g with a prime-to-p (quasi-)polarization and a K^p-level structure, is smooth over Z_p by the deformation theory of abelian varieties. In particular the ordinary locus of its p-adic completion, which is IG_{K^pP′(Z_p)}, is a smooth formal scheme.
items.note: Prime-to-p polarization is M2's invertible polarization defect. The consequence for the ordinary locus needs that locus as an open formal subscheme. The Siegel ordinary locus is planned nowhere; it is the base of the Igusa tower, routed with it. The Pilloni (2020) item on smoothness of Y_K is planned at the same layers. External input: Deformation theory of abelian varieties (Serre–Tate, Grothendieck–Messing); the paper gives no reference.

items.name: Igusa varieties over Z_p^cycl
items.statement: IG_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} = IG_{K^p} ×_{Spf Z_p} Spf Z_p^cycl. For any compact open subgroup K_{p,P} of P(Q_p), IG_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} is the quotient of IG_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} by \overline{K_{p,P}}. Over Z_p^cycl, P(Q_p) is identified with P'(Q_p) by a choice of Z_p(1) ≅ Z_p. If K_{p,P} comes from a subgroup of P'(Q_p), then IG_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} = IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} ×_{Spf Z_p} Spf Z_p^cycl.
items.note: §3.4.12, checked on the p. 38 image. This is the base change of the missing Igusa tower, with quotients by subgroups of P(Q_p) that need not be Galois-stable.

items.name: Hecke correspondences on Igusa varieties
items.statement: Let g ∈ M(Q_p) and let K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Q_p) be compact open. Then gK_{p,P}g^{-1} ∩ K_{p,P} is compact open, and the Hecke correspondence is IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} ←(p_2) IG_{K^p(gK_{p,P}g^{-1}∩K_{p,P})} →(p_1) IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}. Here p_1 is induced by the inclusion gK_{p,P}g^{-1} ∩ K_{p,P} ⊆ K_{p,P}. p_2 is the action map [g] : IG_{K^p(gK_{p,P}g^{-1}∩K_{p,P})} → IG_{K^p(K_{p,P}∩g^{-1}K_{p,P}g)} followed by the projection induced by g^{-1}K_{p,P}g ∩ K_{p,P} ⊆ K_{p,P}. The maps p_1 and p_2 are finite flat by Proposition 3.4.9. Over Z_p^cycl one may take any g ∈ P(Q_p) (Remark 3.4.14).
items.note: Hecke correspondences on Igusa varieties at p (g ∈ M(Q_p); any g ∈ P(Q_p) over Z_p^cycl) are missing together with the Igusa varieties. The introduction (§1.3.9, p. 4) singles out the 'privileged' Hecke correspondences IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} ← IG_{K^p(K_{p,P} ∩ tK_{p,P}t^{-1})} → IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}, where g = t ∈ T^+(Q_p) acts through the map T(Q_p) → P′(Q_p) attached to w ∈ ^MW. In the body they appear from §5.1 (p. 53) on, as the correspondences attached to elements of T_w(Q_p)^{++} = wT(Q_p)^{++}w^{-1} (and of T_w(Q_p)^+ in Lemma 5.2.2, p. 54).

items.name: The partial toroidal compactification IG^tor_{K^p,Σ} of IG_{K^p}
items.statement: Let Σ be a K^pG(Z_p)-admissible cone decomposition. IG^tor_{K^pP'(Z_p),Σ} is the ordinary locus in the toroidal compactification of the Siegel variety of level K^pG(Z_p). IG^tor_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1),Σ} → IG^tor_{K^pP'(Z_p),Σ} is the pro-étale torsor of isomorphisms μ_{p^∞}^g → A[p^∞]^m together with c ∈ Z_p^×. This makes sense because the connected part of the p-divisible group extends over the toroidal compactification. Both spaces carry lifts F of Frobenius, and IG^tor_{K^p,Σ} := lim_F IG^tor_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1),Σ}. By construction there is an open immersion IG_{K^p} ↪ IG^tor_{K^p,Σ}.
items.note: The paper calls this a special case of Caraiani–Scholze (2024), §3.2. That source is planned only in the unitary geometric branch of IG.2, whose scope excludes other data. The Siegel ordinary partial toroidal compactification over Z_p, built through the Frobenius limit, is missing. External input: [CS24] A. Caraiani, P. Scholze, On the generic part of the cohomology of non-compact unitary Shimura varieties, Ann. of Math. 199 (2024), §3.2 (this construction is a special case).

items.name: P'(Z_p)-action on IG^tor_{K^p,Σ} and existence of IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P},Σ} (Prop. 3.4.16)
items.statement: IG^tor_{K^p,Σ} carries an action of P'(Z_p) that extends the action on IG_{K^p}. For every (open) subgroup K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Z_p), the categorical quotient of IG^tor_{K^p,Σ} by K_{p,P} exists; it is denoted IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P},Σ}.
items.note: Proposition 3.4.16. The proof uses normality of IG^tor_{K^pU_P(Z_p)(1),Σ}, affineness of the map to IG^tor_{K^pP'(Z_p),Σ}, and finiteness of invariant rings. It is missing together with the partial toroidal Igusa tower.

items.name: Partial toroidal compactification IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}}
items.statement: By construction there is an open immersion IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} ↪ IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P},Σ}, and IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P},Σ} is called a partial toroidal compactification of IG_{K^pK_{p,P}}. Blowing up at the boundary gives such compactifications for more general cone decompositions. From now on the dependence on the cone decomposition is dropped: IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} denotes a partial toroidal compactification for a suitable cone decomposition.
items.note: This is a definition and a convention on the missing objects above. Refinement by blowing up at the boundary follows Lan (2017).

items.name: Independence of coherent cohomology from the cone decomposition
items.statement: Let Σ′ be a refinement of the cone decomposition Σ. The corresponding partial toroidal compactification is obtained from that for Σ by blowing up along the boundary (as in [Lan17]). The coherent cohomology of the automorphic sheaves on these partial toroidal compactifications, namely the canonical extensions of automorphic vector bundles and their subcanonical (cuspidal) versions, does not depend on the choice of the cone decomposition ([Lan17], Prop. 7.5). For this reason the dependence on Σ is dropped from the notation.
items.note: Independence of all coherent cohomology groups needs Rπ_*O = O for refinement maps (Lan 2017, Prop. 7.5). Here it is also needed for partial toroidal compactifications of Igusa varieties. This generalizes the Pilloni (2020) item on independence from the cone decomposition, which is missing and routed to C3; the Calegari–Geraghty (2020) extraction decides the same way. External input: [Lan17] K.-W. Lan, Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2017, no. 11, 3237–3280, Proposition 7.5.

items.name: P(Q_p)-equivariant map from the Igusa tower to the perfectoid Siegel space
items.statement: Work over Z_p^cycl and fix an isomorphism Z_p(1) = Z_p. Let 𝓘𝓖_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} = IG_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} × Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl) be the adic generic fibre. There is a P(Q_p)-equivariant map 𝓘𝓖_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} → S_{K^p} × Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl). It sends A, together with an isomorphism (Q_p/Z_p)^g ⊕ μ_{p^∞}^g → A[p^∞], to the level structure Z_p^g ⊕ Z_p^g(1) = Z_p^{2g} → T_p(A). It induces an injective G(Q_p)-equivariant map 𝓘𝓖_{K^p,Z_p^cycl} ×^{P(Q_p)} G(Q_p) → S_{K^p} × Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl).
items.note: This is the P(Q_p)-equivariant map sending a trivialization (Q_p/Z_p)^g ⊕ μ_{p^∞}^g ≅ A[p^∞] to the level structure Z_p^{2g} ≅ T_p(A), using Z_p(1) = Z_p, and its injective G(Q_p)-equivariant induction. Missing together with the Igusa tower.

items.name: Open immersion 𝓘𝓖_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} → S_{K^pK_p} for K_{p,P} = P(Q_p) ∩ xK_px^{-1}
items.statement: Let x ∈ G(Q_p), let K_p be a compact open subgroup of G(Q_p), and let K_{p,P} = P(Q_p) ∩ xK_px^{-1}. The map 𝓘𝓖_{K^p} ×^{P(Q_p)} G(Q_p) → S_{K^p} × Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl) induces an open immersion 𝓘𝓖_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} →(x) S_{K^pK_p} × Spa(Q_p^cycl, Z_p^cycl).
items.note: §3.4.17. Remark 3.4.18 notes that the map does not descend to Z_p in general. Missing together with the Igusa tower.

items.name: The stacks A_{g,d} ⊇ A_{g,δ}, the groups K_δ and their ordinary loci
items.statement: A_{g,d} → Spec Z is the moduli stack of abelian schemes of dimension g with a polarization of degree d² [dJ93]. Let δ = (δ_1, …, δ_g) be positive integers with δ_1 | δ_2 | ⋯ | δ_g and ∏_{i=1}^g δ_i = d. Let M_δ ∈ GL_{2g}(Q) be the diagonal matrix with entries (δ_1, …, δ_g, 1, …, 1), and K_δ = M_δ GL_{2g}(Ẑ) M_δ^{−1} ∩ G(A_f). A_{g,δ} → A_{g,d} is the substack where the kernel of the polarization is, locally for the fppf topology, isomorphic to ∏_{i=1}^g Z/δ_iZ × μ_{δ_i} [printed 'locally in the étale topology'. The two conditions agree over Z[1/d], but for p | d the étale-local condition need not cut out a locally closed substack; sourceIssues E63]. Then A_{g,δ,Q} = S_{K_δ,Q} (as stacks; K_δ contains −1) and A_{g,d,Q} = ∐_δ S_{K_δ,Q}. 𝔄_{g,d} and 𝔄_{g,δ} are the p-adic formal completions of A_{g,d} and A_{g,δ}, and 𝔄^ord_{g,d} and 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} are their ordinary loci. Then 𝔄^ord_{g,d} and ∐_δ 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} have the same underlying topological space [printed as an equality 𝔄^ord_{g,d} = ∐_δ 𝔄^ord_{g,δ}, which can fail as an equality of formal schemes when g ≥ 2; sourceIssues E63]; on the ordinary locus the p-part of δ is read off from the étale quotient of the p-primary part of the kernel of the polarization.
items.note: Four things are not planned: de Jong's stack A_{g,d} over Z for all d, including p | d; its locally closed substacks A_{g,δ} by the fppf-local type of ker λ; the groups K_δ = M_δGL_{2g}(Ẑ)M_δ^{-1} ∩ G(A_f) with A_{g,δ,Q} = S_{K_δ,Q}; and the ordinary loci of the p-adic completions. Checked: the form restricted to M_δZ^{2g} has type δ, so K_δ is the stabilizer of a lattice of the right type. The paper calls A_{g,δ} a locally closed substack of A_{g,d} (p. 40); with the printed étale-local condition this can fail when p | d (sourceIssues E63). The decomposition A_{g,d,Q} = ∐_δ S_{K_δ,Q} is asserted without proof ('We also see easily', p. 40). External input: [dJ93] A. J. de Jong, The moduli spaces of polarized abelian varieties, Math. Ann. 295 (1993), 485–503.

items.name: 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} is an Igusa variety (Lemma 3.4.20)
items.statement: Let A_{g,δ} be defined by the fppf-local condition of §3.4.19 [the paper prints an étale-local condition, under which the lemma can fail when p divides some δ_i; sourceIssues E63]. Then 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} = IG_{K_{δ,P}}, where K_{δ,P} = K^p_δ(K_{δ,p} ∩ P(Q_p)). Here K_{δ,p} ∩ P(Q_p) = (K_{δ,p} ∩ M(Q_p)) ⋉ (K_{δ,p} ∩ U_P(Q_p)) is a semi-direct product, so it defines a compact open subgroup of P′(Q_p). Since K^p_δ contains −1 and is not neat, both sides are formal algebraic stacks. That is, 𝔄^ord_{g,δ} is the Igusa formal stack IG_{K^pK_{p,P}} with K^p = K^p_δ and K_{p,P} = K_{δ,p} ∩ P(Q_p).
items.note: Lemma 3.4.20 ('Clear from the definition'). For p | δ_i the polarization is not prime to p, so it uses the quasi-isogeny formulation of the Igusa moduli problem. Missing together with the Igusa tower and A_{g,δ}.

items.name: Integral models S_{K^pK_p} and S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} by normalization
items.statement: Fix K = K_pK^p. Choose positive integers d_1, …, d_r, sequences δ_i = (δ_{i,1}, …, δ_{i,g}) as in §3.4.19 with ∏_j δ_{i,j} = d_i, and maps K ↪ K_{δ_i} given by conjugation by elements of G(A_f) followed by inclusion. These induce finite maps S_{K^pK_p,Q} → ∏_{i=1}^r A_{g,d_i,Q}. S_{K^pK_p} → Spec Z_p is the normalization of ∏_{i=1}^r A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p in S_{K^pK_p,Q_p}. In general S_{K^pK_p} depends on the choice of the auxiliary spaces A_{g,d_i} (Remark 3.4.21). Similarly, S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} → Spec Z_p^cycl is the normalization of ∏_{i=1}^r A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p^cycl in S_{K^pK_p,Q_p^cycl}. The natural map S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} → S_{K^pK_p} ×_{Spec Z_p} Spec Z_p^cycl is in general not an isomorphism (Remark 3.4.22).
items.note: M4 covers the choice r = 1, d_1 = 1 after conjugating K_p into G(Z_p). The paper allows auxiliary stacks A_{g,d_i} with p | d_i, which are not good-level models. It also uses the separate normalization over Z_p^cycl, which by Remark 3.4.22 is not the base change. M4 does not state these, and they need the missing A_{g,d}. The paper presents this as the standard method of obtaining integral models of Shimura varieties of deep level by normalization, following for example Lan (2016, Compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties in ramified characteristics) and Madapusi Pera (2019, Toroidal compactifications of integral models of Shimura varieties of Hodge type) (§3.4.19, p. 39). External input: [Lan16] K.-W. Lan, Compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties in ramified characteristics, Forum Math. Sigma 4 (2016), e1; [MP19] K. Madapusi Pera, Toroidal compactifications of integral models of Shimura varieties of Hodge type, Ann. Sci. ÉNS 52 (2019) (the standard method followed).

items.name: Integral toroidal compactifications S^tor_{K^pK_p} by normalization
items.statement: Consider a finite map S^tor_{K^pK_p,Q} → ∏_{i=1}^r A^tor_{g,d_i,Q}. S^tor_{K^pK_p} → Spec Z_p is the normalization of ∏_{i=1}^r A^tor_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p in S^tor_{K^pK_p,Q_p}. A similar variant exists over Z_p^cycl.
items.note: The construction needs toroidal compactifications A^tor_{g,d} of the auxiliary stacks, possibly with p | d, and normalization in S^tor_{K,Q_p}. Neither is planned in this generality.

items.name: Igusa varieties are open formal subschemes of the integral models (Lemma 3.4.24)
items.statement: Let x, K_p and K_{p,P} = P(Q_p) ∩ xK_px^{-1} be as in §3.4.17. The open immersion 𝓘𝓖_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} →(x) S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} of adic generic fibres comes from an open immersion of formal schemes IG_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} ↪ 𝔖_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl}, where 𝔖_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} is the p-adic completion of the normalization model S_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl}. In particular, although the integral model depends on the auxiliary choices, this part of its ordinary locus does not.
items.note: Lemma 3.4.24. Its proof: the maps to ∏ 𝔄^ord_{g,δ_i} are finite and the source is normal by Proposition 3.4.9. Proposition 3.4.9 covers only levels that come from P′(Q_p); for other K_{p,P} the normality of the source needs a Z_p^cycl version of it, which the paper does not state (sourceIssues E59). Missing together with the Igusa tower and the normalization models. Lemma 4.1.7 (p. 41) applies the lemma with x = w ∈ ^MW and K_p = K_{p,n}, the group of matrices in G(Z_p) that reduce modulo p^n into B(Z/p^nZ). It identifies the open formal subscheme 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} of the Iwahori-level model with 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P,w}}, where K_{p,P,w} = wK_{p,n}w^{-1} ∩ P(Q_p), and notes that there the embedding is defined over Z_p, not only over Z_p^cycl.

items.name: The Iwahori subgroups K_{p,n}
items.statement: For n ∈ Z_{≥0}, K_{p,n} ⊆ G(Q_p) is the subgroup of matrices in G(Z_p) whose reduction modulo p^n lies in B(Z/p^nZ), where B is the Borel subgroup of §3.1.
items.note: For n = 1, K_{p,1} is the Iwahori subgroup attached to the paper's Borel B ⊆ P, a parahoric of RG2.3. For n ≥ 2 it is the preimage of B(Z/p^nZ) under reduction G(Z_p) → G(Z/p^nZ), a direct definition from RG2.0's integral points. For n = 0 it is G(Z_p). The extraction of Calegari–Geraghty (2020) marks its GSp4 Iwahori planned at RG2.3.

items.name: Toroidal extension of the Igusa open immersion (with Remark 3.4.25)
items.statement: For suitable choices of cone decompositions, the open immersion of Lemma 3.4.24 extends to an open immersion 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P},Z_p^cycl} ↪ 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_p,Z_p^cycl} of (partial) toroidal compactifications. In general it does not descend to a map 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} ↪ 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_p} over Z_p (Remark 3.4.25).
items.note: Missing. No layer extends the open immersion of Lemma 3.4.24 to partial toroidal compactifications, for suitable cone decompositions. No layer records Remark 3.4.25 either: in general the toroidal immersion does not descend from Z_p^cycl to Z_p. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration IG.2 plans partial toroidal compactifications of Igusa varieties ('construct their partial toroidal/minimal compactifications') only for the unitary central-leaf Igusa varieties of Caraiani–Scholze. The generic-fibre toroidal compactifications and their refinements are ShimuraCompactifications C2–C3.

items.name: Integral model S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} of Iwahori level p^n
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},Q_p} be a toroidal compactification of the Siegel moduli space of level K_{p,n}K^p over Q_p. Away from the boundary there is a self-dual chain of isogenies A = A_g → A_{g+1} → ⋯ → A_{2g} → A_1 → ⋯ → A_g = A. Its composite A → A is multiplication by p^n, and for 0 ≤ i ≤ g the group Ker(A_g → A_{g+i}) is a totally isotropic subgroup of A[p^n] that is étale-locally isomorphic to (Z/p^nZ)^i. For 1 ≤ i ≤ g, A_{g+i} carries a polarization of degree p^{2ng−2in} = d_i², i.e. d_i = p^{n(g−i)}; put d_0 = 1. This gives a map S_{K^pK_{p,n},Q} → ∏_{i=0}^g A_{g,d_i}. S_{K^pK_{p,n}} → Spec Z_p is defined as the normalization of ∏_{i=0}^g A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p in S_{K^pK_{p,n},Q_p}, and S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} is constructed in the same way (§3.4.19, §3.4.23). For n = 1, S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1}} is the usual integral model of Iwahori level (Remark 4.1.2).
items.note: Missing. The generic-fibre Siegel moduli at level K_{p,n}K^p and its toroidal compactifications over Q_p are planned (PELModuli M1–M3, ShimuraCompactifications C2–C3). The following are planned nowhere: the description away from the boundary by a self-dual chain of isogenies A_g → ⋯ → A_{2g} → A_1 → ⋯ → A_g whose composite is p^n; the integral model obtained by normalizing ∏_{i=0}^g A_{g,d_i} × Spec Z_p; and its toroidal version. For n = 1 this is the usual Iwahori-level model (Remark 4.1.2). The item generalises the Klingen-level model X_{Kli(p)K} of Pilloni (Duke 2020), which comes with its chain G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G, to GSp_{2g} at Iwahori level p^n.

items.name: Chain of isogenies of semi-abelian schemes over S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}
items.statement: Over the integral model S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} of §4.1.1 there is a chain of isogenies of semi-abelian schemes A = A_g → A_{g+1} → ⋯ → A_{2g} → A_1 → ⋯ → A_g = A. It extends the chain over the generic interior, and its composite A → A is multiplication by p^n.
items.note: Missing. Two inputs are both missing: the normalized toroidal model S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, and the extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes over a normal base (Faltings–Chai I, Prop. 2.7). The extension of the chain from the generic interior to semi-abelian isogenies over S^tor, with composite p^n, is therefore planned nowhere. ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans the universal semi-abelian scheme only over good-level integral toroidal compactifications. External input: [FC90] G. Faltings, C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties, Ergeb. Math. Grenzgeb. (3) 22, Springer 1990, Chap. I, Prop. 2.7

items.name: Extension of homomorphisms of semi-abelian schemes over a normal base ([FC90] I, Prop. 2.7)
items.statement: As used in §4.1.1 and Lemma 4.2.2: over a normal noetherian base scheme, a homomorphism (hence a quasi-isogeny) between semi-abelian schemes that is given over a dense open subscheme extends uniquely over the whole base.
items.note: Missing. ShimuraCompactifications C4 plans semi-abelian schemes ('Construct semi-abelian schemes, their character groups, extensions of abelian schemes by tori, biextensions, and the degeneration data'). NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1 plans the Néron-model extension over Dedekind bases ('Prove uniqueness and functorial extension of homomorphisms'). No layer plans the extension, unique over a normal noetherian base, of a homomorphism of semi-abelian schemes given over a dense open (Faltings–Chai, Chap. I, Prop. 2.7). Neither library has semi-abelian schemes. External input: [FC90] G. Faltings, C.-L. Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties, Springer 1990, Chap. I, Prop. 2.7

items.name: Flag H_{g+1} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ H_g = A[p^n] and graded pieces Gr_i
items.statement: Let 0 ⊆ H_{g+1} ⊆ H_{g+2} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ H_{2g} = H_{2g}^⊥ ⊆ H_1 ⊆ H_2 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ H_g = A[p^n] be the full flag of subgroups of A[p^n] given by the kernels H_j = Ker(A → A_j) of the maps in the chain of isogenies. Let Gr_j = H_j/H_{j−1} for 1 ≤ j ≤ 2g, where the predecessor is taken in the order g+1, …, 2g, 1, …, g: so Gr_{g+1} = H_{g+1} and Gr_1 = H_1/H_{2g}. Over the interior of the Shimura variety the Gr_j are finite flat group schemes of order p^n, and Gr_{2g−j+1} = Gr_j^D (Cartier dual).
items.note: Missing. Cartier duality of finite flat group schemes is planned (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1). Tau Ceti has it over affine bases (tauceti:FiniteLocallyFreeCommAffineGroupSchemeCat.cartierDual). No layer defines the full flag of kernels H_j = Ker(A → A_j) of the Iwahori-level chain, its graded pieces Gr_j (finite flat of order p^n over the interior), or the duality Gr_{2g+1−j} = Gr_j^D coming from the self-duality of the chain. It generalises to a full flag of A[p^n] the subgroup H ⊂ G[p] and its orthogonal H^⊥ at the Klingen level of Pilloni (Duke 2020).

items.name: Strata S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w} indexed by w ∈ ^MW
items.statement: Let S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p} be the special fibre. For w ∈ ^MW, S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w} is the locus where Gr_{w^{-1}(i)} is a multiplicative group scheme for i = g+1, …, 2g. Notation (§3.1): W is realized as the permutations w of {1, …, 2g} with w(i) + w(2g+1−i) = 2g+1, and ^MW is the set of w with w^{-1}(g+1) < ⋯ < w^{-1}(2g) (the minimal length representatives of W_M\W). To w one attaches (w_1, …, w_g) with w_0 = 0, where w_i − w_{i−1} = 1 if g+i ∈ w^{-1}{g+1, …, 2g} and w_i − w_{i−1} = 0 otherwise. By Cartier duality, on S_{F_p,w} each Gr_{g+i} (1 ≤ i ≤ g) is multiplicative if w_i − w_{i−1} = 1 and étale if w_i − w_{i−1} = 0.
items.note: Missing. No layer plans strata of the special fibre by the étale or multiplicative type of the graded pieces Gr_j, indexed by the Kostant representatives ^MW of §3.1. No layer plans the Weyl group of GSp_{2g} as signed permutations with its minimal-length representatives of W_M\W either; Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups Layer 7 plans Weyl groups in general. The reformulation in terms of Gr_{g+i} was checked by direct computation from w(i) + w(2g+1−i) = 2g+1 and Gr_{2g+1−j} = Gr_j^D: Gr_{g+i} is multiplicative exactly when g+i ∈ w^{-1}{g+1,…,2g}, that is when w_i − w_{i−1} = 1, as the proof of Lemma 4.1.6 (p. 41) records. The item generalises the multiplicative/étale loci of Pilloni (Duke 2020, §10.2) from GSp4 to GSp_{2g}.

items.name: Remark 4.1.4: S_{F_p,w} lies in the ordinary locus, strictly unless n = 1
