items.statement: For n ≥ 1 and w ∈ ^MW, S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w} is contained in the ordinary locus. Unless n = 1, the ordinary locus is strictly bigger than ∪_{w∈^MW} S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w}.
items.note: Missing. The strata S_{F_p,w} and the ordinary locus of the Iwahori-level model are both missing (see the strata S_{F_p,w}), and so is Remark 4.1.4: each stratum lies in the ordinary locus, and for n ≥ 2 the union of the strata is strictly smaller than the ordinary locus.

items.name: 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w}, their adic spaces, and π_{HT,K_{p,n}}
items.statement: 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} is the p-adic formal completion of S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, and 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} (w ∈ ^MW) is its open formal subscheme with underlying space S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w}. 𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} is the associated adic space over Spa(Q_p, Z_p), and 𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} is the adic space of 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w}. There is a set-theoretic map π_{HT,K_{p,n}}: |𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}| → |FL|/K_{p,n}, FL = P\G, obtained by passing the Hodge–Tate period map of §3.3 to the quotient.
items.note: Missing. Formal completion and the adic generic fibre are planned (AdicSpacesPartII R2). So is the Hodge–Tate period map with its toroidal extension: PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S3 ('Construct the Hodge–Tate period map on the open perfectoid tower') and S6 ('construct the Hodge–Tate map from the toroidal tower diamond ... via Boxer–Pilloni Theorem 4.4.40'). Two things are planned nowhere. The first is the set-theoretic quotient map π_{HT,K_{p,n}}: |𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}| → |FL|/K_{p,n}, FL = P\G, of Boxer–Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory (arXiv:2110.10251), §4.5. The second is the open formal subschemes 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} of the Iwahori-level model, which is itself missing, with their adic spaces. External input: [BP21] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory (2021), arXiv:2110.10251, §4.5 (Hodge–Tate period map at finite level)

items.name: Lemma 4.1.6: the Hodge–Tate fibre over w·K_{p,n}
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW, π^{-1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(w·K_{p,n}) is the closure of 𝒮^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w}.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.1.6 (p. 41) identifies the fibre of π_{HT,K_{p,n}} over w·K_{p,n} with the closure of 𝒮^tor_w. Its proof reads off, on π_HT^{-1}(w), which Gr_{g+i} are multiplicative, using Lie_A(1) = ⟨e_{w^{-1}(i)}, g+1 ≤ i ≤ 2g⟩. Every object in the statement is missing (see the formal and adic strata).

items.name: Lemma 4.1.7: 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} is a formal Igusa variety
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW, 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} = 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K_{p,P,w}K^p}, where K_{p,P,w} = wK_{p,n}w^{-1} ∩ P(Q_p). The identification is defined over Z_p, not only over Z_p^cycl.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.1.7 (p. 41) follows from Lemma 3.4.24 and adds that the identification 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w} = 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K_{p,P,w}K^p} is defined over Z_p, not only over Z_p^cycl. Its inputs, the Siegel Igusa varieties and the Iwahori-level model, are missing. For GSp4 at Klingen level, Pilloni (Duke 2020, §9.1) identifies the ordinary Klingen locus with an Igusa tower; this lemma is the GSp_{2g} Iwahori-level counterpart.

items.name: Fargues' divisor D_H of a generically étale finite flat group scheme
items.statement: To a finite flat group scheme H that is generically étale over a p-adic base, Fargues attaches an effective Cartier divisor D_H, whose complement is the locus where H is étale. For H of order p^h one has D_H + D_{H^D} = V(p^h). Over a complete valuation ring V with rank-one valuation v normalized by v(p) = 1, D_H = (x) with x ∈ V, and deg H := v(x).
items.note: Missing. Neither library defines Fargues's divisor or degree of a finite flat group scheme. HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 plans 'the relevant Hodge ideal, invariant under duality where used'. The extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) routes Fargues's degree over O_K to T0 by a source route: definition, additivity, deg G + deg G^D = height, and growth along generic isomorphisms. This paper also needs the divisor D_H of a generically étale finite flat H over a general p-adic base (Fargues, Crelle 645, 2010, §2, Déf. 3), whose complement is the étale locus, and the identity D_H + D_{H^D} = V(p^h) (Lemme 3). External input: [Far10] L. Fargues, La filtration de Harder–Narasimhan des schémas en groupes finis et plats, J. Reine Angew. Math. 645 (2010), 1–39, §2, Déf. 3 and Lemme 3

items.name: Cartier divisors D_i (1 ≤ i ≤ 2g) on S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}
items.statement: For 1 ≤ i ≤ 2g, D_i is the effective Cartier divisor on S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} attached to the generically étale finite flat group scheme Gr_i as in [Far10], §2, Déf. 3. The complement of D_i is the locus where Gr_i is étale, and D_i + D_{2g+1−i} = V(p^n).
items.note: Missing. The divisors D_i = D_{Gr_i} on the Iwahori-level model depend on the missing flag Gr_i and on Fargues's divisor (see those items). One point must be settled wherever these divisors are planned. §4.1.1 (p. 41) asserts finite flatness of Gr_i only over the interior, while §4.1.8 uses D_i, and D_i + D_{2g+1−i} = V(p^n), on all of S^tor. The text does not say how D_i is defined along the toroidal boundary. External input: [Far10] §2, Déf. 3 and Lemme 3

items.name: Lemma 4.1.9 (1): S_{F_p,w} as a complement of divisors
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW, S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w} = S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p} \ (D_{w^{-1}(1)} ∪ ⋯ ∪ D_{w^{-1}(g)}), the complement of the support of Σ_{i=1}^g D_{w^{-1}(i)}.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.1.9 (1) (p. 41) says that S_{F_p,w} is the complement of the support of Σ_{i=1}^g D_{w^{-1}(i)}, that is, the locus where Gr_{w^{-1}(i)} is étale for i ≤ g; by duality this is the locus where Gr_{w^{-1}(i)} is multiplicative for i > g. It depends on the missing strata and divisors D_i.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.9 (2): ∪_w S_{F_p,w} = complement of ∪_i (D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i})
items.statement: ∪_{w∈^MW} S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w} = S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p} \ ∪_{i=1}^g (D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}); that is, the union of the strata is the locus where every Gr_i is étale or multiplicative.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.1.9 (2) (p. 41) says that the union of the strata is the complement of ∪_{i=1}^g (D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}); the paper prints the sum Σ_{i=1}^g D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}, meaning the union of supports. It depends on the missing strata and divisors.

items.name: Proposition-construction 4.1.11: blowing up to separate two Cartier divisors
items.statement: Let X̄ be a scheme and D_1, D_2 effective Cartier divisors on X̄. Let p: X̃ → X̄ be the blow-up along the ideal generated by O_X̄(−D_1) and O_X̄(−D_2). There are effective Cartier divisors D'_1, D'_2 on X̃ with disjoint supports such that p^*D_1 + D'_2 = p^*D_2 + D'_1. Locally, with X̄ = Spec A, D_i = V(x_i), I = (x_1, x_2) and X̃ = Proj ⊕_n I^n, D'_i is the divisor of the section x'_i of O_X̃(1) given by x_i ∈ I in degree 1. Then x'_1x_2 = x'_2x_1 and V(x'_1, x'_2) = Proj(⊕_n I^n/(x_1, x_2)I^{n−1}) = ∅.
items.note: Missing. Blow-ups themselves are planned. Tau Ceti StableReduction Layer 4 has 'Construct the Rees algebra and the blowup of a quasi-coherent finite-type ideal as a relative Proj. Prove the universal property ... exceptional divisor, strict transform, and affine chart descriptions'. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.7a has 'Construct blowups by the Rees algebra with their projective universal property, affine charts, strict/total/controlled transforms'. Mathlib has the Rees algebra (mathlib:reesAlgebra) and the projective spectrum of a graded ring, but no blow-up of a scheme. The separation statement is stated nowhere. It asserts effective Cartier divisors D'_1, D'_2 with disjoint supports and p^*D_1 + D'_2 = p^*D_2 + D'_1, with D'_i the divisor of the section x'_i of O(1). It follows from the affine charts and the invertibility of the exceptional ideal.

items.name: Partial sums Z_k = D_{g+1} + ⋯ + D_{g+k}
items.statement: For 0 ≤ k ≤ g, Z_k = Σ_{i=1}^k D_{g+i} (Z_0 = 0), an effective Cartier divisor on S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} supported in the special fibre. This is used implicitly in the proofs of Cor. 4.2.10 and Props. 4.2.14–4.2.15. Let V be a complete rank-one valuation ring with v(p) = 1, and let x̃: Spec V → S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} be a point along which H_{g+1} ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ H_{g+k} pull back to finite flat group schemes with graded pieces x̃^*Gr_{g+i} (for example, x̃ avoids the boundary). Then x̃^*Z_k = (x) with v(x) = Σ_{i=1}^k deg x̃^*Gr_{g+i} = deg x̃^*H_{g+k}.
items.note: Missing. Z_k = D_{g+1} + ⋯ + D_{g+k} is built from the missing divisors D_i. Its degree over a rank-one valuation ring equals deg H_{g+k}; this uses additivity of Fargues's degree (see the Fargues items). The definition in §4.1.12 (p. 42) is misprinted as 'Z_i = Σ_{i=1}^k D_{g+i}'; §4.2.9 (p. 45) restates it correctly.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.13 (1): the blow-up S̃^tor and the divisors Z_{i,>j}, Z_{i,<j}
items.statement: There is a blow-up S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} → S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} such that for all 0 ≤ i ≤ g and all 0 ≤ j ≤ i there are effective Cartier divisors Z_{i,>j}, Z_{i,<j} on S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} with disjoint supports and Z_{i,>j} − Z_{i,<j} = Z_i − V(p^{nj}) (pull-backs to S̃). It is constructed as a tower S̃_g → S̃_{g−1} → ⋯ → S̃_1 = S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, where S̃_{k+1} → S̃_k is obtained by applying Proposition-construction 4.1.11 to the pairs (Z_{k+1}, V(p^{nj})) for 0 ≤ j ≤ k+1; then S̃^tor = S̃_g.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.1.13 (1) (p. 42) builds the tower of blow-ups S̃_g → ⋯ → S̃_1 = S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} by applying Proposition-construction 4.1.11 to the pairs (Z_{k+1}, V(p^{nj})). This is paper-specific geometry on the missing Iwahori-level model. It has no counterpart in Pilloni (Duke 2020), where the Klingen-level spaces need no such modification.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.13 (2): the open subsets S̃_{=j_1,…,=j_k}
items.statement: Let 1 ≤ k ≤ g and let 0 ≤ j_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ j_k be integers with j_i ≤ i. Put S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},=j_1,…,=j_k} = ∩_{i=1}^k (Z^c_{i,>j_i} ∩ Z^c_{i,<j_i}). This is an open subset of S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, on which Z_i = V(p^{nj_i}) for 1 ≤ i ≤ k. It contains the whole generic fibre, and its special fibre is empty unless j_i − j_{i−1} ∈ {0, 1} for 1 ≤ i ≤ k (j_0 = 0). For k = g, the map S̃_{=j_1,…,=j_g} → S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} is an open immersion. Its image is the open subscheme where, for each 1 ≤ i ≤ g, Gr_{g+i} is multiplicative if j_i − j_{i−1} = 1 and étale if j_i − j_{i−1} = 0; this constrains only the special fibre. For general k, the same holds for the analogous open subset S̃_{k,=j_1,…,=j_k} of the k-th intermediate blow-up S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},k}, with conditions on Gr_{g+i} for 1 ≤ i ≤ k only.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.1.13 (2) (p. 42) concerns the opens S̃_{=j_1,…,=j_k} of the blow-up: they are empty unless j_i − j_{i−1} ∈ {0,1}, they map by open immersions to S^tor, and their images are described by the types of the Gr_{g+i}. The proof passes through the intermediate blow-ups S̃_k. Everything in the statement is missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.1.13 (3): Z_{k+1,>j_k} and Z_{k+1,<j_k+1} over S̃_{=j_1,…,=j_k}
items.statement: For 1 ≤ k ≤ g−1 and j_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ j_k as in (2), over S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},=j_1,…,=j_k} one has Z_{k+1,>j_k} = D_{g+k+1} and Z_{k+1,<j_k+1} = D_{g−k} = V(p^n) − D_{g+k+1}.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.1.13 (3) (p. 42) states Z_{k+1,>j_k} = D_{g+k+1} and Z_{k+1,<j_k+1} = D_{g−k} = V(p^n) − D_{g+k+1}; D_{g−k} is the divisor dual to D_{g+k+1}. The proof misprints the second as '−D_{g−k−1}'. The statement depends on the missing blow-up and divisors.

items.name: Corollary 4.1.14: S̃_{=w_1,…,=w_g} ≅ an open of S^tor with special fibre S_{F_p,w}
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW with attached sequence (w_1, …, w_g) (§3.1). The map S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},=w_1,…,=w_g} → S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} is an open immersion, and S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},=w_1,…,=w_g} × Spec F_p identifies with S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w}.
items.note: Missing. Corollary 4.1.14 (p. 42) specializes Proposition 4.1.13 (2) to the sequence (w_1,…,w_g) of w ∈ ^MW (§3.1); every object in it is missing.

items.name: Convention: S^tor denotes the blow-up S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}
items.statement: From the paragraph following Corollary 4.1.14 on, S^tor denotes S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}}, and the level is dropped from other spaces. S^tor_{F_p,w} := S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},F_p,w}, viewed inside S^tor via Cor. 4.1.14. 𝔖^tor_w := 𝔖^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},w}, an open formal subscheme of the p-adic completion 𝔖^tor of S^tor.
items.note: Missing. This is a notational convention on the missing blow-up S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} and its opens. It fixes the model on which the later cohomology and control theorems (§4.4 onwards) are stated.

items.name: Remark 4.1.15: blow-ups with centre away from ∪_w S_{F_p,w}
items.statement: Any further blow-up of S^tor whose centre is disjoint from ∪_{w} S^tor_{F_p,w} would still satisfy a version of the control theorem 4.5.2, which relates the ordinary part of the integral cohomology over S^tor to the ordinary cohomology of the ordinary locus.
items.note: Missing. Remark 4.1.15 (p. 43) asserts without proof that the control theorem 4.5.2 survives any further blow-up with centre disjoint from ∪_w S^tor_{F_p,w}. It depends on the missing model and on the control theorem of §4.5.

items.name: Closed subsets Z_{>w−1} of the special fibre
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW with sequence (w_1, …, w_g), Z_{>w−1} = ∩_{i=1}^g Z_{i,>w_i−1}. This is a closed subset of S^tor_{F_p}, an intersection of supports, with the convention Z_{i,>−1} := S^tor_{F_p} for the indices with w_i = 0.
items.note: Missing. The closed sets Z_{>w−1} = ∩_i Z_{i,>w_i−1} (§4.1.16, p. 43) are intersections of supports of the missing divisors Z_{i,>j}. The case w_i = 0 needs the stated convention Z_{i,>−1} = S^tor_{F_p}, since Proposition 4.1.13 defines Z_{i,>j} only for 0 ≤ j ≤ i.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.17 (1): monotonicity in j
items.statement: For 0 ≤ i ≤ g and 0 ≤ j, j' ≤ i: Z_{i,>j} ≤ Z_{i,>j'} if j' ≤ j, and Z_{i,<j} ≤ Z_{i,<j'} if j' ≥ j.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.1.17 (1) (p. 43) is proved from Z_{i,>j} − Z_{i,<j} = Z_i − V(p^{nj}) and the disjointness of supports. It concerns the missing divisors of Proposition 4.1.13.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.17 (2): Z_{>w−1} ⊆ Z_{>w'−1} for w ≤ w'
items.statement: For w, w' ∈ ^MW with w ≤ w' in the Bruhat order, Z_{>w−1} ⊆ Z_{>w'−1}.
items.note: Missing. Tau Ceti has the Bruhat order on a Coxeter group (tauceti:CoxeterSystem.BruhatLE). The proof of Lemma 4.1.17 (2) (p. 43) uses that w ≤ w′ in the Bruhat order on ^MW forces w′_i ≤ w_i for all i; the proof words this as 'w′ ≤ w implies w′_i ≥ w_i'. This fact about the sequences attached to Kostant representatives of the Siegel parabolic is planned nowhere, and neither are the sets Z_{>w−1}.

items.name: Filtration F_{−1} = ∅ ⊆ F_0 ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ F_{g(g+1)/2} = S^tor_{F_p}
items.statement: For 0 ≤ i ≤ g(g+1)/2, F_i = ∪_{w∈^MW, ℓ(w) ≤ i} Z_{>w−1}, and F_{−1} = ∅. This is an increasing filtration of S^tor_{F_p} by closed subsets, with F_{g(g+1)/2} = S^tor_{F_p}.
items.note: Missing. The filtration F_i = ∪_{ℓ(w)≤i} Z_{>w−1} (p. 43) is built from the missing sets Z_{>w−1}. The endpoints were checked by direct computation. The identity of ^MW has w_i = i, so F_0 = ∩_i Z_{i,>i−1}. The longest element of ^MW has length g(g+1)/2 and all w_i = 0, so F_{g(g+1)/2} = S^tor_{F_p}.

items.name: Lemma 4.1.18: strata of the filtration
items.statement: For 0 ≤ i ≤ g(g+1)/2, F_i \ F_{i−1} = ∐_{w∈^MW, ℓ(w)=i} ∩_{j=1}^g (Z_{j,>w_j−1} ∩ Z^c_{j,>w_j}). Moreover S^tor_{F_p,w} ⊆ ∩_{j=1}^g (Z_{j,>w_j−1} ∩ Z^c_{j,>w_j}) for each w ∈ ^MW. Here Z_{j,>−1}, which occurs when w_j = 0, is the whole special fibre S^tor_{F_p} [the paper defines Z_{j,>m} only for 0 ≤ m ≤ j (Proposition 4.1.13(1)); sourceIssues E76].
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.1.18 and the sentence after it (p. 43, 'This follows easily from the definitions') describe F_i \ F_{i−1} as a disjoint union over ℓ(w) = i. They underlie the Cousin complex of §4.4 onwards. Everything in the statement is missing. The paper uses the letter i both for the filtration index and for the index of the intersection; the statement writes j for the latter (sourceIssues E74). Lemma 4.5.7 (p. 52) restates the result as F_i ∖ F_{i−1} = ∐_{ℓ(w)=i} (Z_{>w−1} ∖ D_{−,w}), where Z_{>w−1} = ∩_j Z_{j,>w_j−1} and D_{−,w} = Σ_j Z_{j,>w_j}, and proves it by citing Lemma 4.1.18. The two descriptions agree because the support of D_{−,w} is ∪_j Z_{j,>w_j}. Lemma 4.5.7 is used in the proof of Theorem 4.5.2 (§4.5.6, p. 52) to write each term RΓ_c(F̂_p ∖ F̂_{p−1}, ω̃^κ) of the spectral sequence of Theorem 2.9.7 for this filtration as a direct sum over the w with ℓ(w) = p.

items.name: Hecke correspondence C^tor_t and its integral model
items.statement: For t ∈ T^+(Q_p), let C^tor_{t,Q_p} = S^tor_{(tK_{p,n}t^{-1} ∩ K_{p,n})K^p,Q_p,Σ'} for a suitable cone decomposition Σ'. Let p_1 × p_2: C^tor_{t,Q_p} → S^tor_{Q_p} × S^tor_{Q_p} be the Hecke correspondence attached to K_{p,n}tK_{p,n}, which is finite for good choices of cone decompositions. C^tor_t is the normalization of S^tor × S^tor in C^tor_{t,Q_p}; here S^tor is the blown-up Iwahori model over Z_p.
items.note: Missing. The generic-fibre toroidal Hecke correspondence C^tor_{t,Q_p} with finite p_1 × p_2 is planned in ShimuraCompactifications C3 ('For a morphism of data or a Hecke translation, choose compatible source and target fans and construct the extension'). Relative normalization is in Mathlib (mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.normalization). The integral model C^tor_t, the normalization of S^tor × S^tor over the missing blown-up Iwahori model, is planned nowhere. It generalises to GSp_{2g} the integral Klingen-level U-correspondences of Pilloni (Duke 2020, §§10.2, 14.2).

items.name: Lemma 4.2.2: the universal quasi-isogeny extends over C^tor_t
items.statement: The universal quasi-isogeny p_1^*A → p_2^*A over C^tor_{t,Q_p} extends uniquely to a quasi-isogeny p_1^*A → p_2^*A of semi-abelian schemes over C^tor_t.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.2.2 (p. 43) applies Faltings–Chai I, Prop. 2.7 to the normal scheme C^tor_t. Both are missing (see those items). External input: [FC90] I, Prop. 2.7

items.name: Formal Hecke correspondences 𝔆^tor_t and 𝔆^tor_{t,w}
items.statement: 𝔆^tor_t is the p-adic formal completion of C^tor_t. For w ∈ ^MW, 𝔆^tor_{t,w} = p_1^{-1}𝔖^tor_w ∩ p_2^{-1}𝔖^tor_w. This gives a correspondence p_1, p_2: 𝔆^tor_{t,w} → 𝔖^tor_w (t ∈ T^+(Q_p)).
items.note: Missing. 𝔆^tor_t and 𝔆^tor_{t,w} = p_1^{-1}𝔖^tor_w ∩ p_2^{-1}𝔖^tor_w are built from the missing C^tor_t and strata 𝔖^tor_w. Formal completion itself is planned (AdicSpacesPartII R2).

items.name: Proposition 4.2.4: 𝔆^tor_{t,w} is the Igusa Hecke correspondence for w(t)
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p), w ∈ ^MW, w(t) = wtw^{-1} ∈ T(Q_p) ⊆ M(Q_p), and K_{p,P,w} = wK_{p,n}w^{-1} ∩ P(Q_p). Under 𝔖^tor_w ≃ 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K_{p,P,w}K^p} (Lemma 4.1.7), there is an isomorphism of correspondences 𝔆^tor_{t,w} ≃ 𝔍𝔊^tor_{(w(t)K_{p,P,w}w(t)^{-1} ∩ K_{p,P,w})K^p}. Here the right-hand side carries the two projections of the Igusa Hecke correspondence of §3.4.13 for the element w(t).
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.4 (pp. 43–44) identifies 𝔆^tor_{t,w} with the Igusa Hecke correspondence of §3.4.13 for w(t) = wtw^{-1}. The proof uses the decomposition P(Q_p)wK_{p,n} = P(Q_p)w ∏U_{α,n}∏U_{α,0} and Lemma 3.4.24. The Igusa Hecke correspondences, the strata and C^tor_t are all missing. The item generalises the ordinary-locus description of the Klingen U-correspondence in Pilloni (Duke 2020, §10) from GSp4 to GSp_{2g}.

items.name: §4.2.5: carrying the Iwahori level structure along the Hecke isogeny
items.statement: Let t = diag(p^{n_1}, …, p^{n_{2g}}) ∈ T^+(Q_p) with all n_i ≤ 0. Over the generic fibre of C^tor_t, the quasi-isogeny p_1^*A → p_2^*A is an isogeny with kernel L. It factors as p_1^*A = G_0 → G_1 → ⋯ → G_k = p_2^*A with ker(G_i → G_{i+1}) = L[p^{i+1}]/L[p^i], each killed by p. Transport rule: let G, G' be p-divisible groups of height 2g over a scheme of characteristic 0, and ϕ: G → G' an isogeny with kernel L ⊆ G[p] of rank p^s. Let H_{g+i} ⊆ G[p^n] be finite flat of rank p^{in}, étale-locally ≅ (Z/p^nZ)^i, in generic position with L, i.e. H_{g+i} ∩ L has rank p^{max(0, i+s−2g)}. Put H'_{g+i} = ϕ(H_{g+i}) if i + s ≤ 2g, and H'_{g+i} = ϕ(p^{-1}H_{g+i} ∩ p^{-n}L) if i + s > 2g. There is an isomorphism Gr_{g+i} → Gr'_{g+i}. If i + s ≤ 2g it is induced by H_{g+i} ≅ H'_{g+i}. If i + s > 2g, let H''_{g+i} = p(p^{-1}H_{g+i} ∩ p^{-n}L) ⊆ H_{g+i}. Then H''_{g+i}/(H''_{g+i} ∩ H_{g+i−1}) → Gr_{g+i} is an isomorphism, and ϕ (which factors through multiplication by p) induces an isomorphism H''_{g+i}/(H''_{g+i} ∩ H_{g+i−1}) → Gr'_{g+i}. Applying this step by step to the flag p_1^*H_{g+1} ⊆ p_1^*H_{g+2} ⊆ ⋯ gives the flag on p_2^*A[p^n].
items.note: Missing. §4.2.5 (p. 44) factors the isogeny through the p-torsion layers L[p^{i+1}]/L[p^i] and transports the flag H_{g+i} along each layer. The rule, the generic-position hypothesis rank(H_{g+i} ∩ L) = p^{max(0,i+s−2g)}, and the isomorphisms Gr_{g+i} ≅ Gr′_{g+i} through H″_{g+i} are paper-specific. They generalise the single-subgroup transport (G, H, L) ↦ (G/L, (H + L)/L) of Pilloni's Klingen correspondences (Duke 2020, §14.2) to full flags.

items.name: Remark 4.2.6: strict dominance and the layers L[p^{i+1}]/L[p^i]
items.statement: In the situation of §4.2.5 (t ∈ T^+(Q_p) of the form diag(p^{n_1}, …, p^{n_{2g}}) with all n_i ≤ 0), t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) if and only if the ranks of the groups L[p^{i+1}]/L[p^i] take all the values p, p², …, p^{2g−1}.
items.note: Missing. Remark 4.2.6 (p. 44), stated without proof, characterizes strict dominance of t = diag(p^{n_1},…,p^{n_{2g}}), all n_i ≤ 0, by the ranks of the layers L[p^{i+1}]/L[p^i]. It is elementary linear algebra about the kernel of t acting on the Tate module, and no layer states it.

items.name: §4.2.7: degree over a valuation ring and the transported subgroup H'
items.statement: Let V be a complete valuation ring for a rank-one valuation v extending the p-adic valuation (v(p) = 1), with fraction field K. For H finite flat over Spec V, deg H = v(x), where D_H = (x) is Fargues' divisor. Let G, G' be p-divisible groups of height h over Spec V, and ϕ: G → G' an isogeny with kernel L ⊆ G[p] of rank p^s. Let H ⊆ G[p^n] be finite flat of rank p^{in} with H_K étale-locally ≅ (Z/p^nZ)^i, and assume H and L are in generic position: H_K ∩ L_K has rank p^{max(0, i+s−h)}. Define H' ⊆ G' as the schematic closure of ϕ(H_K) if i + s ≤ h, and as the schematic closure of ϕ(p^{-1}H_K ∩ p^{-n}L_K) if i + s ≥ h.
items.note: Missing. §4.2.7 (pp. 44–45) combines Fargues's degree over a complete rank-one valuation ring, which is missing (see the Fargues items), with the schematic closure H′ of the transported subgroup. The finite-flat closure of a generic subgroup is planned in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 ('Finite-flat closure of a generic subgroup requires a proof under the correct base hypotheses'); H′ itself is planned nowhere. External input: [Far10] §2

items.name: Degree comparison for generic isomorphisms ([Far10] §3, Cor. 3)
items.statement: As used in Prop. 4.2.8: over V as in §4.2.7, the degree of finite flat group schemes is additive in short exact sequences. If u: H_1 → H_2 is a homomorphism of finite flat group schemes that is an isomorphism on generic fibres, then deg H_1 ≤ deg H_2, with equality iff u is an isomorphism.
items.note: Missing. Fargues's §3, Cor. 3 says that a map of finite flat group schemes over O_K which is a generic isomorphism has deg H_1 ≤ deg H_2, with equality iff it is an isomorphism; the degree is also additive in exact sequences. Neither library has it, and no layer plans it. The extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) records the same result as missing and routes it to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 by a source route ('growth along generic isomorphisms'). This paper also uses the equality case and additivity. External input: [Far10] L. Fargues, J. Reine Angew. Math. 645 (2010), §3, Cor. 3

items.name: Proposition 4.2.8 (1): deg H' ≥ deg H
items.statement: In the situation of §4.2.7, deg H' ≥ deg H.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.8, first assertion (p. 45), follows from Fargues's comparison and additivity, both missing. It generalises Pilloni's 'U does not decrease deg H' (Duke 2020, Lemma 14.3.1 (5)) from the Klingen subgroup of GSp4 to a subgroup of rank p^{in} in a height-h p-divisible group.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.8 (2): equality case forces BT_1 and BT_n
items.statement: In the situation of §4.2.7, if i + s = h and deg H = deg H', then L is a BT_1 and H is a BT_n.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.8, equality case (p. 45), needs truncated Barsotti–Tate groups BT_1 and BT_n. No layer defines these: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 defines only p-divisible groups, and the extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) routes BT_n there by a source route. It generalises the equality case of Pilloni's Lemma 14.3.1 (5) ('H is of multiplicative or of étale type').

items.name: Corollary 4.2.10 (1): p_2^*Z_i ≥ p_1^*Z_i on C^tor_t
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p). Over C^tor_t, p_2^*Z_i ≥ p_1^*Z_i as effective Cartier divisors, for all 1 ≤ i ≤ g.
items.note: Missing. Corollary 4.2.10, first assertion (p. 45), follows from Proposition 4.2.8 at the generic points of the special fibre of the normal scheme C^tor_t. Its objects are missing. It is the GSp_{2g} Iwahori-level form of Pilloni's 'the U-correspondence increases deg H' (Duke 2020, Cor. 14.3.2).

items.name: Corollary 4.2.10 (2): support of p_2^*Z_i − p_1^*Z_i for t ∈ T^{++}
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and 1 ≤ i ≤ g. The support of the effective divisor p_2^*Z_i − p_1^*Z_i on C^tor_t contains p_1^{-1}(∩_{j=0}^i (Z_{i,<j} ∪ Z_{i,>j})) and p_2^{-1}(∩_{j=0}^i (Z_{i,<j} ∪ Z_{i,>j})).
items.note: Missing. Corollary 4.2.10, second assertion (p. 45), is the strict increase for t ∈ T^{++}. Its proof prints 'p_1^*H_{g+i,x} and p_1^*H_{g+i,x}' where p_1^* and p_2^* are meant. It depends on the missing C^tor_t and divisors.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.11: behaviour of Z_{i,>j}, Z_{i,<j} under the Hecke correspondence
items.statement: For t ∈ T^+(Q_p), 1 ≤ i ≤ g and 0 ≤ j ≤ i, over C^tor_t: p_1^*Z_{i,>j} ≤ p_2^*Z_{i,>j} and p_2^*Z_{i,<j} ≤ p_1^*Z_{i,<j}.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.2.11 (p. 45) follows from Corollary 4.2.10 and the disjoint supports of Proposition 4.1.13. Its objects are missing.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.12: an inequality of divisors attached to w ∈ W
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.2.12 (p. 45) rewrites p_2^*Z_k ≥ p_1^*Z_k using D_i + D_{2g+1−i} = V(p^n). Its objects are missing.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.13: 𝔆^tor_{t,w} as a complement of divisors
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.2.13 (p. 45) follows from Lemma 4.1.9 (1) and Lemma 4.2.12. It was checked by direct computation: since {1,…,g} = I_{w,1} ⊔ I_{w,2}, the support of p_1^*Σ_{i=1}^g D_{w^{-1}(i)} + p_2^*Σ_{i=1}^g D_{w^{-1}(i)} is the support of p_1^*Σ_{I_{w,1}} + p_2^*Σ_{I_{w,2}}. Its objects are missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.14 (1): the good locus of 𝔆^tor_t is ∪_w 𝔆^tor_{t,w}
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p). The open formal subscheme of 𝔆^tor_t complementary to ∪_{i=1}^g (p_1^*D_i ∩ p_2^*D_{2g+1−i}) equals ∪_{w∈^MW} 𝔆^tor_{t,w}.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.14 (1) (p. 45) is proved by a degree induction along mixed-characteristic discrete valuation rings (p. 46). Its objects are missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.14 (2): p_2^*Z_i = p_1^*Z_i on ∪_w 𝔆^tor_{t,w}
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p). Over ∪_{w∈^MW} 𝔆^tor_{t,w}, p_2^*Z_i = p_1^*Z_i for all 1 ≤ i ≤ g.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.14 (2) (p. 46) depends on the missing C^tor_t, strata and divisors.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.14 (3): natural isomorphisms p_1^*Gr_i ≅ p_2^*Gr_i on ∪_w 𝔆^tor_{t,w}
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p). Over ∪_{w∈^MW} 𝔆^tor_{t,w} there are natural isomorphisms p_1^*Gr_i → p_2^*Gr_i for all 1 ≤ i ≤ 2g.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.14 (3) (p. 46) extends the generic-fibre isomorphisms of §4.2.5 integrally, using that the groups involved are extensions of étale by multiplicative groups. Its objects are missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.15 (1): for t ∈ T^{++}, the equality locus of Σ Z_i
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and 1 ≤ k ≤ g. The complement of the support of p_2^*Σ_{i=1}^k Z_i − p_1^*Σ_{i=1}^k Z_i is the locus where, for all 1 ≤ i ≤ k, p_1^*Gr_{g+i} and p_2^*Gr_{g+i} are multiplicative or étale BT's of the same type.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.15 (1) (p. 46) uses the equality case of Proposition 4.2.8 and hence truncated BT_n, which no layer defines. Its objects are missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.15 (2): natural isomorphisms on the equality locus
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and 1 ≤ k ≤ g. On the complement of the support of p_2^*Σ_{i=1}^k Z_i − p_1^*Σ_{i=1}^k Z_i there are natural isomorphisms p_1^*Gr_{g+i} → p_2^*Gr_{g+i} for 1 ≤ i ≤ k.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.15 (2) (p. 46) follows from the construction of §4.2.5. Its objects are missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.2.15 (3): support of p_2^*ΣZ_i − p_1^*ΣZ_i
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and 1 ≤ k ≤ g. The support of p_2^*Σ_{i=1}^k Z_i − p_1^*Σ_{i=1}^k Z_i equals the support of Σ_{i=1}^k (p_1^*D_{g−i+1} ∩ p_2^*D_{g+i}), i.e. ∪_{i=1}^k (p_1^*D_{g+1−i} ∩ p_2^*D_{g+i}).
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.2.15 (3) (p. 46) identifies the support of p_2^*ΣZ_i − p_1^*ΣZ_i with ∪_i (p_1^*D_{g+1−i} ∩ p_2^*D_{g+i}). Proposition 4.3.13 uses this to twist by an ideal supported there. Its objects are missing.

items.name: The M-torsor M_dR over S^tor
items.statement: Over S^tor, let H_{1,dR}(A) be the relative logarithmic de Rham homology of the semi-abelian scheme A, with filtration 0 → ω_{A^t} → H_{1,dR}(A) → Lie_A → 0. M_dR → S^tor is the M-torsor of triples (ψ_1, ψ_2, c) with ψ_1: O^g_{S^tor} → Lie_A and ψ_2: O^g_{S^tor} → ω_{A^t} isomorphisms and c ∈ O^×_{S^tor}, such that ψ_2 = c(ψ_1^t)^{-1}. Pushing out along representations gives a functor Rep(M) → Coh(S^tor), where Rep(M) is the category of representations of M on Z_p-modules.
items.note: Missing. AutomorphicBundles B0–B4 plan automorphic bundles of Levi representations and their canonical extensions to toroidal compactifications ('Construct the canonical extension on a toroidal compactification through its degeneration charts'). AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 plans relative H^1_dR of abelian schemes with its Hodge exact sequence. No layer plans the relative logarithmic de Rham homology of the semi-abelian scheme over a non-hyperspecial integral toroidal model, nor the M-torsor M_dR of triples (ψ_1, ψ_2, c) over S^tor. The item generalises the sheaves Ω^{(k,r)} of Pilloni (Duke 2020) on Klingen and paramodular models from GSp4 to GSp_{2g}. Pilloni's extraction left those sheaves missing and routed them to ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary.

items.name: The model V_κ and the automorphic sheaf ω^κ
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X^*(T)^{M,+} be M-dominant: κ = (k_1, …, k_g; k) with k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g. V_κ is the Z_p-module of functions f: M → A^1 such that f(mb) = (w_{0,M}κ)(b^{-1})f(m) for all (m, b) ∈ M × (B ∩ M). M acts by left translation, (m'·f)(m) = f(m'^{-1}m) [printed m′.f(m) = f(m^{−1}m′); sourceIssues E84]. V_κ is a Z_p-model of the irreducible representation of highest weight κ. The attached sheaf is ω^κ = π_*O_{M_dR}[−w_{0,M}κ], where π: M_dR → S^tor is the projection and [−w_{0,M}κ] denotes the isotypic part for the action of B ∩ M. The torsor M_dR, and hence ω^κ, depends on the choice of the semi-abelian scheme A in its isogeny class. Another member A_i of the chain gives another natural torsor, identified with M_dR only over Q_p. ω^κ also depends on the choice of the model V_κ (Remark 4.3.2).
items.note: Missing. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.1 plans integral highest-weight modules for its unitary applications ('Construct integral algebraic coefficient modules over O, ... Weyl/dual Weyl modules'). V_κ is such a Z_p-model for M = GL_g × G_m: the functions f with f(mb) = (w_{0,M}κ)(b^{-1})f(m). The sheaf ω^κ = π_*O_{M_dR}[−w_{0,M}κ] over the Iwahori-level model is missing, because M_dR is (see the torsor M_dR). Remark 4.3.2 notes that ω^κ depends on the choice of A in the chain and on the model V_κ. The introduction (§1.1, p. 2) describes the same sheaves over Q. The tower of Siegel Shimura varieties carries a natural M_µ-torsor, equivariant for G(A_f). For each level K and cone decomposition Σ, this torsor gives a functor Rep(M_µ) → VB(S^tor_{K,Σ}) sending the irreducible representation of highest weight κ ∈ X⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} to ω^κ. Here M_µ is the Levi of the Siegel parabolic P_µ (printed 'unipotent radical'; sourceIssues E1). The integral version of this torsor over the Iwahori-level model is M_dR.

items.name: Remark 4.3.3: normalization of weights
items.statement: The construction is normalized so that the standard representation of M, of highest weight ((0, …, 0, −1); 1), corresponds to Lie(A). Consequently ω_A corresponds to κ = ((1, 0, …, 0); −1).
items.note: Missing. AutomorphicBundles B4 plans the characteristic-zero dictionary for Siegel data ('For Siegel data, identify the Hodge vector bundle, its determinant, and Schur-functor weights') in its own normalization. Remark 4.3.3 (p. 47) fixes this paper's convention: the standard representation, of highest weight ((0,…,0,−1);1), corresponds to Lie(A), so ω_A corresponds to ((1,0,…,0);−1). The roadmap that takes ω^κ must record the conversion between the two conventions.

items.name: Rational isomorphism p_2^*ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^*ω^κ[1/p]
items.statement: Over C_{t,Q_p}, the quasi-isogeny p_1^*A → p_2^*A induces an isomorphism of torsors p_1^*M_dR = p_2^*M_dR, and hence an isomorphism p_2^*ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^*ω^κ[1/p].
items.note: Missing. AutomorphicBundles B5 plans 'pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences' in characteristic zero, and ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans the toroidal Hecke correspondences over Q_p. The isomorphism of torsors p_1^*M_dR = p_2^*M_dR over C_{t,Q_p} induced by the universal quasi-isogeny is planned nowhere, since M_dR is missing. Neither is the resulting isomorphism p_2^*ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^*ω^κ[1/p].

items.name: Lemma 4.3.4: p_2^*ω^κ ⊆ ⟨w_{0,M}κ, w(t)⟩ p_1^*ω^κ over 𝔆^tor_{t,w}
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p), w ∈ ^MW, w(t) = wtw^{-1} and κ ∈ X^*(T)^{M,+}. Over 𝔆^tor_{t,w}, the map p_2^*ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^*ω^κ[1/p] satisfies p_2^*ω^κ ⊆ ⟨w_{0,M}κ, w(t)⟩ p_1^*ω^κ. Here ⟨λ, s⟩ denotes the value λ(s) ∈ Q_p^× of a character λ at s ∈ T(Q_p).
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.3.4 (p. 47) compares the two integral lattices through the Hodge–Tate map on the multiplicative and étale parts of the Tate module. It uses the extreme eigenvalue ⟨−w_{0,M}κ, w(t)⟩ of w(t)^{-1} on V_κ. Its objects are missing. It generalises to GSp_{2g} and arbitrary κ the normalized pullback (1/p^r) on Ω^{(k,r)} of Pilloni (Duke 2020, §10.4).

items.name: §4.3.5: K_{p,1,n} and the integral model S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1,n},Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}
items.statement: K_{p,1,n} ⊆ K_{p,n} is the subgroup of elements congruent modulo p^n to an element of U(Z_p), U the unipotent radical of B. Then K_{p,n}/K_{p,1,n} ≅ T(Z/p^nZ). Working over Z_p(ζ_{p^n}), there is a map S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1,n},Q_p(ζ_{p^n})} → S^tor_{K^pK_{p,n},Q_p(ζ_{p^n})}. The integral model π: S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1,n},Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} → S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} is defined by normalization.
items.note: Missing. No layer defines K_{p,1,n}, the elements of K_{p,n} congruent modulo p^n to an element of U(Z_p), or the isomorphism K_{p,n}/K_{p,1,n} ≅ T(Z/p^nZ). ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans only parahorics and 'pro-p congruence subgroups'. No layer defines the normalized integral model over Z_p(ζ_{p^n}) either.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.6 (1): the level-K_{p,1,n} cover is finite étale over the good locus
items.statement: The restriction of π: S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1,n},Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} → S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} to S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} \ ∪_{i=1}^g (D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}) is a finite étale Galois cover with group T(Z/p^nZ).
items.note: Missing. The proof of Lemma 4.3.6 (1) (p. 47) uses that integral closure commutes with étale base change (Stacks 03GE), which is in Mathlib (see the Stacks item). It also uses that Gr_i is finite flat over the good locus, and it trivializes Gr_{w^{-1}(l)} ≅ Z/p^nZ and Gr_{w^{-1}(g+l)} ≅ μ_{p^n} étale-locally. The proof and the definition of O(χ) print 'Σ_{i=1}^d' where Σ_{i=1}^g is meant. The objects are missing. External input: [Sta22] The Stacks Project, Tag 03GE (integral closure commutes with étale localization)

items.name: Lemma 4.3.6 (2): the level-K_{p,1,n} cover over the Igusa strata
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW, S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1,n},Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} ×_{S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}} 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K_{p,P,w}K^p,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} = 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K_{p,P,1,w}K^p,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}, where K_{p,P,1,w} = wK_{p,1,n}w^{-1} ∩ P(Q_p).
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.3.6 (2) (p. 47) identifies the level-K_{p,1,n} cover over the Igusa strata with the Igusa variety of level K_{p,P,1,w}. The Igusa varieties and the cover are missing.

items.name: The sheaf O(χ) and ω^κ(χ)
items.statement: For a character χ: T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^×, O(χ) is the subsheaf of π_*O_{S^tor_{K^pK_{p,1,n},Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}} of sections s with t·s = χ(t)s for all t ∈ T(Z/p^nZ). It is coherent, and invertible over S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} \ ∪_{i=1}^g (D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}). Put ω^κ(χ) = ω^κ ⊗ O(χ).
items.note: Missing. The χ-isotypic part O(χ) of π_*O of the missing level-K_{p,1,n} cover, invertible over the good locus, and ω^κ(χ) = ω^κ ⊗ O(χ) are planned nowhere. The nebentypus of the Tau Ceti ModularForms roadmap concerns modular curves only.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.8: the trace of p_1 on 𝔆^tor_{t,w} is divisible by ⟨w^{-1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ, t⟩
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW and t ∈ T^+(Q_p). The trace Tr_{p_1}: (p_1)_*O_{𝔆^tor_{t,w}} → O_{𝔖^tor_w} factors through ⟨w^{-1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ, t⟩ O_{𝔖^tor_w}. Here ρ is half the sum of the positive roots.
items.note: Missing. Lemma 4.3.8 (p. 48) computes the trace of p_1 on the Igusa Hecke correspondence (Prop. 3.4.9, Remark 3.4.11). It uses the identity w^{-1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ = Σ_{α∈(w^{-1}Φ^{+,M})∩Φ^+} α. Its objects are missing. It generalises to GSp_{2g} and every w ∈ ^MW the normalized traces of Pilloni (Duke 2020, Lemma 10.3.2: divisibility by p^3; Lemma 7.1.1).

items.name: Fundamental class for lci correspondences ([FP21] Prop. 2.6)
items.statement: This is the form used in the proof of Prop. 4.3.11 ([FP21], Prop. 2.6). Suppose that in a correspondence (p_1, p_2) the map p_1 is a local complete intersection morphism of relative dimension 0. In the application, p_1: C^tor_t \ ∪_i (p_1^*D_i ∩ p_2^*D_{2g+1−i}) → S^tor \ ∪_i (D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}) is a quasi-finite morphism between schemes smooth over Z_p of the same dimension. Then p_1^!O is an invertible sheaf in degree 0, and there is a fundamental class p_2^*O = O → p_1^!O. Where p_1 is finite flat, the fundamental class is given by the trace of p_1.
items.note: Missing. Mathlib has the trace of a finite free algebra (mathlib:Algebra.trace), the affine ingredient of the finite flat case. No layer plans the upper-shriek functor, the invertibility of p_1^!O for lci p_1, or the fundamental class p_2^*O → p_1^!O. The extraction of Pilloni (Duke 2020) records the same material from its §4 (Hartshorne duality for embeddable morphisms, f^! of lci maps, fundamental classes from the trace) as missing. It routes that material to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension by a source route. External input: [FP21] N. Fakhruddin, V. Pilloni, Hecke operators and the coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu (2021), Prop. 2.6

items.name: Proposition 4.3.9: the normalized correspondence t_w on 𝔆^tor_{t,w} is integral
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p), w ∈ ^MW and κ ∈ X^*(T)^{M,+}. Over 𝔆^tor_{t,w} there is a natural cohomological correspondence t_w: p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ, equal to ⟨−w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩ t_w^{naive}. Here t_w^{naive} is the rational map obtained as the tensor product of p_2^*ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^*ω^κ[1/p] with the fundamental class p_2^*O_{𝔖^tor_w} → p_1^!O_{𝔖^tor_w} given by the trace of p_1. In particular the normalized map is integral. The normalization depends on t ∈ T^+(Q_p) itself, not only on its class modulo T(Z_p) (Remark 4.3.10).
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.3.9 (p. 48) combines Lemmas 4.3.4 and 4.3.8. The normalization factor ⟨−w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩ is the product of the two lemmas' factors, since ⟨λ, w(t)⟩ = ⟨w^{-1}λ, t⟩ (checked by direct computation). The general notion of a normalized cohomological correspondence is missing; Pilloni (2020, §4.3) routes it to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. The item generalises the normalized operators T_1, T_2, U_1, U_2 of Pilloni (Duke 2020, §§7.1, 10.4) from GSp4 Klingen level to GSp_{2g} at Iwahori level.

items.name: The set C(κ) ⊆ ^MW
items.statement: For κ ∈ X^*(T)^{M,+}, C(κ) = {w ∈ ^MW : w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) ∈ X^*(T)^−_Q}. Here X^*(T)^−_Q = −X^*(T)^+_Q is the antidominant cone, where X^*(T)^+ is given by 0 ≥ k_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ k_g. Since X^*(T)^−_Q is a fundamental domain for the action of W on X^*(T)_Q, C(κ) is nonempty and w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) is independent of w ∈ C(κ).
items.note: Missing. The fundamental-domain fact the paper cites is partly in Tau Ceti. tauceti:TauCeti.exists_mem_dominantChamber states that every weight of a root system is Weyl-conjugate into the closed dominant chamber of a base. Uniqueness of that representative is planned in Tau Ceti RootSystems Layer 4 ('a dominant representative exists and is unique'). No layer plans the set C(κ) ⊆ ^MW, or the root datum of GSp_{2g} with w_{0,M} and ρ in the paper's coordinates. C(κ) is first defined in §1.3.3 (p. 3), in the equivalent form −w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) ∈ X⋆(T)^+. There the condition has to be read in X⋆(T)_Q, as on p. 48 [printed X⋆(T)^+; sourceIssues E3]. For w ∈ C(κ), the introduction puts ν + ρ = −w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ), which does not depend on w. It is the dominant representative of the infinitesimal character of the automorphic forms that contribute to coherent cohomology in weight κ. If ν + ρ is regular, then C(κ) has exactly one element.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.11: the normalized correspondence t on C^tor_t \ ∪(p_1^*D_i ∩ p_2^*D_{2g+1−i})
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p) and κ ∈ X^*(T)^{M,+}. Over C^tor_t \ ∪_{i=1}^g (p_1^*D_i ∩ p_2^*D_{2g+1−i}) there is a cohomological correspondence t: p_2^*ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ equal to ⟨−w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩ t^{naive} for any w ∈ C(κ). Here t^{naive} is the rational map obtained as the tensor product of p_2^*ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^*ω^κ[1/p] and the fundamental class p_2^*O_{S^tor \ ∪(D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i})} → p_1^!O_{S^tor \ ∪(D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i})} induced by the trace. The map p_1: C^tor_t \ ∪(p_1^*D_i ∩ p_2^*D_{2g+1−i}) → S^tor \ ∪(D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}) is lci, because source and target are smooth over Z_p. So p_1^!O is invertible, and the normalized rational map is an honest map.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.3.11 (p. 48) says p_1 is lci on the good locus because source and target are smooth over Z_p. It then uses the fundamental class of Fakhruddin–Pilloni (Prop. 2.6) and checks integrality at the generic points of the special fibre by Proposition 4.3.9. The display prints 'D_{2g+i−1}' where D_{2g+1−i} is meant. The objects are missing. External input: [FP21] Prop. 2.6

items.name: Remark 4.3.12: restriction of t to 𝔆^tor_{t,w'}
items.statement: Let w ∈ C(κ). The restriction of t to 𝔆^tor_{t,w} is t_w. For any w' ∈ ^MW, the restriction of t to 𝔆^tor_{t,w'} is ⟨(w')^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ), t⟩ t_{w'}, i.e. p^{n_{w'}} t_{w'} up to a p-adic unit. Here n_{w'} = ⟨(w')^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) + ρ, v(t)⟩ − ⟨w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) + ρ, v(t)⟩ ≥ 0 for t ∈ T^+(Q_p). If t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), then n_{w'} > 0 for w' ∉ C(κ).
items.note: Missing. Remark 4.3.12 (p. 48) prints n_{w′} with unbalanced parentheses and pairs with t where an exponent of p requires v(t). The +ρ terms cancel, so the restriction of t to 𝔆^tor_{t,w′} is ⟨(w′)^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ), t⟩ t_{w′}, as the item states. The objects are missing.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.13: t extends over C^tor_t after twisting by −kΣZ_i
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and κ ∈ X^*(T)^{M,+}. There is k ∈ Z_{≥0}, depending on κ, such that t extends to a cohomological correspondence t̃: p_2^*(ω^κ(−kΣ_{i=1}^g Z_i)) → p_1^!(ω^κ(−kΣ_{i=1}^g Z_i)) over C^tor_t.
items.note: Missing. Proposition 4.3.13 (p. 48) extends t over C^tor_t after a twist by −kΣZ_i. The proof uses pseudo-coherence of p_2^*ω^κ and the ideal of p_2^*ΣZ_i − p_1^*ΣZ_i, supported on ∪(p_1^*D_i ∩ p_2^*D_{2g+1−i}) by Proposition 4.2.15 (3). Its objects are missing. It generalises the device of Pilloni (Duke 2020, Lemma 14.9.1 (b)), which makes U_{Kli(p),2} integral after twisting by I^{−3}.

items.name: Remark 4.3.19: normalized Hecke operators preserve a lattice; [BP21] Conjecture 5.10.7 in the Siegel case
items.statement: For t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), the normalized cohomological correspondences of Propositions 4.3.13 and 4.3.18 imply the following. The normalized Hecke operators ⟨−w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩[K_{p,n}tK_{p,n}] (w ∈ C(κ)) preserve a lattice in the rational coherent cohomology of S^tor with coefficients in ω^κ (resp. ω^κ(χ)), so their eigenvalues are p-adically integral. This proves Conjecture 5.10.7 of [BP21] in the Siegel case.
items.note: Missing. Remark 4.3.19 (p. 49) deduces from Propositions 4.3.13 and 4.3.18 that the normalized operators at p preserve a lattice in rational coherent cohomology, so their eigenvalues are p-adically integral. This proves Conjecture 5.10.7 of Boxer–Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory (arXiv:2110.10251), in the Siegel case. That paper serves the atlas only through its Theorem 4.4.40 (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S6, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6); its conjecture is planned nowhere. The item generalises Pilloni's integrality of the T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} eigenvalues (Duke 2020, Prop. 14.9.1) from GSp4 in degrees 0 and 1 to GSp_{2g}, every t ∈ T^{++} and every degree. External input: [BP21] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory (2021), arXiv:2110.10251, Conjecture 5.10.7

items.name: Integral closure commutes with étale localization ([Sta22] Tag 03GE)
items.statement: As used in Lemma 4.3.6: forming the integral closure (normalization) of a scheme in a finite extension of its generic fibre commutes with étale base change.
items.note: Library. Mathlib proves the stronger smooth form, at the ring level and for relative normalization of schemes. The étale case used in the proof of Lemma 4.3.6 is a special case. External input: [Sta22] The Stacks Project Authors, Stacks Project (2022), Tag 03GE

items.name: The twisted automorphic sheaf ω̃^κ
items.statement: Fix t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+}. Let k ∈ Z_{≥0} be as in Proposition 4.3.13, so that the normalized cohomological correspondence t : p_2^⋆ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ (defined over C_t^tor ∖ Σ_{i=1}^g p_1^⋆D_i ∩ p_2^⋆D_{2g+1−i}) extends over the whole of C_t^tor to t̃ : p_2^⋆ω^κ(−kΣ_{i=1}^g Z_i) → p_1^!ω^κ(−kΣ_{i=1}^g Z_i). For an integer k' ≥ k, taken large enough (how large is fixed in the proof of Proposition 4.5.8), put ω̃^κ := ω^κ(−k'Σ_{i=1}^g Z_i), a locally free sheaf on the integral model S^tor = S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} (the blow-up of Proposition 4.1.13), where Z_i = Σ_{j=1}^i D_{g+j}.
items.note: ω̃^κ = ω^κ(−k′Σ_{i=1}^g Z_i) lives on the blown-up integral toroidal model S̃^tor_{K^pK_{p,n}} of the Siegel variety of genus g at the Iwahori-type level K_{p,n} of §4.1 (Proposition 4.1.13), with Z_i = Σ_{j=1}^i D_{g+j}. None of these objects is planned. PELModuli:M5 ('Construct Siegel moduli for every dimension') and ShimuraCompactifications:C5 ('Construct the integral toroidal algebraic spaces with their universal semi-abelian extensions'; 'Keep the good-prime assumptions on the input PEL datum') stop at hyperspecial level. AutomorphicBundles:B4 ('For Siegel data, identify the Hodge vector bundle, its determinant, and Schur-functor weights') plans ω^κ, but not its integral twists by the divisors Z_i at parahoric level. The twist exists to make the normalized Hecke correspondence integral on the whole of C_t^tor (Proposition 4.3.13). For GSp4 at Klingen level, Pilloni (2020) obtained integrality instead by factoring the correspondence through paramodular level (PAPER-PILLONI-20/factorization-into-integral-correspondences, missing). Neither library has coherent cohomology of Shimura varieties or Hecke correspondences at p. The Nebentypus variant is defined in the same way after Proposition 4.3.18 (p. 49): ω̃^κ(χ) = ω^κ(χ)(−k′Σ_{i=1}^g Z_i) for some k′ ≥ k, with k given by that proposition.

items.name: Factorization of t̃ on ω̃^κ (Lemma 4.3.14)
items.statement: With t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and k ≤ k' as in the definition of ω̃^κ, the correspondence t̃ of Proposition 4.3.13 induces a cohomological correspondence t̃ : p_2^⋆ω̃^κ → p_1^!ω̃^κ over C_t^tor which factors as p_2^⋆ω̃^κ → O_{C_t^tor}((k'−k)(Σ_{i=1}^g p_2^⋆Z_i − Σ_{i=1}^g p_1^⋆Z_i)) ⊗ p_2^⋆ω̃^κ → p_1^!ω̃^κ. The first map is induced by the effective Cartier divisor (k'−k)(p_2^⋆ΣZ_i − p_1^⋆ΣZ_i) (effective since p_2^⋆Z_i ≥ p_1^⋆Z_i, Corollary 4.2.10); the second is the composite of the identification O_{C_t^tor}((k'−k)(Σp_2^⋆Z_i − Σp_1^⋆Z_i)) ⊗ p_2^⋆ω̃^κ ≅ p_2^⋆ω^κ(−kΣZ_i) ⊗ p_1^⋆O_{S^tor}((k−k')ΣZ_i), of t̃ ⊗ id, and of the identification p_1^!ω^κ(−kΣZ_i) ⊗ p_1^⋆O_{S^tor}((k−k')ΣZ_i) ≅ p_1^!ω̃^κ.
items.note: The factorization combines three inputs. The first is the extension t̃ of Proposition 4.3.13, which is missing. The second is the inequality p_2^⋆Z_i ≥ p_1^⋆Z_i of Corollary 4.2.10, on the missing Iwahori-level Hecke correspondence; it makes (k′−k)(Σp_2^⋆Z_i − Σp_1^⋆Z_i) effective. The third is the compatibility of p_1^! with twisting by a line bundle pulled back along p_1. The upper-shriek functor for the projections of C_t^tor belongs to coherent Grothendieck duality, which no layer plans. SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3 plans Serre duality only for curves, and PAPER-PILLONI-20 sent Grothendieck duality by source route to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension (PAPER-PILLONI-20/grothendieck-duality-projectively-embeddable). The lemma is used, with Corollary 4.4.3, in the proof of Proposition 4.5.8. There the factorization is reprinted at the top of p. 53 without the parentheses around the difference Σp_2^⋆Z_i − Σp_1^⋆Z_i (sourceIssues E105).

items.name: Identification of graded pieces and of O(χ) along the Hecke correspondence (Lemma 4.3.16)
items.statement: Let χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× be a character, O(χ) the χ-isotypic subsheaf of π_⋆O of the normalized level-K_{p,1,n} model (invertible on S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} ∖ Σ_{i=1}^g D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}), and ω^κ(χ) = ω^κ ⊗ O(χ). Let t ∈ T^+(Q_p). Over C^tor_{t,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} ∖ Σ_{i=1}^g p_1^⋆D_i ∩ p_2^⋆D_{2g+1−i} there are canonical isomorphisms p_1^⋆Gr_i ≅ p_2^⋆Gr_i (1 ≤ i ≤ 2g), and they induce an isomorphism p_2^⋆O(χ) → p_1^⋆O(χ).
items.note: Every ingredient comes from §4.2 and is missing: the level-K_{p,1,n} model with the sheaf O(χ) ⊂ π_⋆O, the graded pieces Gr_i of the filtration it carries, and Proposition 4.2.14, from which the lemma follows (proof on p. 49). No layer plans integral models of Siegel varieties with p^n-level structure refining Iwahori level. The printed statement removes Σ_{i=1}^d p_1^⋆D_i ∩ p_2^⋆D_{2g+1−i}. The index runs over 1 ≤ i ≤ g, as in the next paragraph and in Proposition 4.3.18's setting; d is a misprint for g (sourceIssues E85).

items.name: Normalized Hecke correspondence with Nebentypus on ℭ^tor_{t,w} (Proposition 4.3.17)
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW, t ∈ T^+(Q_p), κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} and χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^×. Over ℭ^tor_{t,w,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} (the base change of the formal scheme ℭ^tor_{t,w} = p_1^{-1}𝔖^tor_w ∩ p_2^{-1}𝔖^tor_w) there is a natural cohomological correspondence t_w : p_2^⋆ω^κ(χ) → p_1^!ω^κ(χ) equal to ⟨−w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩ t_w^{naive}, where t_w^{naive} is the rational map obtained as the tensor product of p_2^⋆ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^⋆ω^κ[1/p], of p_2^⋆O(χ) → p_1^⋆O(χ), and of the fundamental class p_2^⋆O_{𝔖^tor_{w,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}} → p_1^!O_{𝔖^tor_{w,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}} given by the trace of p_1. In other words, this normalized rational map is integral.
items.note: This is the Nebentypus analogue of Proposition 4.3.9; its proof reads 'This is analogue to proposition 4.3.9'. No layer plans integral normalized Hecke correspondences in coherent cohomology. AutomorphicBundles:B5 plans 'pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences' with 'all scalar normalizations' for sections of automorphic bundles, not integral cohomological correspondences p_2^⋆F → p_1^!F on formal ordinary strata. The formalism of cohomological correspondences, their construction from a fundamental class, and their renormalization (Pilloni 2020, §4.3) is missing too (PAPER-PILLONI-20/cohomological-correspondence-from-fundamental-class, PAPER-PILLONI-20/normalized-cohomological-correspondence). On p. 49 the factor is printed ⟨−w^{−1}(w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩, with an unbalanced parenthesis. The intended factor is ⟨−w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩, as in the next paragraph and in Proposition 4.4.5 (sourceIssues E89).

items.name: Normalized Hecke correspondence with Nebentypus off Σ p_1^⋆D_i ∩ p_2^⋆D_{2g+1−i}
items.statement: For t ∈ T^+(Q_p), κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} and χ as above, a cohomological correspondence t : p_2^⋆ω^κ(χ) → p_1^!ω^κ(χ) is defined over C^tor_{t,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} ∖ Σ_{i=1}^g p_1^⋆D_i ∩ p_2^⋆D_{2g+1−i} as ⟨−w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ, t⟩ t^{naive} for any w ∈ C(κ) (the factor does not depend on w ∈ C(κ)), where t^{naive} is the tensor product of p_2^⋆ω^κ[1/p] → p_1^⋆ω^κ[1/p], of the isomorphism p_2^⋆O(χ) → p_1^⋆O(χ) of Lemma 4.3.16, and of the fundamental class p_2^⋆O_{S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} ∖ Σ D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}} → p_1^!O_{S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} ∖ Σ D_i ∩ D_{2g+1−i}} induced by the trace.
items.note: Missing for the same reasons as Proposition 4.3.17: it is built from the missing sheaves ω^κ(χ) and the Hecke correspondence C_t^tor of §§4.2–4.3, and from a fundamental class given by a trace map (coherent duality, not planned). In the printed display of the fundamental class (p. 49) the removed locus is Σ_{i=1}^g D_i ∩ D_{2g+i−1}. D_{2g+1−i} is meant, as in Lemma 4.3.16 and in the first line of the same paragraph (sourceIssues E88).

items.name: Integral extension of the Hecke correspondence with Nebentypus (Proposition 4.3.18)
items.statement: Assume t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p). There exists k ∈ Z_{≥0} (depending on κ and χ) such that the correspondence t : p_2^⋆ω^κ(χ) → p_1^!ω^κ(χ) extends to a cohomological correspondence over the whole of C^tor_{t,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}: t̃ : p_2^⋆ω^κ(χ)(−kΣ_{i=1}^g Z_i) → p_1^!ω^κ(χ)(−kΣ_{i=1}^g Z_i).
items.note: This is the Nebentypus analogue of Proposition 4.3.13 ('This is analogue to proposition 4.3.13'), on the missing blown-up Iwahori-level model. It is missing for the reasons given under ω̃^κ and Proposition 4.3.17. Its GSp4 counterpart, integral Hecke operators at Klingen level obtained through a factorization, is PAPER-PILLONI-20/factorization-into-integral-correspondences (missing).

items.name: The twisted sheaf ω̃^κ(χ)
items.statement: With k as in Proposition 4.3.18, ω̃^κ(χ) := ω^κ(χ)(−k'Σ_{i=1}^g Z_i) on S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})} for some integer k' ≥ k (taken large enough for Proposition 4.5.8).
items.note: This is a definition on the missing Iwahori-level model with p^n-level structure; see ω̃^κ. The printed text says only 'for some k′ ≥ k'. The Cousin spectral sequence with Nebentypus (Theorem 4.5.2) needs k′ large enough for Proposition 4.5.8, as for ω̃^κ.

items.name: The closed neighbourhood S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} and the divisors D_{w,±}
items.statement: Fix t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and w ∈ ^MW with associated sequence (w_1, …, w_g) (§3.1). Put S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} := S^tor_{F_p} ∩ ∩_{i=1}^g (Z_{i,>w_i−1} ∩ Z_{i,<w_i+1}) (corrected from the printed Z_{i,>w_i+1}), D_{w,−} := ∪_i Z_{i,>w_i} and D_{w,+} := ∪_i Z_{i,<w_i} (in §4.5.6 these are taken as the Cartier divisors D_{−,w} = Σ_{i=1}^g Z_{i,>w_i}, D_{+,w} = Σ_{i=1}^g Z_{i,<w_i}), C^tor_{t,F_p,(w−1,w+1)} := p_1^{-1}S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} ∩ p_2^{-1}S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} and C^tor_{t,F_p,w} := p_1^{-1}S^tor_{F_p,w} ∩ p_2^{-1}S^tor_{F_p,w}. By Proposition 4.1.13(2) and Corollary 4.1.14, S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} ∖ (D_{w,+} ∪ D_{w,−}) = S^tor_{F_p,w}.
items.note: These are built from the closed subsets Z_{i,>j} and Z_{i,<j} of the special fibre of the blown-up Iwahori-level model (§4.1.16, Proposition 4.1.13(2), Corollary 4.1.14). Those subsets are missing, like the model itself. No atlas stage plans a stratification of the special fibre of a Siegel variety at Iwahori level. The strata that are planned are the unitary Newton and Ekedahl–Oort strata of IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.0 and IG.2, and Hasse loci for modular curves and Hilbert varieties. The printed definition on p. 50 is ∩_i Z_{i,<w_i+1} ∩ Z_{i,>w_i+1}. The notation (w−1, w+1) and the set Z_{>w−1} = ∩_i Z_{i,>w_i−1} of §4.1.16 (recalled on p. 52) show that Z_{i,>w_i−1} is meant; the item uses the corrected form.

items.name: Strict dynamic compactification of the Hecke correspondence on S^tor_{F_p,w} (Lemma 4.4.2)
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and w ∈ ^MW. Then (C^tor_{t,F_p,(w−1,w+1)}, S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)}, p_1, p_2, D_{w,+}, D_{w,−}) is a strict dynamic compactification (Definition 2.1.26) of the correspondence (C^tor_{t,F_p,w}, S^tor_{F_p,w}, p_1, p_2): there is 0 < s < 1 with p_2^⋆D_{w,+} ≤ s p_1^⋆D_{w,+} and p_1^⋆D_{w,−} ≤ s p_2^⋆D_{w,−}.
items.note: Strict dynamic compactifications (Definition 2.1.26, p. 10) belong to the paper's §2 formalism of cohomology with partial support for correspondences, which no atlas layer plans. No stage mentions dynamic correspondences or cohomology with partial support. The ordinary projectors of PadicFamilies:L0a act on 'a finite underlying module' and degreewise on 'finite perfect/cohomological complexes', not on cohomology with support. Pilloni (2020) worked instead with locally finite endomorphisms (PAPER-PILLONI-20/def-2-3-1-locally-finite-chain-endomorphism, missing). The inputs Lemma 4.2.11 and Corollary 4.2.10 concern the missing Iwahori-level correspondence. In the proof (p. 50) the second inequality is printed p_1^⋆Z_{i,<w_i} ≥ p_1^⋆Z_{i,<w_i}. The intended inequality is p_1^⋆Z_{i,<w_i} ≥ p_2^⋆Z_{i,<w_i}, as the conclusion s·p_1^⋆Z_{i,<w_i} ≥ p_2^⋆Z_{i,<w_i} shows.

items.name: Factorization of O → O(m(p_2^⋆ΣZ_i − p_1^⋆ΣZ_i)) through D_{w,+} (Corollary 4.4.3)
items.statement: Let t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), w ∈ ^MW and i ∈ {1,2}. There exists m ∈ Z_{≥0} (depending on w and i) such that over p_i^{-1}S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} ⊆ C^tor_{t,F_p} the canonical map O → O(m(p_2^⋆Σ_{j=1}^g Z_j − p_1^⋆Σ_{j=1}^g Z_j)) factors as O → O(p_1^⋆D_{w,+} + p_2^⋆D_{w,+}) → O(m(p_2^⋆Σ_j Z_j − p_1^⋆Σ_j Z_j)); dually, O(−m(p_2^⋆ΣZ_j − p_1^⋆ΣZ_j)) → O factors through O(−p_1^⋆D_{w,+} − p_2^⋆D_{w,+}).
items.note: This statement lives on the missing C^tor_{t,F_p}, so it is missing. The proof compares locally two effective Cartier divisors with the same support over p_i^{−1}S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)}, namely p_2^⋆ΣZ_j − p_1^⋆ΣZ_j and p_1^⋆D_{w,+} + p_2^⋆D_{w,+}, and then glues the local maps. It sets m = 2n and glues a map out of O(−2m(p_2^⋆ΣZ_i − p_1^⋆ΣZ_i)), so it proves the statement for the exponent 2m. Since m is only claimed to exist, this is harmless. The corollary is used with Lemma 4.3.14 in Proposition 4.5.8 to fix k′.

items.name: Strict dynamic compactification modulo p^s (Proposition 4.4.4)
items.statement: For every s ≥ 1, t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and w ∈ ^MW, the correspondence (C^tor_{t,w,Z/p^sZ}, S^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ}, p_1, p_2) (the reduction mod p^s of ℭ^tor_{t,w} ⇉ 𝔖^tor_w) admits a strict dynamic compactification (printed 'for all s ≥ 0'; for s = 0 the statement is empty). The compactification used is S̄^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ} := the closure of S^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ} in S^tor_{Z/p^sZ}, which does not depend on t, and C̄^tor_{t,w,Z/p^sZ} := p_1^⋆S̄^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ} ∩ p_2^⋆S̄^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ}. For s = 1 the boundary is cut out by the restrictions of D_{w,+} and D_{w,−} to S̄^tor_{w,F_p} ⊆ S^tor_{F_p,(w−1,w+1)} (Lemma 4.4.2). For general s, strictness is deduced from the case s = 1 by Lemma 2.1.35. The boundary closed subschemes it produces have the same underlying sets as D_{w,±} ∩ S̄^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ}; their ideals are generated by lifts of local equations of the reduced boundary together with the nilradical.
items.note: This is deduced from Lemma 4.4.2 by Lemma 2.1.35, part of the §2 formalism, applied to the reductions of the missing formal schemes 𝔖^tor_w and ℭ^tor_{t,w}. The fact that the compactification of S^tor_{w,Z/p^sZ} does not depend on t is used in Proposition 4.4.5.

items.name: Higher Hida complexes in weight κ at Iwahori level
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW, κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+}, t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), K_{w,p,P} := wK_{p,n}w^{-1} ∩ P(Q_p) (so 𝔖^tor_w ≅ 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{w,p,P}}, Lemma 4.1.7), and t_w : p_2^⋆ω^κ → p_1^!ω^κ the normalized correspondence over ℭ^tor_{t,w} of Proposition 4.3.9. Define RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ) := lim_s RΓ(S^tor_{Z/p^sZ,w}, ω^κ)^{C^tor_{t,w,Z/p^sZ}−ord} and RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, cusp) := lim_s RΓ(S^tor_{Z/p^sZ,w}, ω^κ(−D))^{C^tor_{t,w,Z/p^sZ}−ord}, where for each s the ordinary part is that of Theorem 2.5.1, computed on any strict dynamic compactification (Proposition 4.4.4) as the ordinary part of cohomology with partial support RΓ_{D_{w,+},D_{w,−}}, and the transition maps come from the base change formula of Proposition 2.6.13.
items.note: The complex is a limit over s of ordinary parts (Theorem 2.5.1) of cohomology with partial support on a strict dynamic compactification of the reduction of 𝔖^tor_w ≅ 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{w,p,P}}. Every ingredient is the paper's own and unplanned. PadicFamilies:L0a ('Apply the result degreewise to finite perfect/cohomological complexes with commuting U and differential') does not reach ordinary parts of cohomology with support. The complex generalizes to GSp_{2g}, and to every w ∈ ^MW, Pilloni (2020)'s Klingen-level ordinary complex fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) of Theorem 11.2.1 (PAPER-PILLONI-20/integral-klingen-ordinary-perfect-amplitude-0-1, missing).

items.name: Higher Hida complexes in weight κ with Nebentypus χ
items.statement: For χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^×, over Z_p(ζ_{p^n}): RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) := lim_s RΓ(S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})/p^s,w}, ω^κ(χ))^{C^tor_{t,w,Z/p^sZ}−ord} and RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ, cusp) := lim_s RΓ(S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})/p^s,w}, ω^κ(χ)(−D))^{C^tor_{t,w,Z/p^sZ}−ord}, the ordinary part being taken for the correspondence t_w of Proposition 4.3.17.
items.note: Missing, like the complexes without Nebentypus. The correspondence used is the t_w of Proposition 4.3.17 over ℭ^tor_{t,w,Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}, which is missing.

items.name: Independence of t and perfectness (Proposition 4.4.5, first part)
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW, κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} and χ as above, the complexes RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ), RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, cusp), RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) and RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ, cusp) do not depend on the choice of t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), and they are perfect complexes of Z_p-modules.
items.note: The proof has two steps. Independence of t uses that the compactification of Proposition 4.4.4 does not depend on t, together with t^n = t′u and t′^n = tu′ for some u, u′ ∈ T^+(Q_p). Perfectness is Theorem 2.6.8. The notion of a perfect complex is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7); the complexes are not. For GSp4 and the Klingen stratum the perfectness statement is Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.2.1(7), without its amplitude bound (PAPER-PILLONI-20/integral-klingen-ordinary-perfect-amplitude-0-1, missing).

items.name: Locally algebraic T(Q_p)-action of weight ν (Proposition 4.4.5, second part, and Remark 4.4.6)
items.statement: The complexes of the preceding statement carry an action of T(Q_p) (T^+(Q_p) acting through the normalized Hecke correspondences of Propositions 4.3.9 and 4.3.17, invertibly on the ordinary part). This action is locally algebraic with algebraic part ν = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ: T(Z_p) acts on RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ) and RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, cusp) through the character ν, and on RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) and RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ, cusp) through νχ.
items.note: This is the paper's own construction on the missing complexes: T^+(Q_p) acts through the normalized correspondences of Propositions 4.3.9 and 4.3.17, invertibly on the ordinary part. The proof says only that the action of T(Z_p) through ν 'follows from the construction (and the normalization of the Hecke correspondences in proposition 4.3.9)'.

items.name: Cousin spectral sequence with Nebentypus (Theorem 4.5.2, general χ)
items.statement: For κ, t as above and a character χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^×, there are spectral sequences ⊕_{w ∈ C(κ), ℓ(w) = a} H^{a+b}_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}, ω̃^κ(χ))^{t−ord} and ⊕_{w ∈ C(κ), ℓ(w) = a} H^{a+b}_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ, cusp) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}, ω̃^κ(χ)(−D))^{t−ord}.
items.note: Missing, as in the case χ = 1. It uses ω̃^κ(χ) and the correspondence of Proposition 4.3.18, both missing.

items.name: Regular weight: higher Hida complex = ordinary integral cohomology (Corollary 4.5.4)
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} with C(κ) = {w} (printed κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^+). There is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ) ≃ RΓ(S^tor, ω̃^κ)^{t−ord}, and similarly RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, cusp) ≃ RΓ(S^tor, ω̃^κ(−D))^{t−ord}. For a character χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× there is a canonical isomorphism RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) ≃ RΓ(S^tor_{Z_p(ζ_{p^n})}, ω̃^κ(χ))^{t−ord}, and similarly for cuspidal cohomology.
items.note: This is the degenerate case #C(κ) = 1 of the Cousin spectral sequence (Remark 1.4.5, p. 5), which is missing. Its GSp4 counterpart is Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.2.1(5), for weights (k,r) with r ≥ 3: the classical ordinary complex equals the ordinary complex over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus (PAPER-PILLONI-20/integral-classical-vs-p-rank-at-least-one-r-ge-3, missing).

items.name: Classicality in regular weight (Corollary 4.5.5)
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} with C(κ) = {w} (printed κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^+) and ν = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ. There is a canonical isomorphism of T(Q_p)-modules RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ) ⊗ Q_p(−ν) ≃ RΓ(S^tor_{Q_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} (level K^pK_{p,n}; ord is the part where T^+(Q_p) acts invertibly with characters ordinary in weight κ, §1.3.4), and similarly for cuspidal cohomology. For χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× there is an isomorphism of T(Q_p)-modules RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) ⊗ Q_p(ζ_{p^n})(−ν) ≃ RΓ(S^tor_{Q_p(ζ_{p^n})}, ω^κ(χ))^{ord}.
items.note: This follows from Corollary 4.5.4 after inverting p and untwisting by ν, both missing. The ordinary part RΓ(S^tor_{Q_p}, ω^κ)^{ord} of §1.3.4 is the paper's own notion. For GSp4 and the Klingen stratum, the analogous classical comparison in large weight is Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.3.1(4) (PAPER-PILLONI-20/higher-hida-classical-comparison-large-weight, missing).

items.name: The Cousin spectral sequence of S^tor and its local terms
items.statement: By Theorem 2.9.7 the filtration F_• gives a spectral sequence E_1^{a,b} = H_c^{a+b}(F̂_a ∖ F̂_{a−1}, ω̃^κ) ⇒ H^{a+b}(S^tor, ω̃^κ), and by Lemma 2.9.3 and Lemma 4.5.7, RΓ_c(F̂_a ∖ F̂_{a−1}, ω̃^κ) = ⊕_{w, ℓ(w) = a} RΓ(S^tor, lim_m lim_n ω̃^κ(−mD_{−,w})/I^n_{Z,>w−1}), where I_{Z,>w−1} is the ideal sheaf of Z_{>w−1}. Each t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) acts on this spectral sequence (Proposition 2.9.9, the condition p_1^⋆F_l ⊆ p_2^⋆F_l following from Corollary 4.2.10 via Lemma 4.2.11).
items.note: Several inputs belong to the paper's §2 formalism, and none is planned: Theorem 2.9.7 (p. 28), the spectral sequence of a filtration by closed subsets in coherent cohomology with compact supports along formal completions; Lemma 2.9.3; and Proposition 2.9.9, for the action of t. The filtration F_• and its strata are those of §4.1.16, also missing. Coherent cohomology with supports is unplanned; see the Cousin spectral sequence.

items.name: Comparison of the local Cousin term with cohomology with partial support (Proposition 4.5.8)
items.statement: For w ∈ ^MW, t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and k' large enough, the natural map RΓ(S^tor, lim_m lim_n ω̃^κ(−mD_{−,w})/I^n_{Z,>w−1}) → RΓ(S^tor, lim_n colim_r lim_m ω̃^κ(−mD_{−,w} + rD_{+,w})/p^n) induces a quasi-isomorphism on ordinary parts (for the action of t).
items.note: The proof runs as follows. It tensors the correspondence with the graded pieces I^{n−1}_{Z,>w−1}/I^n_{Z,>w−1}. It factors it through ω̃^κ(−mD_{−,w} + D_{+,w}) using Lemma 4.3.14 and Corollary 4.4.3; this is where k′ is fixed. It then applies Lemma 2.4.4 and uses that (p) = I_{Z,>w−1} over 𝔖^tor_w. All of this takes place on the missing Iwahori-level model.

items.name: Compact open subgroups of P'(Q_p) decomposable with respect to w
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW, B_w := wBw^{-1}, with maximal torus T_w := wTw^{-1} = T and unipotent radical N_w := wNw^{-1} (N the unipotent radical of B), N̄_w the opposite unipotent radical, and T_w(Q_p)^{++} := wT(Q_p)^{++}w^{-1}. A compact open subgroup K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Q_p) is decomposable with respect to w if: (1) K_{p,P} = M_{K_{p,P}} ⋉ U_{K_{p,P}}, where M_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ M(Q_p) and U_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ U_P(Q_p)(1) (automatic if p > 2, Remark 3.4.7); (2) K_{p,P} has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to B_w: K_{p,P} = N_{w,K_{p,P}} × T_{w,K_{p,P}} × N̄_{w,K_{p,P}} (the factors being the intersections with N_w, T, N̄_w); (3) M_{K_{p,P}} is contained in the Iwahori subgroup of M(Q_p) with respect to B ∩ M = B_w ∩ M and has an Iwahori decomposition N_{M_{K_{p,P}}} × T_{w,K_{p,P}} × N̄_{M_{K_{p,P}}}.
items.note: The group P′(Q_p) of §3.4.2 (p. 36) is missing. It is generated by M(Q_p) and U_P(Q_p)(1) ≅ Q_p(1) ⊗ Sym²Z_p^g inside the group of self quasi-isogenies of the ordinary p-divisible group. No layer plans Iwahori factorizations K = N_K × T_K × N̄_K of compact open subgroups. The atlas's Iwahori material is the Iwahori–Bruhat double-coset decomposition (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.4, 'Prove the Cartan and Iwahori–Bruhat decompositions') and pro-p congruence subgroups (ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.3). Neither library has Iwahori subgroups or Iwahori factorizations.

items.name: Cofinality of decomposable compact open subgroups (Remark 5.1.1)
items.statement: For fixed w ∈ ^MW, the compact open subgroups of P'(Q_p) decomposable with respect to w are cofinal among all compact open subgroups of P'(Q_p).
items.note: Remark 5.1.1 gives no proof. The expected argument is short. The principal congruence subgroups P′(Z_p)_n, n ≥ 1, of P′(Z_p) form a neighbourhood basis of 1 (p. 38). Each is the product, in any order, of its intersections with T and with the root subgroups of P, which gives conditions (1)–(3). It is missing with the rest of §5.1.

items.name: Conjugating a decomposable subgroup into P'(Z_p) (Remark 5.1.2, corrected)
items.statement: Let t_0 = diag(1_g, p1_g) and let K_{p,P} be decomposable. For n large enough, t_0^n K_{p,P} t_0^{−n} ⊆ P'(Z_p) (printed t_0^{−n}K_{p,P}t_0^n; sourceIssues E104).
items.note: This is elementary group theory on the missing P′(Q_p). The direction was checked by direct computation. The printed t_0^{−n}K_{p,P}t_0^n (p. 53) enlarges the unipotent part instead (sourceIssues E104). P is the stabilizer of ⟨e_{g+1}, …, e_{2g}⟩ (p. 33), so P consists of block matrices (A 0; C D) and its unipotent radical of (1 0; C 1). For t_0 = diag(1_g, p1_g) one has t_0^n (1 0; C 1) t_0^{−n} = (1 0; p^nC 1), while t_0^{−n}(·)t_0^n multiplies C by p^{−n}. The Levi part M_{K_{p,P}} lies in M(Z_p) by condition (3) and is fixed by the conjugation. Hence t_0^nK_{p,P}t_0^{−n} ⊆ P′(Z_p) for n large. The same slip occurs in the proof of Theorem 5.1.4 (p. 53). It is printed t_0^{−r}K_{p,P}t_0^r ⊆ K′_{p,P}, where t_0^rK_{p,P}t_0^{−r} ⊆ K′_{p,P} is meant (sourceIssues E104).

items.name: Iwahori decomposition with respect to B (Remark 5.1.3)
items.statement: A decomposable K_{p,P} also has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to B: K_{p,P} = N_{K_{p,P}} × T_{w,K_{p,P}} × N̄_{K_{p,P}}, with N̄_{K_{p,P}} = N̄_{M_{K_{p,P}}} and N_{K_{p,P}} = N_{M_{K_{p,P}}} × U_{K_{p,P}}.
items.note: Remark 5.1.3 is stated without proof and follows from conditions (1)–(3) of the definition. No layer plans Iwahori factorizations of compact open subgroups; see the definition of decomposable subgroups.

items.name: Hecke correspondences on Igusa varieties for t ∈ T_w(Q_p)^{++}
items.statement: For decomposable K_{p,P} and t ∈ T_w(Q_p)^{++}, the Hecke correspondence p_1, p_2 : 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^p(tK_{p,P}t^{-1} ∩ K_{p,P})} ⇉ 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} of §3.4.13 (p_1 induced by the inclusion, p_2 by the action of t followed by the projection), on partial toroidal compactifications. For a formal scheme 𝔛 over Spf Z_p, X_{Z/p^nZ} denotes the corresponding scheme over Spec Z/p^nZ.
items.note: The Igusa varieties 𝔍𝔊_{K^pK_{p,P}} for compact open K_{p,P} ⊆ P′(Q_p), their partial toroidal compactifications and their Hecke correspondences (§§3.4.5–3.4.15, pp. 36–38) are not planned. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.1–IG.2 build Igusa varieties over central leaves, but only for the unitary PEL datum of Caraiani–Scholze fixed in IG.0. The other planned ordinary Igusa towers are Hilbert and unitary: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T5 ('Construct the finite Igusa torsors ... and their ordinary inverse tower'), OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O7 and AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L4. The Siegel analogue in Pilloni (2020) is the formal Igusa tower over the Klingen p-rank ≥ 1 locus (PAPER-PILLONI-20/formal-igusa-tower, missing).

items.name: Strict dynamic compactifications of Igusa Hecke correspondences (Theorem 5.1.4)
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW. For every compact open subgroup K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Q_p) decomposable with respect to w, every n ∈ Z_{≥0} and every t ∈ T_w(Q_p)^{++}, the correspondence ((IG^tor_{K^p(tK_{p,P}t^{-1} ∩ K_{p,P})})_{Z/p^nZ}, (IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}})_{Z/p^nZ}, p_1, p_2) admits a strict dynamic compactification.
items.note: The proof reduces to the Iwahori case (Proposition 4.4.4), using Lemma 2.1.34 for smaller subgroups and conjugation by t_0. All of these ingredients are the paper's own and missing. The conjugation should read t_0^rK_{p,P}t_0^{−r} ⊆ K′_{p,P}; see Remark 5.1.2.

items.name: Normalized trace correspondence on Igusa varieties (Lemma 5.2.2)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} be decomposable and t ∈ T_w(Q_p)^+. For the correspondence (𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^p(tK_{p,P}t^{-1} ∩ K_{p,P})}, 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}}, p_1, p_2), the map ⟨−w_{0,M}ρ − wρ, t⟩ Tr_{p_1} is a (integral) cohomological correspondence p_2^⋆O_{𝔍𝔊_{K^pK_{p,P}}} → p_1^!O_{𝔍𝔊_{K^pK_{p,P}}}; i.e. the trace of p_1 is divisible by ⟨w_{0,M}ρ + wρ, t⟩.
items.note: The proof reads 'Analogue to lemma 4.3.8'. Trace maps along the correspondences of the missing Igusa varieties, and their integral normalization, are the paper's own. The normalization of cohomological correspondences in Pilloni (2020) is also missing (PAPER-PILLONI-20/normalized-cohomological-correspondence).

items.name: Weight-0 higher Hida complexes at finite level
items.statement: For K_{p,P} decomposable with respect to w: RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}) := RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}}, O)^{ord} := lim_s RΓ((IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}})_{Z/p^sZ}, O)^{ord} and RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, cusp) := RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}}, O(−D))^{ord} := lim_s RΓ((IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}})_{Z/p^sZ}, O(−D))^{ord}, the ordinary part being taken (Theorem 2.5.1, legitimate by Theorem 5.1.4) for the correspondence of Lemma 5.2.2 attached to any t ∈ T_w^{++}(Q_p), with transition maps from Proposition 2.6.13.
items.note: The complex is a limit of ordinary parts of cohomology with support on the missing Igusa varieties. The ordinary part is legitimate by Theorem 5.1.4, and the transition maps come from Proposition 2.6.13. Every ingredient is unplanned.

items.name: Perfectness over the finite torus group ring (Proposition 5.2.3)
items.statement: For K_{p,P} decomposable with respect to w, RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}) and RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, cusp) are objects of D(Z_p[T(Q_p)]) and are perfect complexes of Z_p[T_w(Z_p)/T_{w,K_{p,P}}]-modules.
items.note: The proof is 'a consequence of theorem 2.6.10', part of the §2 formalism. Perfect complexes over the finite group ring Z_p[T_w(Z_p)/T_{w,K_{p,P}}] fall under the notion planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7; the complexes themselves are missing.

items.name: Independence of the compact (Proposition 5.2.5)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} and K'_{p,P} be compact open subgroups of P'(Q_p) decomposable with respect to w with T_{w,K_{p,P}} = T_{w,K'_{p,P}}. Then there is a natural quasi-isomorphism RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}) ≃ RΓ_w(K^pK'_{p,P}), and similarly RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, cusp) ≃ RΓ_w(K^pK'_{p,P}, cusp).
items.note: The paper presents the proposition as a generalization of Casselman's canonical lifting for Jacquet modules ([Cas], §4.1). SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.2 plans Jacquet functors ('For P=MN define unnormalized induction and N-coinvariants, then normalized induction/Jacquet functors') but not the canonical lifting. The proof compares Igusa varieties at the levels K^p·(t^{−m}K_{p,P}t^m ∩ t^nK_{p,P}t^{−n}) through an infinite diagram. Its maps are quasi-isomorphisms on ordinary parts by Proposition 2.8.2, which is missing.

items.name: The higher Hida complexes RΓ_w(K^p) and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Z_p) be decomposable with respect to w and (K_{p,P})_n := {M ∈ K_{p,P} : M mod p^n ∈ N(Z/p^n)}. Put RΓ_w(K^p) := lim_m colim_n RΓ_w(K^p(K_{p,P})_n) ⊗ Z/p^mZ, and define RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) in the same way from RΓ_w(K^p(K_{p,P})_n, cusp).
items.note: In dual (admissible) form, this generalizes Pilloni (2020)'s Λ-adic complex fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D)) of Theorem 11.3.1 (PAPER-PILLONI-20/thm-1-1-perfect-complex-M, missing) in three ways: from GSp4 to GSp_{2g}; from the Klingen stratum to every w ∈ ^MW; and from the one-parameter weight algebra Z_p[[Z_p^×]] to the whole weight space of T(Z_p). Derived inverse limits with lim¹ terms are planned in other settings (CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.2, 'Construct the derived inverse limit of complexes and the Milnor exact sequence'; DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7). The complex lim_m colim_n RΓ_w(K^p(K_{p,P})_n) ⊗ Z/p^mZ is not. The introduction (§1.4, p. 4) attaches these complexes to each w ∈ ^MW as RΓ_w(K^p, cusp/∅) ∈ D(Z_p[T(Q_p)] ⊗ T^sph). Here K^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} K_ℓ, and the abstract Hecke algebra T^sph also acts. T^sph is the restricted tensor product of the spherical Hecke algebras at the primes ℓ with K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ) hyperspecial. The introduction describes the complexes as the ordinary part of the cohomology of toroidal compactifications of the Igusa varieties, with support conditions that depend on w. These support conditions are chosen according to the Hecke correspondences of t ∈ T^+(Q_p), which acts on the Igusa tower through the map T(Q_p) → P′(Q_p) attached to w.

items.name: Admissibility and independence of K_{p,P} (Proposition 5.2.7)
items.statement: The complexes RΓ_w(K^p) and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) in D(Z_p[T(Q_p)]) are admissible (Definition 1.4.1: representable by a bounded complex of T'(Z_p)-modules M^• with M^i ≅ C^0(T'(Z_p), Z_p)^{n_i}, T'(Z_p) the pro-p subgroup of T(Z_p)), and their construction does not depend on the decomposable K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Z_p).
items.note: The proof takes minimal representatives M_n^• over Z_p[T′(Z_p/p^nZ_p)] (planned, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7) and shows that their ranks stabilize. It then uses lim_m colim_n Z/p^mZ[T′(Z_p/p^nZ_p)] = C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p), which rests on the density of locally constant functions (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0, 'Prove density of locally constant functions using finite clopen partitions of an arbitrary profinite space'). Admissible complexes (Definition 1.4.1, p. 4) and the complexes RΓ_w(K^p) are missing.
