In dual form and without the amplitude, the proposition generalizes Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.3.1(2) (PAPER-PILLONI-20/higher-hida-family-perfect-complex-over-Lambda, missing). The introduction states the admissibility of RΓ_w(K^p, cusp/∅) as Theorem 1.4.3(1) (p. 5).

items.name: Minimal representatives of perfect complexes
items.statement: Let R be a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m (here R = Z_p[H] with H = T'(Z_p/p^nZ_p) a finite p-group). Every perfect complex of R-modules is quasi-isomorphic to a minimal complex: a bounded complex M^• with M^i ≅ R^{k_i} finite free and all differentials zero modulo m. The ranks k_i = dim_{R/m} H^i(M^• ⊗^L_R R/m) are determined by the complex, and any quasi-isomorphism between minimal complexes is an isomorphism.
items.note: The P7 node covers the item completely. A perfect complex is pseudo-coherent. A quasi-isomorphism between minimal complexes reduces modulo m to a quasi-isomorphism between complexes with zero differentials, hence to an isomorphism, and Nakayama makes it an isomorphism. The ring used here, R = Z_p[H] with H = T′(Z_p/p^nZ_p) a finite p-group, is a complete noetherian local Z_p-algebra with residue field F_p. It lies within P7's scope ('complete Noetherian local O-algebras'). Pilloni (2020) needed a variant for complexes of flat complete modules of infinite rank, which P7 does not cover (PAPER-PILLONI-20/minimal-subcomplex-differentials-zero-mod-m, missing). The finite free case used here is covered. External input: C. B. Khare, J. A. Thorne, Potential automorphy and the Leopoldt conjecture, Amer. J. Math. 139 (2017), no. 5, 1205–1273, §2.2

items.name: The w-twisted T(Q_p)-action
items.statement: On RΓ_w(K^p) and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) the action of T(Q_p) is twisted by w: t ∈ T(Q_p) acts through the Hecke action of wtw^{-1} ∈ T_w(Q_p), so that T^{++}(Q_p) acts through T_w(Q_p)^{++}. After this twist the compact K_{p,P} is dropped from the notation.
items.note: This is a convention on the missing complexes RΓ_w(K^p). The paper motivates it by §4.1.5: 'the relevant Igusa variety is embedded via w inside the global Shimura variety'.

items.name: Higher Hida complexes in fixed weight for general decomposable level (§5.3.1)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Z_p) be decomposable with respect to w. The map 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} → A_g^tor gives a semi-abelian scheme A and hence the M-torsor M_dR over 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} (as in §4.3.1); for κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} let ω^κ be the corresponding sheaf. Define RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, κ) := RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}}, ω^κ)^{ord} = lim_n RΓ(IG^tor_{K^pK_{p,P},Z/p^nZ}, ω^κ)^{ord}, the ordinary part for the action of some t ∈ T_w^{++}(Q_p), and similarly RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, κ, cusp) with ω^κ(−D). For κ trivial these are the complexes of §5.2.1. They are T(Q_p)-modules, and the action of T(Q_p) is locally algebraic of weight ν = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ.
items.note: The M-torsor M_dR over 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} comes from the semi-abelian scheme pulled back along 𝔍𝔊^tor → A_g^tor (§4.3.1). Associated bundles and the Siegel Hodge bundle are planned on Shimura varieties (AutomorphicBundles:B0, B4), not over formal Igusa varieties, which are themselves missing. This complex extends the Iwahori-level complexes of §4.4 to any decomposable level. For κ trivial it is the weight-0 complex of §5.2.1.

items.name: Reduction of the de Rham torsor to the Igusa tower (Proposition 5.3.3)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} be decomposable, so that 1 → U_{K_{p,P}} → K_{p,P} → M_{K_{p,P}} → 1 is exact and 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} → 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}} is an M_{K_{p,P}}-torsor. There is a map of torsors over 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{p,P}}, 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} → M_dR, equivariant for M_{K_{p,P}} → M_μ. It is induced by the Hodge–Tate map T_p(A[p^∞]^{et}) → ω_{A^t} (of pro-étale sheaves), which induces an isomorphism T_p(A[p^∞]^{et}) ⊗_{Z_p} O_{𝔍𝔊_{U_{K_{p,P}}}} ≅ ω_{A^t} ⊗_{O_{𝔍𝔊_{K_{p,P}}}} O_{𝔍𝔊_{U_{K_{p,P}}}}.
items.note: HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups:T0 plans the finite-level Hodge–Tate map ('Build the finite-level Hodge–Tate map using Cartier duality and differentials of characters'). T2 plans the Hodge–Tate reduction on the pro-étale site of the generic fibre ('Construct the Hodge–Tate parabolic reduction and Levi torsor, compare its Levi torsor with the de Rham/Hodge torsor'). Neither plans this integral statement: the isomorphism T_p(A[p^∞]^et) ⊗ O ≅ ω_{A^t} over the formal Igusa variety, and the resulting M_{K_{p,P}}-equivariant map of torsors 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pU_{K_{p,P}}} → M_dR. This is the GSp_{2g} counterpart of Pilloni (2020)'s §9.4 isomorphism for the universal multiplicative subgroup (PAPER-PILLONI-20/hodge-tate-isomorphism-multiplicative-subgroup, missing), which was source-routed to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 and T5.

items.name: Projection of ω^κ to the lowest weight vector
items.statement: Let B_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ B and N_{K_{p,P}} = K_{p,P} ∩ N, and π : 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}} → 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}} the (affine) T_{w,K_{p,P}}-torsor. The map O_{M_dR} → O_{𝔍𝔊_{U_{K_{p,P}}}} deduced from Proposition 5.3.3 induces a surjective map of sheaves on 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, ω^κ → (π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}}} ⊗ w_{0,M}κ)^{T_{w,K_{p,P}}}, thought of as the projection to the lowest weight vector.
items.note: This generalizes Pilloni (2020)'s projection Sym^kω_G → ω_{H_n}^{⊗k} ≅ F^k_{n,n}, with its kernel KΩ^{(k,r)} (§§9.4, 10.7; PAPER-PILLONI-20/highest-weight-projection-and-kernel-K-Omega, missing). The generalization runs from GSp4 and the Klingen parabolic to GSp_{2g}, to every w, and to every κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+}. It rests on two missing inputs: Proposition 5.3.3, and the fact that 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}} → 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}} is an affine T_{w,K_{p,P}}-torsor. On p. 56 the character is printed ω_{0,M}κ, and once the subscript K^pU(Z_p) appears. The intended forms are w_{0,M}κ and K^pN_{K_{p,P}}, as in the adjacent displays.

items.name: Vanishing of the ordinary cohomology of the kernel of the lowest-weight projection
items.statement: Let 𝒦 be the kernel of ω^κ → (π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}}} ⊗ w_{0,M}κ)^{T_{w,K_{p,P}}} on 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}. Then RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, 𝒦)^{ord} = 0; consequently RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, ω^κ)^{ord} = RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, (π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}}} ⊗ w_{0,M}κ)^{T_{w,K_{p,P}}})^{ord}.
items.note: The paper's whole proof is the sentence 'One checks that RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, K)^{ord} = 0 as in [Pil20], sect. 10.7 for example'. The GSp4 argument cited there is Pilloni (2020), Lemma 10.7.1: U is divisible by p on the kernel KΩ^{(k,r)} (PAPER-PILLONI-20/U-divisible-by-p-on-K-Omega, missing). The GSp_{2g} version, for all κ and w, has to be written out. The kernel and the complexes are missing. External input: V. Pilloni, Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights, Duke Math. J. 169 (2020), no. 9, 1647–1807, §10.7 (the argument invoked)

items.name: Control theorem (Theorem 5.3.5)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} ⊆ P'(Z_p) be decomposable with respect to w, T_{K_{p,P}} := w^{-1}T_{w,K_{p,P}}w ⊆ T(Z_p), κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} and ν = −w^{-1}w_{0,M}(κ+ρ) − ρ. With T(Q_p) acting on RΓ_w(K^p) through the w-twisted action, there is a canonical isomorphism RHom_{T_{K_{p,P}}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p)) ≃ RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, κ), and similarly RHom_{T_{K_{p,P}}}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p, cusp)) ≃ RΓ_w(K^pK_{p,P}, κ, cusp).
items.note: This generalizes Pilloni (2020)'s control theorem, Theorem 11.3.1(3) (PAPER-PILLONI-20/higher-hida-control-theorem-all-weights, missing). The generalization runs from GSp4 with one weight direction (Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]]) to GSp_{2g} with the full torus T(Z_p), and from the Klingen stratum to every w. The proof reduces to Borel level by a version of Proposition 5.2.5, passes to the affine torsor 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}} → 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, and applies the lowest-weight projection. It then exchanges sheaf and group cohomology, and the factor −w^{−1}w_{0,M}ρ − ρ is absorbed by the normalization of the trace. Every ingredient is missing.

items.name: The complexes RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ)
items.statement: Let ν = ν_alg χ : T(Z_p) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× with ν_alg ∈ X^⋆(T) and χ of finite order, and κ := −w_{0,M}w(ν_alg + ρ) − ρ. Put RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ) := RHom_{T(Z_p)}(ν, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗ Z_p(ζ_{p^n})), define RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ, cusp) likewise from RΓ_w(K^p, cusp), and write RΓ_w(K^p, κ) for the case χ trivial.
items.note: These definitions are made on the missing complexes RΓ_w(K^p). The weight relation κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν_alg + ρ) − ρ inverts ν_alg = −w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) − ρ; this was checked by direct computation, using w_{0,M}² = 1 and the linearity of the Weyl action.

items.name: Comparison with the fixed-weight complexes of §4.4
items.statement: For κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+} and χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^×: RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ) = RΓ_w(K^p, κ) and RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) = RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ), the left-hand sides being the Iwahori-level complexes of §4.4; the notation drops K_{w,p,P} because ordinary cohomology does not depend on the compact (Proposition 5.2.7).
items.note: The paper gives only a one-line justification for these equalities: the ordinary cohomology does not depend on the compact (Proposition 5.2.7). They combine Theorem 5.3.5 at K_{p,P} = K_{w,p,P} with the identification 𝔖^tor_w ≅ 𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pK_{w,p,P}} of Lemma 4.1.7. For χ ≠ 1 they also need the sheaf ω^κ(χ) of the level-K_{p,1,n} model to match the χ-isotypic part on the Igusa side. The paper does not spell this out; compare Remark 1.4.6 (p. 5): 'the definition of the level structure on the Shimura variety and the Igusa variety differ slightly'. All objects involved are missing.

items.name: The Iwasawa algebra Λ and the complexes M_w^•, M_{w,cusp}^•
items.statement: Λ := Z_p[[T(Z_p)]]. Define M_w^• := RHom_{T(Z_p)}(1, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ) and M_{w,cusp}^• := RHom_{T(Z_p)}(1, RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ).
items.note: Only Λ is planned. Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]], with T(Z_p) ≅ (Z_p^×)^{g+1}, is a completed group ring as planned in PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1 ('R[[G]] = lim_(n,U) (R/I^n)[G/U]'). Pilloni (2020)'s Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] was marked planned there for the same reason (PAPER-PILLONI-20/iwasawa-algebra-universal-character). Neither library has completed group rings. The complexes M_w^• and M_{w,cusp}^•, built from the missing RΓ_w(K^p) by a completed tensor product and derived T(Z_p)-invariants, are not planned. They generalize Pilloni (2020)'s perfect Λ-complex M of Theorem 1.1 (PAPER-PILLONI-20/thm-1-1-perfect-complex-M, missing) to GSp_{2g}, to every w, and to the whole weight space. Lemma 5.4.1 (p. 56) states that M_w^• and M_{w,cusp}^• are perfect complexes of Λ-modules. The introduction (§1.4, p. 5) defines the same complexes, and calls them perfect, with the uncompleted tensor product ⊗_{Z_p} in place of ⊗̂_{Z_p}. The completed tensor product of §5.4 is the one for which perfectness holds (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: M_w^• and M_{w,cusp}^• are perfect (Lemma 5.4.1)
items.statement: M_w^• and M_{w,cusp}^• are perfect complexes of Λ-modules.
items.note: The lemma generalizes Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.3.1(2), without its amplitude (PAPER-PILLONI-20/higher-hida-family-perfect-complex-over-Lambda, missing). Perfect complexes are planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7 over local rings. Λ is a finite product of complete regular local rings: T(Z_p)/T′(Z_p) = T(F_p) has order prime to p, and its characters take values in Z_p^×. So P7 applies factor by factor. The proof uses Proposition 5.2.7 and RHom_{T′(Z_p)}(1, C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p) ⊗̂ Λ) = Λ[0], both unplanned.

items.name: Anti-equivalence between admissible complexes and perfect Λ-complexes
items.statement: The functor i : M ↦ Hom_{Z_p}(M, Z_p) (continuous Z_p-dual) is an anti-equivalence from admissible complexes (with their T(Z_p)-action) to perfect complexes of Λ-modules, with quasi-inverse i^{-1} = Hom_{Z_p}(−, Z_p); this uses that Λ is the algebra of measures on T(Z_p). With j : M ↦ (M ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ)^{T(Z_p)}, the composite j ∘ i^{-1} is the duality functor Hom_Λ(−, Λ) on perfect complexes of Λ-modules; on Λ[0] this is the isomorphism (Hom_{Z_p}(Λ, Z_p) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ)^{T(Z_p)} → Hom_Λ(Λ, Λ).
items.note: The module-level inputs are planned. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L0 and L1 plan Λ as the algebra of Z_p-valued measures on T(Z_p) ('Define a K-valued bounded measure on a profinite space X as the continuous K-linear dual of C(X,K)'; 'Prove the topological O-algebra equivalence between integral measures and O[[G]]'). CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.3 plans continuous duals with biduality in the admissible category ('Construct continuous O-linear and Pontryagin duals with their correct coefficient targets and compact/discrete topologies'; 'Establish biduality only in its compact/discrete or admissible category'). What is not planned is the anti-equivalence between admissible complexes and perfect complexes of Λ-modules, and the identification of j ∘ i^{−1} with Hom_Λ(−, Λ). Admissible complexes are those of Definition 1.4.1: bounded complexes with terms C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p)^{n_i}. The paper checks the identification on Λ[0].

items.name: Recovering RΓ_w(K^p) from M_w^• (Lemma 5.4.2)
items.statement: RΓ_w(K^p) = RHom_{Z_p}(RHom_Λ(M_w^•, Λ), Z_p), and similarly RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) = RHom_{Z_p}(RHom_Λ(M_{w,cusp}^•, Λ), Z_p).
items.note: This applies the anti-equivalence between admissible and perfect complexes (missing) to RΓ_w(K^p) and M_w^•, both missing.

items.name: Geometric formula for M_w^• in the universal weight (Remark 5.4.3)
items.statement: Let K_{p,P} be decomposable with T_{w,K_{p,P}} = T(Z_p). Then M_w^• = RΓ(𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pB_{K_{p,P}}}, (π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}}} ⊗ Λ)^{T_w(Z_p)})^{ord}, where T_w(Z_p), the diagonal torus of B_{K_{p,P}}, acts on π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊^tor_{K^pN_{K_{p,P}}}} by the torsor action and on Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]] via the character w_{0,M}κ^{univ}, i.e. the composite T_w(Z_p) → T(Z_p) (conjugation by w^{-1}) followed by w^{-1}w_{0,M}κ^{univ} : T(Z_p) → Λ^×; here ν^{univ} : T(Z_p) → Λ^× is the universal character and κ^{univ} := −w_{0,M}w(ν^{univ} + ρ) − ρ.
items.note: This generalizes Pilloni (2020)'s Λ-adic sheaf 𝔉^κ = (π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊(p^∞)} ⊗̂ Λ)^{Z_p^×} over the Klingen Igusa tower (PAPER-PILLONI-20/p-adic-interpolation-sheaf-F-kappa, missing). The generalization runs to GSp_{2g}, to every w, and to the universal character of T(Z_p). The nearest planned constructions are OverconvergentAutomorphicForms:O1 (equivariant sheaves from cocycles) and O8 (Siegel coefficient sheaves 'on the proven anticanonical domains'). Neither builds this Λ-adic sheaf on Siegel Igusa varieties.

items.name: Interpolation property of M_w^• (Remark 5.4.3)
items.statement: For every ν = ν_alg χ : T(Z_p) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× with ν_alg ∈ X^⋆(T) and χ of finite order, and κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν_alg + ρ) − ρ, one has M_w^• ⊗_{Λ,−ν} Z_p(ζ_{p^n}) = RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ), where Λ → Z_p(ζ_{p^n}) is the specialization at −ν (the tensor product being derived); similarly for M_{w,cusp}^•.
items.note: This follows from the control theorem by derived base change of perfect complexes (planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7). It generalizes Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.3.1(3) and Theorem 1.1(1) (PAPER-PILLONI-20/higher-hida-control-theorem-all-weights, missing), to GSp_{2g} and the whole weight space. On p. 57 the weight is printed κ = −w_{0,M}w(ν + ρ) − ρ with ν = ν_alg·χ. ν_alg is meant, as in §5.3.4; the item uses the corrected form.

items.name: Ordinary Hecke algebras and the ordinary Hecke eigenvariety
items.statement: T_w is the image of the Hecke algebra in End(M_w^•); it is a finite Λ-algebra. E_w := Spec T_w → Spec Λ is the ordinary Hecke eigenvariety. T_{w,cusp} is defined in the same way from M_{w,cusp}^•.
items.note: The general construction is planned in IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.2 ('For a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex define its finite image algebras'). The instance is missing, because M_w^• and the Hecke action on it are missing. §1.4 (p. 4) specifies the Hecke algebra as T^sph, the restricted tensor product of the spherical Hecke algebras at the primes ℓ with K_ℓ hyperspecial. Its action on RΓ_w(K^p), through prime-to-p Hecke correspondences on Igusa varieties, is not constructed in §§4–5. PadicFamilies:L0 plans ordinary Hecke algebras only for modular forms. The GSp4 analogue is PAPER-PILLONI-20/hecke-algebra-on-ordinary-complex-finite-semilocal, missing for the same reason. The introduction (§1.4, p. 5) gives the same definition. There T_w and T_{w,cusp} are the finite Λ-algebras equal to the images of T^sph in End(M_w^•) and End(M_{w,cusp}^•).

items.name: Serre duality for higher Hida complexes in fixed weight (Theorem 5.5.1)
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW, κ and χ : T(Z/p^nZ) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× as in the definition of RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ), and d = g(g+1)/2. There is a duality (perfect pairing) RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ) ⊗ RΓ_{w_{0,M}ww_0}(K^p, −w_{0,M}κ − 2ρ_nc, w_0χ^{-1}, cusp) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})[−d] for which the adjoint of t ∈ T(Q_p) is w_0t^{-1} ∈ T(Q_p).
items.note: The proof takes K_{p,P} = {M ≡ 1 mod p^n} and applies Theorem 2.7.4 (p. 24), the duality for ordinary parts of cohomology with support, to Igusa varieties. It then conjugates by w_{0,M} to pass from the T^−(Q_p)-ordinary part to the ordinary part. Coherent Grothendieck–Serre duality in dimension greater than 1 is planned nowhere. SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3 lists 'Serre duality' among curve topics, and PAPER-PILLONI-20 sent Grothendieck duality by source route to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:A0-extension. Here d = g(g+1)/2 is the dimension of the Siegel variety.

items.name: Serre duality for the Λ-complexes (Theorem 5.5.2)
items.statement: There is a perfect pairing M_w^• ⊗ M_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp}^• → Λ[−d] (d = g(g+1)/2) for which the adjoint of t ∈ T(Q_p) is w_0t^{-1}.
items.note: The proof reads 'This follows as in the previous theorem'. The statement is missing with Theorem 5.5.1 and the complexes M_w^•. The introduction states the result as Theorem 1.4.8 (p. 5), where the pairing is written M_w^• ⊗_Λ M^•_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp} → Λ[−d]. Theorem 1.4.8 makes two further assertions. First, the adjoint of [K_ℓgK_ℓ] is [K_ℓg^{−1}K_ℓ] for every prime ℓ ≠ p with K_ℓ = G(Z_ℓ) and every g ∈ G(Q_ℓ). Second, the pairing is compatible with classical Serre duality after specialization to locally algebraic dominant weights. Neither assertion is stated in the body. Read as Λ-bilinear, the pairing cannot have adjoint w_0t^{−1} = t^{−1} for central t ∈ T(Z_p). The Λ-structure of the second factor has to be twisted by the involution ι of Λ induced by t ↦ w_0t^{−1}, which is t ↦ c(t)^{−1}t for GSp_{2g} with c the similitude character. Weight ν on M_w^• then pairs with weight ν∘ι on the cuspidal factor, as in Theorem 5.5.1. The unsubscripted ⊗ of Theorem 5.5.2 has to be read in the same way (sourceIssues E7). The paper does not define d. It is g(g+1)/2, the dimension of the Siegel Shimura variety (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Affineness of the ordinary locus in the minimal compactification
items.statement: Let K_p ⊆ G(Q_p) be the Iwahori subgroup and K_{Id,p,P} = K_p ∩ P(Q_p). The image in the minimal compactification of (Ig_{K^pK_{Id,p,P}})_{Z/pZ} is affine. Here (Ig_{K^pK_{Id,p,P}})_{Z/pZ} is the component of the ordinary locus of the special fibre of the Iwahori-level Siegel variety corresponding to w = Id, i.e. the stratum where all Gr_{g+i} are multiplicative. This is asserted, without proof, in the proof of Proposition 5.6.3 (case g = 2, w = Id).
items.locator: §5.6, proof of Proposition 5.6.3 (case w = Id), p. 58
items.note: This is asserted without proof in the case w = Id of Proposition 5.6.3, for g = 2. There the Igusa variety is printed as (Ig_{K_pK_{w,p,P}})_{Z/pZ}, with the subscript K_p in place of the prime-to-p level K^p [sourceIssues E98]. The planned neighbours do not cover it. ShimuraCompactifications:C5 plans 'the Hodge-line positivity and graded-section finite-generation statements that yield the integral minimal compactification', at hyperspecial level. IgusaVarietiesAndTorsionConcentration:IG.2 plans 'Prove affineness of C^(X,*) and Ig^(X,*)', including 'compute the ordinary case', but for the unitary datum of Caraiani–Scholze. The Hasse invariant of a BT₁ group was source-routed by PAPER-PILLONI-20 to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0. The genus-two Siegel Hasse invariants go to the proposed SiegelModularFormsModPn. PAPER-PILLONI-20 likewise recorded the affineness of the ordinary locus in the minimal compactification as missing (PAPER-PILLONI-20/ordinary-locus-acyclic-resolution-and-complexes-M-N).

items.name: The p-rank ≥ 1 locus of the Siegel threefold is covered by two affines
items.statement: For g = 2, the p-rank ≥ 1 locus in the special fibre of the minimal compactification is covered by two affine opens and hence has coherent cohomological dimension 1; for w the length-one element of ^MW, S^tor_{(w−1,w+1)} ∖ D_{w,+} maps into this locus.
items.note: For genus 2 at spherical level, this is the covering of Pilloni (2020), §14.8 (PAPER-PILLONI-20/two-affine-covering-of-p-rank-one-locus-and-overconvergent-subcomplex, missing, routed to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory). There 𝔛^{⋆,≥1} = D(s_1) ∪ D(s_2), where s_1 and s_2 lift powers of Ha and Ha′ to sections of the ample sheaf (det ω)^{n(p²−1)}. The second clause, that S^tor_{(w−1,w+1)} ∖ D_{w,+} lies in the p-rank ≥ 1 locus, is asserted without proof ('We observe that'). It concerns the missing Iwahori-level model.

items.name: Conjecture 5.6.1 (integral cohomological amplitude of higher Hida complexes)
items.statement: Conjecture. Let g ≥ 1, G = GSp_{2g}, d = g(g+1)/2, let K^p ⊆ G(A_f^p) be a neat compact open subgroup and let w ∈ ^MW (the minimal-length representatives of the cosets W_M·w of W, W_M the Weyl group of the Siegel Levi M), of length ℓ(w). Then the higher Hida complex RΓ_w(K^p) ∈ D(Z_p[T(Q_p)]) of §5.2.6 is an admissible complex of amplitude [ℓ(w), d], and the cuspidal higher Hida complex RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) is an admissible complex of amplitude [0, ℓ(w)]. (Definition 1.4.1: with T′(Z_p) the pro-p subgroup of T(Z_p), a complex in D(Z_p[T′(Z_p)]) is admissible of amplitude [a, b] if it is represented by a complex M^• concentrated in degrees [a, b] with M^i ≅ C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p)^{n_i} as T′(Z_p)-modules.)
items.note: Conjecture 5.6.1 (p. 58), announced in Remark 1.4.4 (p. 5), which adds that it holds for w = Id and for the longest element w_0^M of ^MW in every genus. It should be formalised as a Prop-valued statement about RΓ_w(K^p) and never assumed. No atlas layer plans higher Hida complexes. PadicFamilies plans abstract ordinary projectors (L0a) and one-degree Hida families for modular curves and totally real fields (L0, L5). The OverconvergentAutomorphicForms document excludes this direction: 'Eigenvarieties, general finite-slope classicality, and higher Coleman cohomology are not endpoints of this roadmap.' Admissible complexes (Definition 1.4.1, p. 4) are also unplanned. Their building block C^0(T′(Z_p), Z_p) is Mathlib's ContinuousMap. Remark 1.4.2 (p. 5) says an admissible complex is dual to a perfect Λ′-complex; that duality rests on identifying integral measures with the completed group ring, which PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0–L1 plan. The conjecture generalises the amplitude-[0,1] statement of Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.3.1(2) (GSp_4, Klingen level, one weight variable), to GSp_{2g}, to every w ∈ ^MW and to the whole weight space.

items.name: Remark 5.6.2 (the conjecture in terms of the perfect Λ-complexes M_w^•)
items.statement: Let Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]], M_w^• = RHom_{T(Z_p)}(1, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ) and M^•_{w,cusp} = RHom_{T(Z_p)}(1, RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗̂_{Z_p} Λ). These are perfect complexes of Λ-modules (Lemma 5.4.1). Conjecture 5.6.1 for w is equivalent to the following: M_w^• is a perfect complex of Λ-modules of amplitude [ℓ(w), d], and M^•_{w,cusp} is a perfect complex of Λ-modules of amplitude [0, ℓ(w)]. The equivalence comes from Lemma 5.4.2, RΓ_w(K^p) = RHom_{Z_p}(RHom_Λ(M_w^•, Λ), Z_p), and similarly for cuspidal cohomology. It also uses Remark 1.4.2: the Z_p-dual of an admissible complex of amplitude [a, b] is a perfect complex of amplitude [−b, −a]. The conjecture is compatible with the duality between cuspidal and non-cuspidal complexes.
items.locator: §5.6, Remark 5.6.2, p. 58 (with Lemmas 5.4.1–5.4.2, pp. 56–57, and Remark 1.4.2, p. 5)
items.note: Remark 5.6.2 (p. 58) refers to Lemma 5.4.2 (p. 57): RΓ_w(K^p) = RHom_{Z_p}(RHom_Λ(M_w^•, Λ), Z_p). That lemma is proved from the anti-equivalence M ↦ Hom_{Z_p}(M, Z_p) between admissible complexes and perfect Λ-complexes, which 'uses that Λ is the algebra of measures on T(Z_p)'. Perfectness of M_w^• and M^•_{w,cusp} is Lemma 5.4.1 (p. 56). Two inputs are planned: perfect complexes, duals and Tor-amplitude over complete local rings (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7), and the identification of integral measures with O[[G]] (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1: 'Prove the topological O-algebra equivalence between integral measures and O[[G]]'). Three pieces are planned nowhere: the functor M ↦ RHom_{T(Z_p)}(1, M ⊗̂ Λ), the equivalence of the two amplitude conditions, and the compatibility with the Serre duality M_w^• ⊗ M^•_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp} → Λ[−d] of Theorem 1.4.8 (5.5.1). The equivalence is a theorem even though both sides are conjectural.

items.name: Proposition 5.6.3 for g = 1 (the modular curve)
items.statement: For g = 1 (so d = 1, and ^MW = {Id, w_0^M} with ℓ(Id) = 0 and ℓ(w_0^M) = 1), Conjecture 5.6.1 holds. More strongly: RΓ_{Id}(K^p) and RΓ_{Id}(K^p, cusp) are concentrated in degree 0, and RΓ_{w_0^M}(K^p) and RΓ_{w_0^M}(K^p, cusp) are concentrated in degree 1.
items.locator: §5.6, Proposition 5.6.3 and first lines of its proof, p. 58
items.note: The paper does not prove Proposition 5.6.3 for g = 1 (p. 58). It says: 'The case g = 1 is easy and was treated in [BP22]'. That is G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Hida and Coleman theories on the modular curve, Épijournal Géom. Algébrique 6 (2022), Art. 16. The atlas does not cover it; it should be added as a prerequisite and serves as the source. For w = Id the cuspidal statement is the higher Hida form of Hida's theorem that ordinary Λ-adic cusp forms are finite projective over the weight algebra. PadicFamilies L0 plans that classical statement ('finite flatness/control statements for ordinary cuspidal modules and Hecke algebras over weight Iwasawa algebras'), but for q-expansions over a one-variable weight algebra. It does not plan the complexes RΓ_w(K^p) over Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]], with T the diagonal torus of GSp_2 = GL_2. Nor does it plan the degree-1 statements for w_0^M or the non-cuspidal ones. The comparison with L0 must be proved, not assumed. External input: [BP22] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Hida and Coleman theories on the modular curve, Épijournal Géom. Algébrique 6 (2022), Art. 16 (no specific statement cited)

items.name: Proposition 5.6.3 for g = 2 (integral vanishing for GSp_4; Theorem 1.4.3(2))
items.statement: Let g = 2 (G = GSp_4, d = 3) and let K^p ⊆ G(A_f^p) be neat. For every w ∈ ^MW, RΓ_w(K^p) is an admissible complex of amplitude [ℓ(w), 3] and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) is an admissible complex of amplitude [0, ℓ(w)]. Equivalently (Remark 5.6.2), M_w^• and M^•_{w,cusp} are perfect complexes of Λ-modules of amplitudes [ℓ(w), 3] and [0, ℓ(w)] respectively.
items.locator: §5.6, Proposition 5.6.3 and proof, p. 58; Theorem 1.4.3(2), p. 5
items.note:
Proof on p. 58. By the amplitude criterion on residual fibres (planned; a separate item) it suffices to bound M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗_Λ F_p = RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, cusp) ⊗ Z/pZ for every residual character.
- w = Id: this is a direct summand of the coherent cohomology of the ordinary Igusa variety mod p. It lies in degree 0 because the image of that variety in the minimal compactification is affine and Lan's relative vanishing holds.
- w of length one: a direct summand of RΓ(S^tor_{(w−1,w+1)} ∖ D_{w,+}, ω^κ(−cusp)(−kD_{w,−})) for k large, where D_{w,−} = Z_{2,>1} [printed without the twist by −kD_{w,−}; sourceIssues E113]. That space lies in the p-rank ≥ 1 locus, which has cohomological dimension 1 in the minimal compactification (two affines).
- w of length two: the paper proves the dual non-cuspidal statement for the length-one element ('there is no non-zero section with non-trivial support').
- The proof leaves implicit the remaining bounds: the length-three element, and the non-cuspidal complexes. They follow from the Serre duality of Theorem 1.4.8 (5.5.1) and from dimension 3.
This generalises Pilloni (2020), Theorem 11.3.1(2) (perfect in degrees [0,1], Klingen level, one weight variable) to the three-variable Λ and all four elements of ^MW. Remark 5.6.4 (p. 58) says the argument does not extend to general g. Planned nowhere; the three geometric inputs are separate items. Besides the bounds that the proof leaves implicit, the length-one case has a recorded gap [sourceIssues E113]. Here D_{w,−} is non-empty, and the paper passes to the untwisted cohomology of S^tor_{(w−1,w+1)} ∖ D_{w,+}, which drops the support condition along D_{w,−}. The twisted direct summand comes from Proposition 2.5.4 (with Lemma 2.5.3), and the cohomological-dimension step must then be applied to the twisted sheaf. Only the proof is affected. The amplitude [0, 1], and with it Proposition 5.6.3 (= Theorem 1.4.3(2), p. 5), still hold.

items.name: Amplitude of perfect Λ-complexes is detected on residual fibres
items.statement: Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]] is a finite product of complete Noetherian local rings, each with residue field F_p. Indeed, T(Z_p) = T(F_p) × T′(Z_p) with T′(Z_p) pro-p, and every character of T(F_p) takes values in μ_{p−1} ⊆ Z_p^×. The ring maps Λ → F_p correspond bijectively, by restriction to T(Z_p) ⊆ Λ^×, to the characters T(Z_p) → F_p^×; each such character factors through T(F_p). A perfect complex M of Λ-modules has amplitude [a, b], i.e. it is quasi-isomorphic to a complex of finite projective Λ-modules in degrees [a, b], if and only if M ⊗^L_Λ F_p has cohomology only in degrees [a, b] for every ring map Λ → F_p.
items.note: The paper uses this in one sentence (p. 58): 'It suffices to prove that M_w^• ⊗_Λ F_p and M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗_Λ F_p have the correct amplitude as F_p-vector spaces for all the maps Λ → F_p'. Checked by direct computation. For p odd, T(Z_p) = T(F_p) × T′(Z_p) with T′(Z_p) ≅ Z_p^{g+1} pro-p, and the characters of T(F_p) = (F_p^×)^{g+1} take values in μ_{p−1} ⊂ Z_p. Hence Λ = ∏_χ Z_p[[T′(Z_p)]] ≅ ∏_χ Z_p[[X_1, …, X_{g+1}]], a product of (p−1)^{g+1} complete regular local rings with residue field F_p. For p = 2, T(Z_2) is pro-2 and Λ is local. On each factor, a perfect complex has a minimal complex whose ranks are dim H^i(M ⊗^L F_p), which gives the criterion. Neither library has completed group rings or minimal complexes. In the proof of Proposition 5.6.3 (p. 58) the residual fibres are fixed-weight complexes at Iwahori level: M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗_Λ F_p = RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, cusp) ⊗ Z/pZ, and likewise for M^•_w without the cuspidal condition. Here κ is the residual character, K_p ⊆ G(Q_p) is the Iwahori subgroup and K_{w,p,P} = wK_pw^{−1} ∩ P(Q_p). This is the group written K_{p,P,w} in Lemma 4.1.7 (p. 41), with n = 1. On each local factor of Λ the criterion is the paper's Lemma 2.6.7 (p. 22): over a local ring A, a pseudo-coherent complex M^• such that M^• ⊗^L_A A/m_A is perfect of amplitude [a, b] is itself perfect of amplitude [a, b]. External input: standard commutative algebra: minimal complexes over a Noetherian local ring (cf. [KT17] C. Khare, J. Thorne, Amer. J. Math. 139 (2017), §2.2, used for minimal representatives in the proof of Proposition 5.2.7)

items.name: Vanishing of relative cohomology from the toroidal to the minimal compactification ([Lan17], Thm 8.6)
items.statement: In the form invoked in the proof of Proposition 5.6.3: for the toroidal compactification of the Siegel modular variety and its minimal compactification, reduced modulo p, the higher direct images of the subcanonical extensions ω^κ(−cusp) of the automorphic vector bundles vanish under the natural map. In the paper's words, ‘the relative cohomology to the minimal compactification vanishes’.
items.note: Used on p. 58 for the compactified ordinary Igusa variety mod p (w = Id): 'the relative cohomology to the minimal compactification vanishes ([Lan17], thm. 8.6)'. AutomorphicBundles B3 plans only 'the pushforward to the minimal compactification as a coherent sheaf'. ShimuraCompactifications C3 requires the vanishing of higher direct images to be 'a separate theorem with the relevant coefficient hypotheses', and no layer states it. The extraction of Pilloni (2020) found the same gap and routed it to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes. That brief asks for Lan's Theorem 8.6 in the form of his Definition 8.5: formally subcanonical quasi-coherent sheaves, any neat level, over a Z_(p)-algebra, hence also modulo p^n, and locally over the minimal compactification. Here it is needed at Iwahori level and for sheaves on the Igusa cover, where the hypotheses of Lan's Definition 8.5 must be checked. It is one theorem for both papers and is stated once. External input: [Lan17] K.-W. Lan, Integral models of toroidal compactifications with projective cone decompositions, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2017, no. 11, 3237–3280, Theorem 8.6

items.name: Finite flat correspondence on a quasi-compact rigid space and the maps T, T^t
items.statement: Let 𝒳̄ be a quasi-compact rigid space and let p̄_1, p̄_2 : 𝒞̄ → 𝒳̄ be a correspondence over 𝒳̄ with p̄_1 and p̄_2 finite flat. For a subset 𝒮 ⊆ 𝒳̄ put T(𝒮) = p̄_2(p̄_1^{−1}(𝒮)) and T^t(𝒮) = p̄_1(p̄_2^{−1}(𝒮)).
items.note: pp. 58–59. By Remark 6.1.2 (p. 58), p̄_1 and p̄_2 can rarely both be finite flat on a toroidal compactification for one cone decomposition; the paper keeps the assumption for simplicity. For schemes, the extraction of Pilloni (2020) records a correspondence as library (a span). Here the objects are quasi-compact rigid (adic) spaces over Q_p, whose finite and flat maps and correspondences are planned in AdicSpacesPartII.

items.name: Open/closed support condition (Definition 6.1.3)
items.statement: An open/closed support condition for the correspondence 𝒞̄ is a pair (𝒰, 𝒵) with the following properties: 𝒰 ⊆ 𝒳̄ is a finite union of quasi-Stein open subspaces; 𝒵 ⊆ 𝒳̄ is a closed subset whose complement is a finite union of quasi-Stein open subspaces; T(𝒰̄) ⊆ 𝒰, where 𝒰̄ is the closure of 𝒰; and T^t(𝒵) ⊆ 𝒵̊, the interior of 𝒵. It is a quasi-compact open/closed support condition if moreover 𝒰 is a quasi-compact open subset and 𝒵 is the complement of a quasi-compact open subset.
items.note: Definition 6.1.3 (p. 59) recalls the notion of [BP21] (G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, arXiv:2110.10251). BP21 is not covered by the atlas and should be added as a prerequisite; the atlas cites only its Theorem 4.4.40, in HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T6 and PerfectoidShimuraVarieties S6. No layer mentions quasi-Stein spaces, and none plans cohomology with support in rigid geometry. The notion generalises the neighbourhoods 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε of Pilloni (2020), §14.1, to an abstract condition for any finite flat correspondence.

items.name: The cohomologies with support RΓ_{m,n}
items.statement: Let (𝒰, 𝒵) be an open/closed support condition, and put 𝒰_m = T^m(𝒰) and 𝒵_n = (T^t)^n(𝒵) for m, n ≥ 0. Let ℱ be a coherent sheaf, or more generally a Banach sheaf ([BP21] Definition 2.5.2), defined on a neighbourhood of 𝒰 ∩ 𝒵 in 𝒳̄. Equip ℱ with a cohomological correspondence T : p_2^⋆ℱ → p_1^!ℱ, assumed compact when ℱ is a Banach sheaf; this is automatic for coherent ℱ. Put RΓ_{m,n} := RΓ_{𝒰_m∩𝒵_n}(𝒰_m, ℱ). There are natural maps RΓ_{m,n} → RΓ_{m+1,n} (restriction, as 𝒰_{m+1} ⊆ 𝒰_m) and RΓ_{m,n+1} → RΓ_{m,n} (enlarging the support, as 𝒵_{n+1} ⊆ 𝒵_n). In the quasi-compact case these complexes are represented by complexes of Banach modules; in general they are represented by projective systems of complexes of Banach modules.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.4 (potent compactness of T and independence of the finite slope part)
items.statement: In the setting of §6.1.1, T acts on every RΓ_{m,n}, by composing the cohomological correspondence with restriction and corestriction maps, and this action is potent compact; the paper adds that T^2 is compact. The finite slope parts RΓ_{m,n}^{fs}, for the slope decomposition of [BP21] §5.1.1, are quasi-isomorphic for all m, n ≥ 0 via the natural maps.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.4 (p. 59) is cited from [BP21] Theorem 5.3.7. LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 plans compact operators, Fredholm determinants and slope decompositions for Banach modules. The extraction of Pilloni (2020) routed bounded complexes of projective Banach modules up to homotopy, with their compact endomorphisms, to L4 by a source route. But no layer names finite-slope parts of projective systems of Banach complexes or potent compactness (T^2 compact). This generalises Pilloni (2020), Corollary 13.2.4.2 (restriction is an isomorphism on finite-slope parts), from Klingen-level neighbourhoods for GSp_4 to any open/closed support condition. External input: [BP21] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, arXiv:2110.10251 (2021), Theorem 5.3.7 (with Proposition 5.3.2)

items.name: Lemma 6.1.5 (shrinking to a quasi-compact support condition)
items.statement: Let (𝒰, 𝒵) be an open/closed support condition. Then there is a quasi-compact open/closed support condition (𝒰′, 𝒵′) with T(𝒰) ⊆ 𝒰′ ⊆ 𝒰 and T^t(𝒵) ⊆ 𝒵′ ⊆ 𝒵.
items.note:
Lemma 6.1.5 (p. 59). The proof uses that T(𝒰̄) is closed (finite maps are closed), hence compact in the constructible topology of the spectral space underlying X̄. It then covers T(𝒰̄) by finitely many quasi-compact opens of 𝒰, which are open in the constructible topology. The argument actually gives T(𝒰̄) ⊆ 𝒰′, which is what makes (𝒰′, 𝒵′) a support condition (T(𝒰̄′) ⊆ T(𝒰̄) ⊆ 𝒰′); the statement records only T(𝒰) ⊆ 𝒰′. For 𝒰′ to be a finite union of quasi-Stein opens, the quasi-compact opens should be taken affinoid. The topological inputs exist:
- Mathlib: compactSpace_withConstructibleTopology, IsCompact.isOpen_constructibleTopology_of_isOpen;
- Tau Ceti: IsClosed.isProConstructible, TauCeti.IsProConstructible.isCompact, and TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spectralSpace_spa_of_pairOfDefinition (Spa of a Huber pair is spectral).
The support conditions themselves are unplanned.

items.name: Corollary 6.1.6 (finite slope parts are unchanged by the shrinking)
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 6.1.5, the finite slope parts of RΓ_{𝒰∩𝒵}(𝒰, ℱ) and RΓ_{𝒰′∩𝒵′}(𝒰′, ℱ) are quasi-isomorphic.
items.note: Corollary 6.1.6 (p. 59). The proof compares (𝒰, 𝒵), (𝒰′, 𝒵), (𝒰, 𝒵′) and (𝒰′, 𝒵′) through restriction maps composed with T. These factor through each other, so the restrictions are quasi-isomorphisms on finite-slope parts. Only the first comparison is written; the others are 'left to the reader'. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.7 (the finite slope part depends only on the limit set)
items.statement: Let (𝒰, 𝒵) and (𝒰′, 𝒵′) be two open/closed support conditions, with ℱ and T as in §6.1.1 defined near both 𝒰 ∩ 𝒵 and 𝒰′ ∩ 𝒵′. Assume that ∩_{m,n} T^m(𝒰) ∩ (T^t)^n(𝒵) = ∩_{m,n} T^m(𝒰′) ∩ (T^t)^n(𝒵′). Then RΓ_{𝒰∩𝒵}(𝒰, ℱ)^{fs} and RΓ_{𝒰′∩𝒵′}(𝒰′, ℱ)^{fs} are canonically quasi-isomorphic.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.7, pp. 59–60. The proof reduces to quasi-compact conditions (Lemma 6.1.5) and passes to the union (𝒰 ∪ 𝒰′, 𝒵 ∪ 𝒵′). Compactness in the constructible topology then gives m, n with 𝒰′_m ∩ 𝒵_n ⊆ 𝒰, and a commutative square of restrictions finishes the argument. The constructible-topology inputs are those listed for Lemma 6.1.5. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Degree-defined neighbourhoods 𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝒰_{≤w+ε}, 𝒵_{<w+ε}, 𝒵_{>w−ε} (§6.1.8)
items.note: §6.1.8, p. 60. It uses the Iwahori-level toroidal model of §4.1 and Fargues's degree of finite flat group schemes ([Far10] L. Fargues, J. reine angew. Math. 645 (2010), 1–39; recalled in §4.2.7). No layer defines that degree or the Iwahori-level integral model with its divisors D_{H_{g+i}}. AdicSpacesPartII R2 plans the rational domains used here ('Construct rational subdomains cut out by a section of a line bundle and a valuation bound'). The printed definition of 𝒵_{>w−ε} takes the union over ε′ > ε; by symmetry with 𝒵_{<w+ε} it should be ε′ < ε. This generalises the neighbourhoods 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε of Pilloni (2020), §14.1, to genus g and every w ∈ ^MW.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.9(1)–(2) (one Hecke step improves the degree bounds)
items.statement: (1) For every ε ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q there is ε′ < ε with T(𝒰_{≥w−ε}) ⊆ 𝒰_{≥w−ε′}. (2) For every ε ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q there is ε′ < ε with T^t(𝒰_{≤w+ε}) ⊆ 𝒰_{≤w+ε′}.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.9(1)–(2), p. 60. Proof: by Proposition 4.2.15, deg H_{g+i}(p_1(x)) ≤ deg H_{g+i}(p_2(x)) for every rank-one point x of C_t^tor, with equality only at multiples of n; quasi-compactness then gives ε′. For GSp_4 at Klingen level, Pilloni (2020), §14, has the analogous dynamics of U on the neighbourhoods 𝒳_Kli(p)_ε. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.1.9(3)–(4) (iterated Hecke contraction)
items.statement: (3) For all 0 < ε′ < ε < 1 there is N ≥ 0 with T^N(𝒰_{≥w−ε}) ⊆ 𝒰_{≥w−ε′}. (4) For all 0 < ε′ < ε < 1 there is N ≥ 0 with (T^t)^N(𝒰_{≤w+ε}) ⊆ 𝒰_{≤w+ε′}.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.9(3)–(4), p. 60. The paper gives no proof, only: 'proved as in [Pil11], prop. 2.5. See also [Pil11], thm. 3.1'. [Pil11] is V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), 167–222. The atlas does not cover it; it should be added as a prerequisite. Planned nowhere. External input: [Pil11] V. Pilloni, Prolongement analytique sur les variétés de Siegel, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), 167–222, Prop. 2.5 (see also Thm. 3.1)

items.name: Proposition 6.1.10 (the degree support condition and its limit set)
items.statement: For every ε ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q, the pair (𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝒵_{<w+ε}) is a quasi-compact open/closed support condition for T = C_t^tor. Moreover ∩_{m,n} T^m(𝒰_{≥w−ε}) ∩ (T^t)^n(𝒵_{<w+ε}) is the closure of S^tor_w, the generic fibre of the w-ordinary locus.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.10, p. 60. The proof is one line: 'This follows from proposition 6.1.9.' The limit set is printed as the closure of S^tor_w, the w-ordinary locus of §4. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Bruhat cells, Schubert varieties, Y_w, and pull-back along the Hodge–Tate map
[BP21] Lemma 3.1.2 (the opposite Schubert variety lies in Y_w)
items.statement: [BP21] Lemma 3.1.2: X^w ⊆ Y_w. Proof there: X^w ∩ X_v ≠ ∅ only if v ≥ w, so X^w meets C_v only if v ≥ w. The paper uses it in the form 𝒳_w ⊆ ]X_{w,F_p}[ and 𝒳^w ⊆ ]Y_{w,F_p}[.
items.note: Cited on p. 60 for 𝒳_w ⊆ ]X_{w,F_p}[ and 𝒳^w ⊆ ]Y_{w,F_p}[. It is a statement about the flag variety of a split reductive group over Z_p, resting on the Bruhat decomposition and the closure order on cells. [BP21] is not covered by the atlas. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] G. Boxer, V. Pilloni, Higher Coleman theory, arXiv:2110.10251 (2021), Lemma 3.1.2

items.name: [BP21] Lemma 3.4.1 and its proof (dynamics of Schubert tubes under T)
items.statement: [BP21] Lemma 3.4.1: (1) if t ∈ T^+, then ]X_{w,k}[·t ⊆ ]X_{w,k}[ for all w ∈ ^MW; (2) if t ∈ T^−, then ]Y_{w,k}[·t ⊆ ]Y_{w,k}[ for all w ∈ ^MW. The paper uses the lemma ‘and its proof’ for a sharper claim. Let B_n (resp. B_n^{op}) be the subgroup of elements of B (resp. B^{op}) congruent to 1 mod p^n, and put 𝒳_{w,n} = 𝒳_wB_n^{op} and 𝒳^w_n = 𝒳^wB_n (tubular neighbourhoods of width p^n). Then for t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p): ]X_{w,F_p}[·t^n ⊆ 𝒳_{w,n} and ]Y_{w,F_p}[·t^{−n} ⊆ 𝒳^w_n.
items.note: Cited on p. 60 ('see [BP21], lem. 3.4.1 and its proof') for ]X_{w,F_p}[·t^n ⊆ 𝒳_{w,n} and ]Y_{w,F_p}[·t^{−n} ⊆ 𝒳^w_n (printed 𝒳^{w,n}). This quantitative form is taken from the proof, not the statement, of [BP21] Lemma 3.4.1 and needs its own statement. From it the paper deduces two inclusions (p. 60): the closure of ]X_{w,F_p}[K_{p,n}tK_{p,n} lies in ]X_{w,F_p}[, and the closure of ]Y_{w,F_p}[, translated by K_{p,n}t^{−1}K_{p,n}, lies in its interior, which is ]Y_{w,F_p}[. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] Lemma 3.4.1 (and its proof)

items.name: [BP21] Lemma 3.5.10(5) (iterated Hecke images of Schubert tubes)
items.note: Cited on p. 61 as '[BP21], lem. 3.5.10.5' to bound T^m(π^{−1}]X_{w,F_p}[) ∩ (T^t)^n(π^{−1} of the closure of ]Y_{w,F_p}[). The sets ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n} of [BP21] §3.3.6 are also unplanned. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] Lemma 3.5.10(5) and §3.3.6

items.name: [BP21] Corollary 3.3.14 (]C_w[_{m,n} as orbits of congruence subgroups)
items.statement: [BP21] Corollary 3.3.14: for all m, n ∈ Q_{≥0}, ]C_{w,k}[_{m,n} = P∖PwG_{m,n} for congruence subgroups G_{m,n} of G, and similarly for the partial closures. The paper uses it as (]C_{w,F_p}[_{m,0̄}B_{K_{p,n}}) = ]C_{w,F_p}[_{m,0̄} and (]C_{w,F_p}[_{0,n̄}U^{op}_{K_{p,n}}) = ]C_{w,F_p}[_{0,n̄}.
items.note: Cited on p. 61. Combined with the Iwahori decomposition K_{p,n} = B_{K_{p,n}} × U^{op}_{K_{p,n}}, it gives ]C_{w,F_p}[_{m,0̄}K_{p,n} ∩ ]C_{w,F_p}[_{0,n̄}K_{p,n} = ]C_{w,F_p}[_{m,n̄}K_{p,n}. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] Corollary 3.3.14

items.name: Proposition 6.1.11 (the Hodge–Tate support condition and its limit set)
items.statement: The pair (π^{−1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(]X_{w,F_p}[), π^{−1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(closure of ]Y_{w,F_p}[)) is an open/closed support condition for T = C_t^tor, with t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p). Moreover ∩_{m,n} T^m(π^{−1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}]X_{w,F_p}[) ∩ (T^t)^n(π^{−1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(closure of ]Y_{w,F_p}[)) is the closure of S^tor_w.
items.note: Proposition 6.1.11, pp. 60–61. The proof assembles [BP21] Lemmas 3.1.2, 3.4.1 and 3.5.10(5) and Corollary 3.3.14. As written it shows only that T^m(π^{−1}]X_{w,F_p}[) ∩ (T^t)^n(π^{−1} of the closure of ]Y_{w,F_p}[) is contained in ]C_{w,F_p}[_{m,n̄}K_{p,n}. Two steps are not written: identifying ∩_{m,n} ]C_{w,F_p}[_{m,n̄}K_{p,n}, pulled back to S^tor, with the closure of S^tor_w, and the reverse inclusion. This is the support condition of [BP21] §5.4 for GSp_{2g}. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Comparison of degree-defined and Hodge–Tate-defined finite slope cohomology (implicit)
items.statement: Let w ∈ ^MW, t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) and ε ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q. Let ℱ be a sheaf with a cohomological correspondence for C_t^tor as in §6.1.1, defined near both supports below. Then the finite slope parts of RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ℱ) and of RΓ_{𝒰_{HT}∩𝒵_{HT}}(𝒰_{HT}, ℱ) are canonically quasi-isomorphic. Here 𝒰_{HT} = π^{−1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(]X_{w,F_p}[) and 𝒵_{HT} = π^{−1}_{HT,K_{p,n}}(closure of ]Y_{w,F_p}[).
items.note: Not stated in the paper. It is what Propositions 6.1.7, 6.1.10 and 6.1.11 give together: both support conditions have limit set the closure of S^tor_w (pp. 59–61). It is the bridge by which the degree-defined supports of §6.2 compute the finite-slope cohomology of [BP21], used implicitly in Corollaries 6.2.10 and 6.2.16. It needs one sheaf with a compact cohomological correspondence defined near both supports. Planned nowhere.

items.name: The parameters ε, ε′ of §6.2
items.statement: Fix w ∈ ^MW and t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), and let T denote C_t^tor. Fix ε ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q and ε′ ∈ ]0, ε[ ∩ Q such that T(𝒰_{≥w−ε}) ⊆ 𝒰_{≥w−ε′} and T^t(𝒰_{≤w+ε}) ⊆ 𝒰_{≤w+ε′}.
items.note: §6.2.1, p. 61. Such ε′ exists by Proposition 6.1.9(1)–(2): take the larger of the two values it provides, or any positive value below ε if both are ≤ 0. This works because 𝒰_{≥w−ε′} and 𝒰_{≤w+ε′} grow with ε′. It is notation specific to the paper.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.2 (blow-up separating the rational degree divisors)
items.statement:
There is a blow-up π : S̃^tor → S^tor, where S^tor is the model of level K^pK_{p,n} of Proposition 4.1.13, with the following properties.
(1) For 0 ≤ i ≤ g there are effective divisors Z_{i,>w_i} and Z_{i,<w_i} on S̃^tor with disjoint supports and Z_{i,>w_i} − Z_{i,<w_i} = Z_i − V(p^{nw_i}).
(2) For 0 ≤ i ≤ g and η ∈ {ε, −ε, ε′, −ε′} there are effective divisors Z_{i,>w_i+η} and Z_{i,<w_i+η} on S̃^tor with disjoint supports and Z_{i,>w_i+η} − Z_{i,<w_i+η} = Z_i − V(p^{n(w_i+η)}).
(3) π induces an isomorphism π^{−1}(S^tor_{w,F_p}) → S^tor_{w,F_p}.
The index is printed j in place of i. From here on, S^tor denotes S̃^tor.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.2, p. 61; the proof is 'identical to the proof of proposition 4.1.13'. AdicSpacesPartII R2 plans admissible blow-ups ('Construct admissible formal schemes, formal completion, admissible blow-ups'). V(p^{n(w_i+η)}) involves a fractional power of p when nη ∉ Z. R2 requires such bounds to be defined 'by valuation ideals or by an explicitly chosen extension containing the relevant p-power root', and the construction must say which. The index is printed j for i. The specific blow-up is planned nowhere.

items.name: The divisors D_±, D_{±,ε}, D_{±,ε′}
items.statement: On S^tor = S̃^tor put D_+ = Σ_i Z_{i,<w_i}, D_− = Σ_i Z_{i,>w_i}, D_{+,ε} = Σ_i Z_{i,<w_i−ε}, D_{−,ε} = Σ_i Z_{i,>w_i+ε}, D_{+,ε′} = Σ_i Z_{i,<w_i−ε′} and D_{−,ε′} = Σ_i Z_{i,>w_i+ε′}. The index is printed j in place of i.
items.note: §6.2.1, p. 61: sums over 0 ≤ i ≤ g of the divisors of Proposition 6.2.2 on the blown-up model (index printed j). Notation specific to the paper.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.3(1)–(3) (inequalities between the divisors D)
items.statement: (1) D_+ ≥ D_{+,ε′} ≥ D_{+,ε} and D_− ≥ D_{−,ε′} ≥ D_{−,ε}. (2) p_1^⋆D_+ ≥ p_2^⋆D_+ and p_1^⋆D_{+,ε} ≥ p_2^⋆D_{+,ε′}. (3) p_2^⋆D_− ≥ p_1^⋆D_− and p_2^⋆D_{−,ε} ≥ p_1^⋆D_{−,ε′}. Here p_1, p_2 : C_t^tor → S^tor is the Hecke correspondence over the blown-up model.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.3(1)–(3), p. 61. Part (1) is 'obvious'; (2) and (3) follow from Proposition 6.1.9 and Lemma 4.2.11. It is the integral form of the one-step degree dynamics. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.3(4) (strict contraction off D_{+,ε} ∪ D_{−,ε})
items.statement: Over C_t^tor ∖ (p_1^⋆D_{+,ε} ∪ p_2^⋆D_{−,ε}) there is s ∈ ]0,1[ ∩ Q with s·p_1^⋆D_+ ≥ p_2^⋆D_+ and s·p_2^⋆D_− ≥ p_1^⋆D_−.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.3(4), p. 61; the proof says it 'follows as in lemma 4.4.2' (strict dynamic compactifications, §4.4). Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.5 (integral fundamental class near the w-ordinary locus)
items.statement: Over C_t^tor ∖ (p_1^⋆D_+ ∪ p_2^⋆D_−), the trace of p_1 gives a map p_2^⋆O_{S^tor} → ⟨w^{−1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ, t⟩·p_1^!O_{S^tor}. On this open, and on S^tor ∖ (D_+ ∪ D_−), the spaces are smooth, so p_1^!O_{S^tor} is invertible. The statement is that the fundamental class p_2^⋆O → p_1^!O is divisible by the scalar ⟨w^{−1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ, t⟩, whose valuation is ⟨v(t), w^{−1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ⟩. Here w^{−1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ = Σ_{α∈(w^{−1}Φ^{+,M})∩Φ^+} α, where, in the notation of §3.1, Φ^{+,M} is the set of positive roots in Lie(U_P), the unipotent radical of the Siegel parabolic P; the positive roots of the Levi M are denoted Φ^+_M. By Proposition 6.2.3(2)–(3), supp p_2^⋆D_+ ⊆ supp p_1^⋆D_+ and supp p_1^⋆D_− ⊆ supp p_2^⋆D_−. Hence C_t^tor ∖ (p_1^⋆D_+ ∪ p_2^⋆D_−) = p_1^{−1}(X) ∩ p_2^{−1}(X) with X = S^tor ∖ (D_+ ∪ D_−).
items.locator: §6.2.4, Proposition 6.2.5 and proof, p. 61; Lemma 4.3.8, p. 48; notation Φ^{+,M}: §3.1, p. 34
items.note: Proposition 6.2.5, p. 61. The proof observes that S^tor ∖ (D_+ ∪ D_−) and C_t^tor ∖ (p_1^⋆D_+ ∪ p_2^⋆D_−) are smooth, so p_1^!O is invertible there; the divisibility is Lemma 4.3.8. The extraction of Pilloni (2020) routes the fundamental class of a finite flat map between smooth schemes, given by the trace, to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension. AdicSpacesPartII R3 plans only analytic traces. The item's identity w^{−1}w_{0,M}ρ + ρ = Σ_{α ∈ (w^{−1}Φ^{+,M}) ∩ Φ^+} α is not printed on p. 61. It was checked by direct computation for w ∈ ^MW, with Φ^{+,M} the positive roots outside M: the computation uses that w^{−1} maps the positive roots of M to positive roots. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.6 (the normalized cohomological correspondence t on ω^κ(χ))
items.statement: Let κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} and let χ : T(Z_p) → Z_p(ζ_{p^n})^× be a character of finite order, factoring through T(Z/p^nZ) so that the sheaf ω^κ(χ) = ω^κ ⊗ O(χ) of §4.3.5 is defined. Over C_t^tor ∖ (p_1^⋆D_+ ∪ p_2^⋆D_−), after base change to Z_p(ζ_{p^n}), there is a cohomological correspondence t : p_2^⋆ω^κ(χ) → p_1^!ω^κ(χ) equal to ⟨−w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) − ρ, t⟩·t^{naive}. Here t^{naive} is the rational map obtained by tensoring the isomorphism p_2^⋆ω^κ(χ)[1/p] → p_1^⋆ω^κ(χ)[1/p] with the fundamental class of Proposition 6.2.5.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.6, p. 61; the proof says it 'follows as in proposition 4.3.11'. It generalises the normalised Klingen operator U of Pilloni (2020) (§§7, 14) to every t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), every w and GSp_{2g}. The sheaves ω^κ(χ) are those of §4.3.5. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.7 (integral model ω̃^κ(χ) and factorization of t̃)
items.statement: There is an integral model ω̃^κ(χ) = ω^κ(χ)(m(D_+ − D_−)), for some m ≥ 0, such that t extends to a cohomological correspondence t̃ : p_2^⋆ω̃^κ(χ) → p_1^!ω̃^κ(χ) over C_t^tor ∖ (p_1^⋆D_{+,ε} ∪ p_2^⋆D_{−,ε}). Moreover t̃ factors as p_2^⋆ω̃^κ(χ) → p_2^⋆ω̃^κ(χ)(D_+) → p_1^!ω̃^κ(χ)(−D_−) → p_1^!ω̃^κ(χ).
items.note: Proposition 6.2.7, p. 61; the proof says it is 'analogous to proposition 4.3.13 and lemma 4.3.14'. The factorisation through p_2^⋆ω̃(D_+) and p_1^!ω̃(−D_−) is what makes t̃ act on cohomology with partial supports (Proposition 2.10.4). Planned nowhere.

items.name: Integral overconvergent cohomology RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ))^{int} (§6.2.8)
items.statement:
Let Z_{<w+ε} = ∩_i Z_{i,<w_i+ε}, an intersection of supports. View î : Ẑ_{<w+ε} ↪ S^tor as a closed subset of the locale of D(O_{S^tor,■}), i.e. the formal completion along Z_{<w+ε} (§2.9.1). Let U_{≥w−ε} = S^tor ∖ D_{+,ε} ↪ S^tor and î′ : Ẑ_{<w+ε} ∩ U_{≥w−ε} ↪ U_{≥w−ε}. For s ≥ 1 put RΓ_{Ẑ_{<w+ε}∩U_{≥w−ε},Z/p^sZ}(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) = RΓ(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ}, î′_⋆(î′)^!ω̃^κ(χ)). This complex sits in an exact triangle
RΓ_{Ẑ_{<w+ε}∩U_{≥w−ε},Z/p^sZ}(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) → RΓ(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) → RΓ(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ} ∖ Z_{<w+ε}, ω̃^κ(χ)) →^{+1}.
Define RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ))^{int} := lim_s RΓ_{Ẑ_{<w+ε}∩U_{≥w−ε},Z/p^sZ}(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)). This is printed with U_{≥w+ε} in both places.
items.note: §6.2.8, p. 62. It uses §2.9.1: for an ideal I of R, the closed subset Ẑ of the locale of D(R_■), with idempotent algebra R̂_I = lim R/I^n ([CSa] D. Clausen, P. Scholze, Condensed mathematics and complex geometry, Lecture V). The draft roadmap SolidAnalyticRings treats idempotent algebras and smashing spectra (its layer SA.2, 'Idempotent algebras and smashing spectra (RC §5.1)'), but it is not in the atlas. Nothing in the atlas plans the local cohomology î_⋆î^! of such closed subsets of formal schemes. As printed, the definition has U_{≥w+ε} in place of U_{≥w−ε} in both places. The exact triangle is the localisation sequence of §2.9. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.9(1)–(2) (the ordinary part of integral overconvergent cohomology is higher Hida theory)
items.statement:
Work in the setting of §6.2: w ∈ ^MW, t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), ε, ε′ as in §6.2.1, κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+}, χ and ω̃^κ(χ) as in Propositions 6.2.6–6.2.7.
(1) RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ))^{int} carries an action of t.
(2) Its ordinary part identifies with the higher Hida complex RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ), which equals RΓ_w(K^pK_{w,p,P}, κ, χ) of §4.4.
More precisely, fix s ≥ 1 and consider the change-of-support maps
RΓ_{D_{+,ε},D_{−,ε′}}(S^tor_{Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) → RΓ_{Ẑ_{<w+ε}∩U_{≥w−ε},Z/p^sZ}(U_{≥w−ε,Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) → RΓ_{D_{+,ε′},D_{−,ε}}(S^tor_{Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)).
Composed with the map t̃ : RΓ_{D_{+,ε′},D_{−,ε}}(S^tor_{Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) → RΓ_{D_{+,ε},D_{−,ε′}}(S^tor_{Z/p^sZ}, ω̃^κ(χ)) of Proposition 2.10.4, they give compatible endomorphisms of the three complexes. All three become quasi-isomorphic on ordinary parts, and the ordinary parts identify with RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ) ⊗_{Z_p} Z/p^sZ.
items.note: Theorem 6.2.9(1)–(2), p. 62. The proof combines Lemma 2.10.1 (change of support), Proposition 2.10.4 (the map t̃ between cohomologies with partial supports) and Theorem 2.11.4 (ordinary parts compute RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ) ⊗ Z/p^s). The passage from the level-s statements to the inverse limit over s is not written. This is the integral form of Theorem 1.4.9 (p. 6): 'The slope 0 part of higher Coleman theory canonically identifies with the rational part of higher Hida theory'. It generalises the comparison of the overconvergent complex M† with M ⊗ Q_p in Pilloni (2020) (§1, pp. 4–5; §14.8) from GSp_4 at Klingen level to GSp_{2g}, Iwahori level and every w. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.9(3) (rational comparison and lattices in slope ≤ h overconvergent cohomology)
items.statement: RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ))^{int} ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p = RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ)), the rigid-analytic cohomology with support of §6.1. For every h ∈ Q, the image of RΓ^{int} in the slope ≤ h part RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ))^{≤h}, taken for the action of t, is a Z_p-lattice; the slope ≤ h part is a finite-dimensional Q_p-vector space.
items.note: Theorem 6.2.9(3), p. 62. Via the two localisation triangles, the comparison reduces to two identities: lim_s RΓ(U_{≥w−ε, Z/p^s}, ω̃^κ(χ)) ⊗ Q_p = RΓ(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, ω^κ(χ)), and the same on the complement of 𝒵_{<w+ε}. Both are comparisons of formal and rigid coherent cohomology on non-proper quasi-compact opens, stated without proof. AdicSpacesPartII F0 plans formal functions and formal GAGA only 'in the proper finite-presentation setting'. The lattice statement is deduced from [BP21] Lemma 5.9.10. It generalises Pilloni (2020), Lemma 14.7.1, where small-slope classes inject into an integral limit. Planned nowhere.

items.name: [BP21] Lemma 5.9.10 (integral cohomology with support gives open bounded submodules)
items.statement: [BP21] Lemma 5.9.10(1): let w ∈ ^MW and κ ∈ X^⋆(T^c)^{M_µ,+}. Let (U, Z) be a (+, w, K_{p,m′,b})-allowed support condition ([BP21] Definition 5.4.10). This is defined relative to a fixed t ∈ T^{++} with min(t) ≥ 1 and C = max(t), and means the following. U is an open subset of S^tor_{K^pK_{p,m′,b},Σ} that is a finite union of quasi-Stein opens. Z is a closed subset whose complement is a finite union of quasi-Stein opens. Both Z ∩ U and U are squeezed between Hodge–Tate preimages of the neighbourhoods ]C_{w,k}[_{a,b}K_{p,m′,b} of the tube of the Bruhat cell, as in condition (3) of that definition. Assume moreover that U is a quasi-compact open and that Z has quasi-compact complement. Then the image of H^i_{U∩Z}(U, V_κ^+) in the finite slope overconvergent cohomology H^i_w(K^p, κ)^{+,fs} is an open and bounded submodule; here V_κ^+ is the integral structure of the automorphic sheaf V_κ. Part (2) is the analogue for '−'. On p. 62 the paper invokes this lemma as the model for constructing lattices, for the pair (𝒰_{≥w−ϵ}, 𝒵_{<w+ϵ}).
items.locator: §6.2.8, proof of Theorem 6.2.9, p. 62; [BP21] Lemma 5.9.10 and Definition 5.4.10
items.note: Invoked on p. 62 ('which explains how to construct lattices'). Also unplanned: the allowed support conditions of [BP21] Definition 5.4.10 and the integral structure V_κ^+. [BP21] is not covered by the atlas. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] Lemma 5.9.10

items.name: Corollary 6.2.10 ([BP21] Conjecture 5.9.2 holds for Siegel varieties)
items.statement:
[BP21] Conjecture 5.9.2 holds for G = GSp_{2g}. Fix w ∈ ^MW, κ ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M_µ,+} and a character χ of T(Z_p) of finite order.
(1) Every character λ of T^+ occurring in the finite slope overconvergent cohomology RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ)^{+,fs} or RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ, cusp)^{+,fs} of [BP21] §5.4 satisfies v(λ) ≥ w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) + ρ; that is, v(λ(t)) ≥ ⟨v(t), w^{−1}w_{0,M}(κ + ρ) + ρ⟩ for all t ∈ T^+.
(2) Every character λ of T^− occurring in the ‘−’ versions satisfies v(λ) ≤ w^{−1}(κ + ρ) − ρ.
In [BP21] the notation RΓ_w(K^p, κ, χ)^{±,fs} denotes overconvergent cohomology, not the higher Hida complexes of this paper.
items.locator: §6.2.8, Corollary 6.2.10 and proof, p. 62; Theorem 1.4.10, p. 6
items.note: Corollary 6.2.10, p. 62; Theorem 1.4.10, p. 6. The proof has three steps: the slope bound is equivalent to the normalised action of t stabilising a lattice; it suffices to treat t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p), which generate T(Q_p); and Theorem 6.2.9(3) supplies the lattice. It improves Pilloni (2020), Proposition 13.3.1.1 (slopes ≥ −3 in all degrees and ≥ 0 in degree 0, GSp_4), to the optimal bound in all degrees and genera. Planned nowhere: the OverconvergentAutomorphicForms document excludes higher Coleman cohomology. Theorem 1.4.10 (p. 6) states this corollary together with Corollary 6.2.16 (p. 64). That corollary gives the bounds v(λ) ≥ 0 on T^+ and v(λ) ≤ 0 on T^− of [BP21] Conjecture 6.8.1 for finite slope locally analytic overconvergent cohomology, and it is a separate item. The printed proof covers less than the statement [sourceIssues E126]. The fact that T^{++}(Q_p) generates T(Q_p) is not enough to pass from T^{++}(Q_p) to T^+(Q_p). That step needs a cone argument: the slope inequality is linear in v(t), and the positive multiples of v(T^{++}) are dense in the closed dominant cone. Theorem 6.2.9 treats only the non-cuspidal '+' theory. The cuspidal case of (1) needs the cuspidal analogue of Theorem 6.2.9, which is proved in the same way. (2) follows from (1) by the Serre duality of [BP21] Theorems 5.7.1–5.7.2, which exchanges the two bounds ([BP21] Remark 5.9.5).

items.name: Small slope versions of the [BP21] classicality and vanishing theorems (Siegel case)
items.statement:
For G = GSp_{2g}, the strongly small slope conditions (sss^M(κ), sss_b(ν); [BP21] Definition 5.11.14) may be replaced by the small slope conditions (ss^M(κ), ss_b(ν); [BP21] Definition 5.11.2) in the following theorems.
- [BP21] Theorem 5.12.3 (classicality): for κ + ρ regular with C(κ)^± = {w^±}, RΓ_{w^±}(K^p, κ, χ)^{±,ss^M(κ)} ≃ RΓ(K^p, κ, χ)^{±,ss^M(κ)}, and the same for cuspidal cohomology.
- [BP21] Theorem 5.12.5 (vanishing for rational coherent cohomology): RΓ(K^p, κ, χ, cusp)^{±,ss^M(κ)} lies in degrees [0, ℓ_max(κ)], RΓ(K^p, κ, χ)^{±,ss^M(κ)} lies in [ℓ_min(κ), d], and interior cohomology lies in [ℓ_min(κ), ℓ_max(κ)].
- [BP21] Theorem 5.12.11 (vanishing for Betti cohomology): for ν ∈ X^⋆(T)^+, H^i(S_K(C), W_ν^∨)^{±,ss_b(ν)} lies in degrees [d, 2d], H^i_c in [0, d], and interior cohomology in degree d.
items.note: Stated without proof on p. 62: 'we can replace the “strongly small slope” conditions with the weaker “small slope” conditions'. According to [BP21] Remarks 5.12.6 and 5.12.12, the replacement follows from [BP21] Conjecture 5.9.2. The introduction (p. 6) states this paragraph together with the one after Corollary 6.2.16 (p. 64), citing 'the classicality theorems 5.12.3 and 6.8.4 and the vanishing theorem 5.12.20 of [BP21]'. The two lists agree. [BP21] Theorem 5.12.20 is the form of Theorems 5.12.5 and 5.12.11 for cohomology at tame level K^p, and [BP21] deduces it immediately from them. [BP21] Corollary 6.8.4 belongs to the paragraph on p. 64. It generalises Pilloni (2020), Corollary 13.3.3.1 (small-slope classicality for GSp_4). Planned nowhere. The paragraph on p. 64 makes the same replacement in [BP21] Corollary 6.8.4 and Theorem 6.9.3(2), and that part is a separate item. The introduction (p. 6) adds a remark: when the weight is not sufficiently regular, even ordinary classes may fail to be of strongly small slope, so the versions of these results under the strongly small slope condition may be vacuous. The paragraph on p. 62 ends by deducing Theorem 1.5.1 (p. 6). For N divisible by p and Γ = {γ ∈ Sp_{2g}(Z) : γ ≡ 1 mod N}, that theorem says H^i(Γ, Q_p)^{ord} = 0 for 0 ≤ i < g(g+1)/2. External input: [BP21] Theorems 5.12.3, 5.12.5, 5.12.11, with Remarks 5.12.6 and 5.12.12 (the strongly small slope conditions can be weakened to small slope conditions if Conjecture 5.9.2 holds)

items.name: Analytic weight space W and the character ν_A
items.statement: Λ = Z_p[[T(Z_p)]] and W = Spa(Λ, Λ) ×_{Spa(Z_p,Z_p)} Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is the analytic weight space over Spa(Q_p, Z_p). Let Spa(A[1/p], A) ⊆ W be a quasi-compact open subset, and let ν_A : T(Z_p) → A^× be the restriction of the universal character.
items.note: §6.2.11, p. 63, with G = T(Z_p) ≅ (Z_p^×)^{g+1}. The extraction of Pilloni (2020) marked the one-variable case (Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]]) as planned at the same layers. Neither library has completed group rings or rigid character spaces.

items.name: The groups 𝒯_n, 𝔗_n, ℐ𝒲_n, 𝔍𝔚_n, 𝔅𝔍𝔚_n and the weight κ_A
items.statement: For n ≥ 1, 𝒯_n → Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is the affinoid group with 𝒯_n(C, C^+) = {x ∈ T(C^+) : x mod p^n ∈ T(Z/p^nZ) ⊆ T(C^+/p^nC^+)}; this is printed ‘T(Z/pnZ)’. 𝔗_n = Spf O^+_{𝒯_n} is a formal group scheme, and for n large enough ν_A extends to a character 𝔗_n → 𝔊_m × Spf A. Put κ_A = −w_{0,M}w(ν_A + ρ) − ρ, and K_{p,P} = wK_{p,n}w^{−1} ∩ P(Q_p) with Levi quotient M_{K_{p,P}}. ℐ𝒲_n → Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is the affinoid group with ℐ𝒲_n(C, C^+) = {x ∈ M(C^+) : x mod p^n lies in M_{K_{p,P}} mod p^n}. 𝔍𝔚_n = Spf O^+_{ℐ𝒲_n}, and 𝔅𝔍𝔚_n is its ‘Borel’ subgroup, with torus 𝔗_n.

items.name: The big sheaves 𝔉^{ν_A} (topological induction) and 𝔉^{ν_A,n} (locally analytic induction)
items.statement:
Start from the M_{K_{p,P}}-torsor π : 𝔍𝔊_{U_{K_{p,P}}} → 𝔍𝔊_{K_{p,P}} = 𝔖^tor_w, the Igusa formal scheme of §5.3.2 and Lemma 4.1.7. Push it out along M_{K_{p,P}} → 𝔍𝔚_n to an 𝔍𝔚_n-torsor π′ : 𝔍𝔊_{U_{K_{p,P}}} ×^{M_{K_{p,P}}} 𝔍𝔚_n → 𝔍𝔊_{K_{p,P}}; the subscripts are printed U_{K_p}, M_{K_{p,n}} and K_{p,n}. Define:
- 𝔉^{ν_A} = (π_⋆O_{𝔍𝔊_{U_{K_{p,P}}}} ⊗̂ A)^{B=−w_{0,M}κ_A} (the topological induction; B is printed B_{K_{p,n}});
- 𝔉^{ν_A,n} = (π′_⋆O ⊗̂ A)^{𝔅𝔍𝔚_n=−w_{0,M}κ_A} (the locally analytic induction).
In both, one takes the part on which the Borel subgroup acts through the character −w_{0,M}κ_A. There is a canonical restriction map 𝔉^{ν_A,n} → 𝔉^{ν_A}. ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} and ℱ_r^{ν_A} denote the reductions modulo p^r.
items.note: §6.2.11, p. 63. The sheaves are built from the M_{K_{p,P}}-torsor of Igusa formal schemes over 𝔖^tor_w (§5.3.2, Lemma 4.1.7). They generalise the Λ-adic Igusa sheaves (§9) and the formal Banach sheaves 𝔉^{κ_A,w} (§12.6) of Pilloni (2020) to GSp_{2g}, every w and the whole weight space. The extraction of Pilloni (2020) routes formal Banach sheaves to AdicSpacesPartII by a source route. Induction from a Borel through a character of a formal group is planned nowhere; the Hilbert coefficient sheaves of OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O1–O3 are built from cocycles, not from Igusa torsors. The reductions are printed ℱ_r^{κ_A,n} and ℱ_r^{ν_A}; read ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} for the first.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.12 (Hecke correspondences on the big sheaves)
items.statement: For every r ≥ 0 there are cohomological correspondences t : p_2^⋆ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} → p_1^!ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} and t : p_2^⋆ℱ_r^{ν_A} → p_1^!ℱ_r^{ν_A}, defined over the Hecke correspondence of t on the w-ordinary locus and compatible with the restriction map ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} → ℱ_r^{ν_A}. They are obtained from compatible maps p_2^⋆ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} → p_1^⋆ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} and p_2^⋆ℱ_r^{ν_A} → p_1^⋆ℱ_r^{ν_A} by tensoring with the normalized fundamental class of Proposition 6.2.5.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.12, p. 63. The maps p_2^⋆ℱ → p_1^⋆ℱ are tensored with the normalised fundamental class of Proposition 6.2.5, citing [BP21] §6.3.10. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.13 (locally analytic and topological induction have the same ordinary cohomology)
items.statement: For r ≥ 1, the map RΓ_{D_+,D_−}(S^tor_{w,Z/p^rZ}, ℱ_r^{ν_A,n}) → RΓ_{D_+,D_−}(S^tor_{w,Z/p^rZ}, ℱ_r^{ν_A}) induces a quasi-isomorphism on ordinary parts. Moreover RΓ_{D_+,D_−}(S^tor_{w,Z/p^rZ}, ℱ_r^{ν_A})^{ord} = M_w^• ⊗_Λ A/p^r; this is printed A/p^n.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.13, p. 63. The first point is proved by showing that the Hecke operator is nilpotent on the kernel of ℱ_r^{ν_A,n} → ℱ_r^{ν_A}. The paper compares this with [Pil20] §10.7, i.e. Pilloni (2020), Lemma 10.7.1: U is divisible by p on the kernel of the highest-weight projection. The second point 'follows from the definition' via Remark 5.4.3 (p. 57). The statement prints A/p^n; the proof has A/p^r. Planned nowhere.

items.name: [BP21] Lemma 6.3.10 (Hecke maps on the n-analytic induction sheaves)
items.statement:
[BP21] Lemma 6.3.10. For t ∈ T^+, the map of torsors [t̃^{−1}] : p_1^⋆M_HT^{an}/U^{an} → p_2^⋆M_HT^{an}/U^{an} over the Hecke correspondence depends on t, not only on its class modulo T(Z_p).
(1) It restricts to p_1^⋆M_{HT,n,K_p}/U_n → p_2^⋆M_{HT,n,K_p}/U_n.
(2) For t ∈ T^{++} and n ≥ 1 it factors through p_1^⋆M_{HT,n−1,K_p}/U_{n−1}.
(3) For an n-analytic weight ν_A it induces [t̃^{−1}] : p_2^⋆V^{n−an}_{ν_A} → p_1^⋆V^{n−an}_{ν_A}, locally modelled on wtw^{−1} acting on V^{n−an}_{κ_A}; this map is compact ([BP21] Definition 2.5.3) when t ∈ T^{++}.
items.locator: §6.2.11, proof of Proposition 6.2.14, p. 64 (also the proof of Proposition 6.2.12, p. 63)
items.note: Cited on p. 64, and through [BP21] §6.3.10 on p. 63, for maps p_2^⋆𝔉̃^{ν_A,n}[1/p] → p_1^⋆𝔉̃^{ν_A,n}[1/p]. Their integrality is asserted as 'it follows from the local description given there that they extend'. Compact maps of Banach sheaves in the sense of [BP21] Definition 2.5.3 are unplanned; LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4 plans compact operators on Banach modules only. [BP21] is not covered by the atlas. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] Lemma 6.3.10

items.name: [BP21] proof of Lemma 6.6.2 (formal models of Hodge–Tate neighbourhoods and of the analytic induction sheaf)
items.statement: In the proof of [BP21] Lemma 6.6.2 (Hodge type Shimura data), take an affinoid U in the flag variety contained in ]C_{w,k}[_{n,n}K_p, and a small enough level K′_p. Then π_HT^{−1}(U) admits normal formal models, obtained from normalizations of blow-ups ([BP21] Theorem 4.4.36). Over these, the torsor M_{HT,n} becomes trivial on the generic fibre of a Zariski cover ([BP21] Proposition 4.6.15). Gluing with the resulting cocycle gives a flat formal Banach sheaf model V^{n−an,+}_{ν_A} of the n-analytic induction sheaf.
items.note: Cited on p. 64: the blow-up Ũ_{[w−ε,w+ε]} and the sheaf 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n} 'are constructed as in the proof of lem. 6.6.2 of [BP21]', to obtain an integral model of the Hodge–Tate period map. AdicSpacesPartII R2 plans admissible formal models and blow-ups. Unplanned: an integral model of the finite-level Hodge–Tate map over the boundary (the extraction of Pilloni (2020) routes its genus-two, full-level version to HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0/T5), and the gluing of a flat formal Banach sheaf from a cocycle. External input: [BP21] proof of Lemma 6.6.2 (with Theorem 4.4.36 and Proposition 4.6.15)

items.name: Proposition 6.2.14 (extension of 𝔉^{ν_A,n} to a strict neighbourhood, with factorized Hecke correspondence)
items.statement: For ε sufficiently small, the sheaf 𝔉^{ν_A,n} extends to a sheaf 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n} over 𝔘̃_{[w−ε,w+ε]}. Here 𝔘̃_{[w−ε,w+ε]} → 𝔘_{[w−ε,w+ε]} is a further blow-up away from 𝔖^tor_w, and 𝔘_{[w−ε,w+ε]} is not defined in the paper, presumably the formal open S^tor ∖ (D_{+,ε} ∪ D_{−,ε}). Moreover, after replacing 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n} by 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n}(m′(D_+ − D_−)) for m′ large, as in the proof, for all r > 0 there are cohomological correspondences p_2^⋆ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n} → p_1^!ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n}. They factor as p_2^⋆ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n} → p_2^⋆ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n}(D_+) → p_1^!ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n}(−D_−) → p_1^!ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n}.
items.note: Proposition 6.2.14, pp. 63–64. The proof tensors with the fundamental class to get p_2^⋆𝔉̃_r(−mD_−) → p_1^!𝔉̃_r(mD_+), with m independent of r. It then twists by m′(D_+ − D_−) and uses the dynamics of Proposition 6.2.3. The paper never defines 𝔘_{[w−ε,w+ε]}; by Proposition 6.2.3(4) it is presumably the formal open S^tor ∖ (D_{+,ε} ∪ D_{−,ε}). Planned nowhere.

items.name: Integral locally analytic overconvergent cohomology, in families and in a fixed weight
items.statement: Define RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ϵ}∩𝒰_{≥w−ϵ}}(𝒰_{≥w−ϵ}, 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n})^{int} = lim_r RΓ_{Ẑ_{<w+ϵ}∩U_{≥w−ϵ},Z/p^rZ}(U_{≥w−ϵ,Z/p^rZ}, ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n}), where ℱ̃_r^{ν_A,n} is the reduction of 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n} mod p^r. Let ℂ be a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p (the notation of §3.3). Let ν : T(Z_p) → O_ℂ^× be a continuous character inducing ν : A → O_ℂ, i.e. a ℂ-point of Spa(A[1/p], A). Put 𝔉̃^{ν,n} = 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n} ⊗_{A,ν} O_ℂ, the fixed-weight sheaf. Its integral cohomology RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ϵ}∩𝒰_{≥w−ϵ}}(𝒰_{≥w−ϵ}, 𝔉̃^{ν,n})^{int} is defined in the same way.
items.note: §6.2.11, p. 64. It gives an integral structure to the locally analytic overconvergent cohomology of [BP21] §6, and generalises H^i(†, κ_A, r) of Pilloni (2020), §12.8, to GSp_{2g} and every w. The field of the fixed weight ν is not specified; presumably a complete algebraically closed extension of Q_p such as C_p. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.15(1) (ordinary part of integral locally analytic overconvergent cohomology in families)
items.statement: The operator t acts on RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝔉̃^{ν_A,n})^{int}, and its ordinary part identifies with the higher Hida complex M_w^• ⊗_Λ A.
items.note: Theorem 6.2.15(1), p. 64; the proof is 'similar to the proof of theorem 6.2.9', with Proposition 6.2.13 for the passage to topological induction. It is the family version of Theorem 6.2.9(2) and extends the comparison of M† with M in Pilloni (2020) to the whole weight space. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Theorem 6.2.15(2) (rational comparison and lattices in a fixed p-adic weight)
items.statement: For ν as in §6.2.11: RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝔉̃^{ν,n})^{int} ⊗_{O_C} C = RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝔉̃^{ν,n}[1/p]). For h ∈ Q, the image of RΓ^{int}(𝔉̃^{ν,n}) in the slope ≤ h part RΓ_{𝒵_{<w+ε}∩𝒰_{≥w−ε}}(𝒰_{≥w−ε}, 𝔉̃^{ν,n}[1/p])^{≤h} is a lattice.
items.note: Theorem 6.2.15(2), p. 64. It supplies the lattice asked for by [BP21] Conjecture 6.8.1. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Corollary 6.2.16 ([BP21] Conjecture 6.8.1 holds for Siegel varieties)
items.statement:
[BP21] Conjecture 6.8.1 holds for G = GSp_{2g}. Fix w ∈ ^MW and a continuous character ν : T(Z_p) → C_p^×.
(1) Every character λ of T^+ occurring in RΓ_{w,an}(K^p, ν)^{+,fs} or RΓ_{w,an}(K^p, ν, cusp)^{+,fs} satisfies v(λ) ≥ 0.
(2) Every character λ of T^− occurring in the ‘−’ versions satisfies v(λ) ≤ 0.
Here RΓ_{w,an} is the finite slope locally analytic overconvergent cohomology of [BP21] §6.4, with the normalization of Hecke operators used there; equivalently, these operators preserve a lattice.
items.locator: §6.2.11, Corollary 6.2.16 and proof, p. 64; Theorem 1.4.10, p. 6
items.note: Corollary 6.2.16, p. 64; Theorem 1.4.10, p. 6. Proof: 'It suffices to check this for t ∈ T^{++}(Q_p) which then follows from 6.2.15 (2)'. It is the optimal form, for locally analytic weights, of the slope bound of Pilloni (2020), Proposition 13.3.1.1. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Small slope versions of [BP21] Corollary 6.8.4 and Theorem 6.9.3(2) (Siegel case)
items.statement:
For G = GSp_{2g}, the strongly small slope conditions may be replaced by the small slope conditions in two results.
- [BP21] Corollary 6.8.4. Let ν = ν_alg χ be a locally algebraic character with κ_alg = −w_{0,M}wν_alg − (w_{0,M}wρ + ρ) ∈ X^⋆(T)^{M,+}. Then the maps RΓ_w(K^p, κ_alg, χ)^{+,ss_{M,w}(κ_alg)} → RΓ_{w,an}(K^p, ν)(−ν_alg)^{+,ss_{M,w}(κ_alg)}, their ‘−’ analogues and the cuspidal versions are quasi-isomorphisms.
- [BP21] Theorem 6.9.3(2). Take a point (λ_p, λ^S) of the eigenvariety in the support of the w-part of locally analytic overconvergent cohomology, of locally algebraic weight ν = ν_alg χ with ν_alg ∈ X^⋆(T)^+. If its smooth part λ_p^{sm} satisfies the small slope condition ss_w(ν), then it is classical.
items.note: Stated without proof on p. 64. According to [BP21] Remark 6.8.5, the replacement follows from Conjectures 5.9.2 and 6.8.1. It generalises Pilloni (2020), Theorem 14.7.1 and Corollary 14.7.1 (small-slope classicality for GSp_4). Eigenvarieties for coherent cohomology are planned nowhere: PadicFamilies L2a plans only the abstract gluing machine, and the OverconvergentAutomorphicForms document excludes finite-slope classicality. External input: [BP21] Corollary 6.8.4, Theorem 6.9.3(2), Remark 6.8.5 (the replacement is possible if Conjectures 5.9.2 and 6.8.1 hold)

items.name: [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3 (vanishing for locally analytic overconvergent cohomology)
items.statement: [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3 holds in the generality of [BP21], namely abelian type Shimura data, and in particular for Siegel varieties. Let w ∈ ^MW and let ν_A be a weight. Then H^i_{w,an}(K^p, ν_A, cusp)^{±,fs} is concentrated in degrees [0, ℓ_±(w)], and H^i_{w,an}(K^p, ν_A)^{±,fs} is concentrated in degrees [ℓ_±(w), d]. Here ℓ_+(w) = ℓ(w) and ℓ_−(w) = d − ℓ(w). If A is a domain, H^{ℓ_±(w)}_{w,an}(K^p, ν_A)^{±,fs} is a torsion-free sheaf of O_{Spa(A,A^+)}-modules.
items.note: Invoked on p. 64 in the proof of Corollary 6.2.17. It generalises Pilloni (2020), Proposition 12.9.1 (H^i_cusp(†, κ_A, r) = 0 for i > 1, GSp_4), to every w and Hodge-type data. [BP21] is not covered by the atlas. Planned nowhere. External input: [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3 (with Theorem 6.6.1 and Lemma 6.6.2)

items.name: Corollary 6.2.17 (rational cohomological vanishing; Theorem 1.4.3(3))
items.statement: For every g and every w ∈ ^MW: the complexes M_w^• ⊗ Q_p of Λ ⊗ Q_p-modules have amplitude [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2], and the complexes M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗ Q_p have amplitude [0, ℓ(w)].
items.note: Corollary 6.2.17, p. 64; Theorem 1.4.3(3), p. 5. The proof is one line: 'This follows from 6.2.15 combined with [BP21], thm. 6.7.3'. Over the local rings of Λ ⊗ Q_p, vanishing of cohomology above degree b bounds the top of a minimal complex, but vanishing below degree a does not bound its bottom. The bottom bound comes from the top bound for the Serre-dual complex (Theorem 1.4.8, pairing M_w^• with M^•_{w_{0,M}ww_0,cusp}), combined with the other range in [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3. The one-line proof leaves this implicit. It is the rational form, over the whole weight space, of Pilloni (2020), Theorem 1.1. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Remark 6.2.18 (Conjecture 5.6.1 holds after inverting p)
items.statement: For every g and every w ∈ ^MW, RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p satisfy the vanishing of Conjecture 5.6.1, with amplitudes [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2] and [0, ℓ(w)] respectively. That is, Conjecture 5.6.1 holds rationally.
items.note: Remark 6.2.18, p. 64: 'Dually we deduce the analogous vanishing results for RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗ Q_p and RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗ Q_p', through Lemma 5.4.2. Definition 1.4.1 defines amplitude for admissible complexes integrally only, so its meaning after inverting p is not defined. The natural reading is cohomological: H^i(RΓ_w(K^p) ⊗ Q_p) = 0 for i ∉ [ℓ(w), g(g+1)/2], and H^i(RΓ_w(K^p, cusp) ⊗ Q_p) = 0 for i ∉ [0, ℓ(w)]. Planned nowhere. The introduction states this result as Theorem 1.4.3(3) (p. 5), labelled 'Rational cohomological vanishing 6.2.17'. Corollary 6.2.17 (p. 64) is the corresponding statement for M^•_w ⊗ Q_p and M^•_{w,cusp} ⊗ Q_p. It is proved from Theorem 6.2.15 and [BP21] Theorem 6.7.3, and Remark 6.2.18 passes from it to RΓ_w by duality.

items.name: Discreteness of p̄^!F̄ and the projection formula for p̄^!
items.statement: Let p̄ : C̄ → X̄ be a proper morphism of schemes of finite type over Z, and F̄ a coherent sheaf on X̄. Then p̄^*F̄ is pseudo-coherent, and both p̄^*F̄ and p̄^!F̄ are discrete objects of D(O_{C̄,■}). For an invertible sheaf L on X̄ there is a projection formula p̄^!(F̄ ⊗ L) ≅ p̄^!F̄ ⊗ p̄^*L.
items.note: This is used without reference in the proof of Proposition 2.3.13 (p. 17): 'using that p̄⋆2F̄ and p̄!1F̄ are discrete', 'Since p̄⋆2F̄ is pseudo coherent', and 'use the projection formula'. In a dynamic compactification the p̄_i are proper but need not have finite Tor-dimension. Checked, the statement is correct.
